title: Overview
text:
APEXREST

![APEXREST pencil and ruler symbol](docs/assets/apexrest-logo.svg)

[![Local quality gates](https://github.com/apexrest-dev/apexrest/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/apexrest-dev/apexrest/actions/workflows/ci.yml)

An Oracle APEX plugin for Codex and Claude Code. An agent writes APEXlang, previews it, runs it and ships it to a development or test application.

[Features](docs/features.md) · [Get started](https://apexrest-dev.github.io/apexrest/getting-started/) · [Documentation](https://apexrest-dev.github.io/apexrest/docs/) · [Deployment safety](https://apexrest-dev.github.io/apexrest/deployment/) · [Release notes](https://apexrest-dev.github.io/apexrest/release-notes/)

 What it is

[Oracle APEX](https://apex.oracle.com/) is a low-code platform for business web applications on Oracle Database. APEX 26.1 and 26.2 can express an application as APEXlang, a readable text source that a coding agent can edit like any other code.

APEXREST gives that agent what it needs to do the work well. One plugin installs into Codex (desktop app and CLI) and Claude Code. Its six skills and twelve MCP tools share one runtime, which is also available as the apexrest CLI for scripts, CI and Codex Cloud.

 What you can do with it

| Step       | What happens                                                                                                      | Read more                                                                                 |
| ---------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Write  | The agent reads Oracle definitions and compiler-checked recipes offline before it writes APEXlang.                | [Component library](docs/features.mdcomponent-library-read-before-writing)               |
| See    | Pages render locally with the genuine Universal Theme, without a database or against your own.                    | [Local preview](https://apexrest-dev.github.io/apexrest/local-preview/)                   |
| Review | In the preview, you click a component and say what to change; the agent applies it to the exact source.           | [Review comments](https://apexrest-dev.github.io/apexrest/local-preview/review-comments) |
| Check  | The official Oracle compiler validates the sources and reports file, line, column and valid values.               | [Testing](https://apexrest-dev.github.io/apexrest/testing/)                               |
| Ship   | Only the changed pages and components are imported into a DEV, QA or TEST application, after a plan and a backup. | [Deployment safety](https://apexrest-dev.github.io/apexrest/deployment/)                  |

![APEXREST connects an agent request to APEXlang source, a verified deployment plan, Oracle APEX and runtime checks.](docs/assets/overview.svg)

You ask for a change, such as "add an order status report". The agent writes the APEXlang, renders the pages locally, validates them with the Oracle compiler, imports only what changed, and checks the result in a browser when you ask it to.

 Features

Writing

- Component library. 389 pinned Oracle 26.2 definitions, 269 compiler-checked component recipes, UX patterns and 1,350 public Oracle pages, searchable in English or Ukrainian.
- Decisions API selection. Optional OpenAI ranking of catalog components before generation. A one-page pilot cut active time by 48%.
- Real compiler validation. Structured diagnostics with file, line, column and valid values.

Reviewing and editing

- Review mode. In the local preview, press Alt+Shift+C, click a region, item, button or report column, and leave a comment for any agent, or edit its title, label, heading, format or sequence in place. Each comment carries the component's patch target and file digest.
- Semantic page edits. project context, project patch and project insert change named properties, report SQL with its columns, or add regions, items and refreshes without rewriting the page file; a file that changed in the meantime is never overwritten.
- CRUD recipes. project scaffold generates a report with a modal edit form, editable grids, master–detail pages and faceted search from one spec, with an explicit authorization, key and lost-update contract.

Seeing and running

- Local preview. Run APEXlang on Node.js and SQLite with the genuine Universal Theme 26.2: reports, grids, forms, items, charts, calendars, maps, dynamic actions and a PL/SQL interpreter.
- Connected and live preview. Run the preview's backend in your own DEV, QA or TEST database, and watch open pages follow each source edit.

Shipping

- Partial imports on APEX 26.2. Import only the changed pages and shared components, with drift and conflict checks.
- Safe deployment. Exact 30-minute plans, backups, drift detection and recovery from unknown outcomes. DEV, QA and TEST targets only.
- Direct or ORDS access. Reach the database through the Oracle listener or REST-Enabled SQL over HTTPS.

Working together

- Two providers, one team. Work in Claude Code with Codex as the reviewer, or in Codex with Claude Code. The second agent reviews each deployment plan read-only under your own subscription or API key; set peerReview.mode: required to block deployment until it approves. See [peer review](docs/configuration.mdcross-vendor-peer-review).

Details and measured results are on the [features page](docs/features.md).

 Requirements

- Codex with native plugin support, or Claude Code.
- Node.js 24 LTS; Node 24–26 is supported.
- For Oracle work: Java 21 and SQLcl, which the setup skill can install for you. Use SQLcl 26.1.2 for APEX 26.1 and SQLcl 26.3 for APEX 26.2.
- A development or test APEX application. APEXREST never deploys to production.

The local preview needs neither Java nor SQLcl.

 Install

Codex:

sh
codex plugin marketplace add apexrest-dev/apexrest
codex plugin add apexrest-apex@apexrest


Claude Code:

sh
claude plugin marketplace add apexrest-dev/apexrest
claude plugin install apexrest@apexrest


CLI only (optional; the same runtime without a host plugin):

sh
npm install -g apexrest


The repository ships the built plugin under plugins/apexrest-apex, so you need no build step. To install from a local checkout, pass its path to marketplace add. Registry packages can lag the source; this README describes source version 2.9.0.

 Quick start

1. Start a new Codex or Claude Code session and check your setup:

   > Use APEXREST to check my setup. Report the compiler, connection and target checks that still need attention.

   If Java or SQLcl is missing, the agent previews the bundled installer and runs it with your consent. Installation never creates a database or deploys an application.

2. Describe a change, or invoke the work skill: $apexrest-work in Codex, /apexrest:apexrest-work in Claude Code.

   > Add an order status report to page 10 of the DEV application and show it to me in the browser.

3. The agent edits the APEXlang sources, previews the pages, validates and ships. It then reports the changed files, the validation result, the import status and what it checked in the browser.

4. To point at what should change, open the local preview, press Alt+Shift+C, click a component and write your comment. Then ask the agent to "apply the preview review comments".

An explicit request to change an identified DEV/QA/TEST application authorizes that import. The [getting started guide](https://apexrest-dev.github.io/apexrest/getting-started/) covers connections, new and existing applications, and removal.

 Documentation

Start

- [Getting started](https://apexrest-dev.github.io/apexrest/getting-started/): install, connect, create or adopt an application, ship and verify.
- [Features](docs/features.md): every capability, the command behind it and its limits.
- [Field report: developing with the plugin is 2 times faster](docs/apex-design-race.md): the same APEX app built with and without the plugin: 2 imports instead of 8, 2.2 times faster and 38% lower model cost.

Build applications

- [Local preview](https://apexrest-dev.github.io/apexrest/local-preview/): run APEXlang without a database, or against your own, and [leave review comments](https://apexrest-dev.github.io/apexrest/local-preview/review-comments) for the agent.
- [Component catalog](https://apexrest-dev.github.io/apexrest/component-catalog/) and [pattern catalog](https://apexrest-dev.github.io/apexrest/pattern-catalog/): what the agent reads before it writes.
- [Troubleshooting](https://apexrest-dev.github.io/apexrest/troubleshooting/): setup, compiler, authorization and recovery diagnostics.

Run and deploy

- [Deployment safety](https://apexrest-dev.github.io/apexrest/deployment/): plans, backups, drift and authorization rules.
- [Configuration](https://apexrest-dev.github.io/apexrest/configuration/): environments, connection references, trust policy and deployment coordination.
- [Codex Cloud](https://apexrest-dev.github.io/apexrest/codex-cloud/): run the CLI in a Cloud container over ORDS.

Project

- [Verification status](https://apexrest-dev.github.io/apexrest/implementation-status/): what has been checked, and how.
- [All documentation](https://apexrest-dev.github.io/apexrest/docs/)

 Development

Use Node 24 LTS and the committed lockfile:

sh
npm ci --ignore-scripts
npm run build
npm run test:unit


Run npm run plugin:sync after source, skill or resource changes to refresh the checked-in bundle. See [contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md) and [testing](https://apexrest-dev.github.io/apexrest/testing/) for the full set of checks.

 Support and license

Report reproducible bugs through [GitHub issues](https://github.com/apexrest-dev/apexrest/issues) with sanitized diagnostics, and follow [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) for sensitive reports. Licensed under [Apache-2.0](LICENSE).

APEXREST is independent tooling, not an official Oracle, OpenAI or Anthropic product.

title: Features
text:
Features

APEXREST is one Oracle APEX plugin for Codex and Claude Code. It helps an agent write APEXlang, see the result, run it and ship it. This page explains each capability, the command behind it and its limits.

| You want to                                     | Feature                                                                                                                                |
| ----------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Write correct APEXlang the first time           | [Component library](component-library-read-before-writing), [Decisions selection](decisions-api-choose-components-before-generating) |
| See pages without a database                    | [Local preview](local-preview-run-apexlang-without-a-database)                                                                        |
| See pages with your real data and PL/SQL        | [Connected preview](connected-preview-run-the-backend-in-your-database)                                                               |
| Watch the page follow each edit                 | [Live preview](live-preview-the-page-follows-the-agent)                                                                               |
| Tell the agent what to change, on the page      | [Review mode](review-mode-point-at-what-should-change)                                                                                |
| Make small edits and generate CRUD pages safely | [Semantic edits and recipes](semantic-edits-and-recipes)                                                                              |
| Import only what changed                        | [Partial imports](apex-262-import-only-what-changed)                                                                                  |
| Deploy without surprises                        | [Safe deployment](safe-deployment), [Oracle access](oracle-access)                                                                   |
| Know what the agent can call                    | [Work in one session](work-in-one-session), [Tools](tools), [Skills](skills)                                                        |

 Component library: read before writing

A single Metric Card page is 69 lines of nested APEXlang, and every guessed property costs another compile round. APEXREST gives the agent an offline library to read before it writes:

- Oracle definitions. The complete [26.2 Oracle inventory](oracle-apexlang-coverage.md): 389 definitions and 32,187 contextual property occurrences.
- Compiler-checked recipes. The [component catalog](component-catalog.md) has 118 component families with 269 ready recipes. The [pattern catalog](pattern-catalog.md) has 58 UX patterns with 84 recipes, 69 of them compiler-checked.
- Reference pages. 1,350 public Oracle pages.
- Retrieval. apexrest_reference searches plain English or Ukrainian terms, ranks ready recipes first and returns the top hit's code. A change uses at most three lookups.
- Recipes as contracts. Each recipe carries a data shape, adaptation rules, working APEXlang, and compiler evidence bound to file checksums.

 Decisions API: choose components before generating

The optional [OpenAI Decisions selection](component-catalog.mdoptional-openai-decisions-selection) runs through apexrest_reference mode:select and apexrest docs select. One bounded predicate batch ranks up to 64 compatible local catalog candidates. The host model then writes the page from the verified local contracts. When selection is disabled, search and read stay fully local.

In a one-page pilot, the same model built the same APEXlang page three times with selection and three times without it:

- Average active time fell from 5:44 to 2:58 (−48%).
- Main-model tokens fell from about 59,000 to 35,000. Decisions usage is additional.
- Two of three selected runs passed on the first generation.
- All six final pages passed the offline Oracle compiler and the same 46 checks.

This is a single-page pilot, not a general benchmark. The pilot page uses synthetic data.

 Local preview: run APEXlang without a database

apexrest preview serves an APEXlang application from Node.js and SQLite on 127.0.0.1. Pages render with the genuine Universal Theme 26.2 templates, CSS and JavaScript. You or the agent can open real pages, submit forms and see an .apx edit on the next reload, before anything is compiled or imported. On a 22-page showcase application with one page per component family, preview check renders all 22 pages with 0 errors and 0 warnings.

sh
apexrest preview setup                         once: extracts the APEX 26.2 browser runtime and theme templates
apexrest preview check --project /abs/app      render every page, list what is not simulated
apexrest preview start --project /abs/app      serve pages and print their URLs


| Area    | What runs locally                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| ------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Reports | Classic reports (every pagination type, directives); interactive reports with control break, highlight, compute, aggregate, Group By, Pivot, Chart and downloads; editable interactive grids and master-detail |
| Forms   | Modal dialogs, Form Initialization and DML, server validations shown inline, interactive grid row validations, lost-update detection                                                                           |
| Items   | Date pickers, popup LOV, combobox, cascading LOVs, shuttle, switch, star rating, color picker, rich text and markdown editors, QR code, file and image upload                                                  |
| Search  | Faceted Search and Smart Filters with live counts; cards with actions; list views; template components (Content Row, Timeline, Comments, Media List, Metric Card, …)                                           |
| Visuals | SVG charts (bar, line, area, combination, pie, donut, scatter, bubble, funnel, pyramid, radar, polar, range, gauges); FullCalendar calendars; offline maps; tree regions                                       |
| Logic   | Dynamic actions; a PL/SQL subset interpreter for processes, validations, computations and dynamic content; one transaction per submit with rollback on error                                                   |
| Data    | Oracle SQL semantics over SQLite; seed scripts; file uploads and BLOB downloads; apex_collection; local e-mail outbox; REST sources from JSON fixtures                                                       |
| Tools   | Developer toolbar: diagnostics, session state, debug log, "view as" roles, device sizes, data reset, theme styles; APEXlang property validation                                                                |

Running APEXlang locally gives you:

- Speed. Design feedback takes seconds, not a compile-and-import cycle.
- No database. You need no Oracle access and no shared workspace, and it works offline.
- Safe experiments. Data lives in local SQLite and resets at any time.
- Agents that check their own work. AI agents can open and click the pages they write.

The preview is a design aid, not Oracle evidence. Charts are SVG rather than Oracle JET, maps have no tiles, and anything it does not simulate is listed in diagnostics. Read the [local preview guide](local-preview.md).

 Connected preview: run the backend in your database

The local UI can run its backend in your own DEV, QA or TEST database. Add --env and the Node.js preview opens one session through your saved SQLcl connection.

- SQL. Region, report, LOV and form SQL runs in Oracle as written, with page items as binds.
- PL/SQL. Processes, validations and conditions run as real PL/SQL blocks, including your own packages. Bind values flow back into the page.
- APEX session. When the application is installed in the target, a real APEX session makes v() and apex_util work inside packages.
- Nothing persists.
  - Every request ends with a rollback.
  - COMMIT and dynamic SQL in page code are never sent, and a tripwire catches commits from stored code.
  - Production is refused, and the database identity must match.

sh
apexrest preview check --project /abs/app --env test    every page against the real database
apexrest preview start --project /abs/app --env test    local UI, data and PL/SQL in Oracle


Measured on an original stock-control application on a demo Oracle Autonomous Database:

- all 17 pages checked in 24 seconds with 0 errors;
- a receipt posted through the project's package and then rolled back;
- an over-stock issue rejected with the package's own error message.

It is a verification aid, not import evidence. Read [Connected Oracle mode](local-preview.mdconnected-oracle-mode).

 Live preview: the page follows the agent

Every preview page keeps a WebSocket to the local server, so the agent sees its changes without navigating or reloading.

- Source edits. Saving an .apx file reloads the open page, which takes about a quarter of a second on localhost. A typo shows its parse error, with file and line, on that page.
- Data changes. A write to a table redraws every region that reads it, in every tab and session. Views resolve to their base tables.
- Presence. The toolbar shows who views the page, so the agent can work as its own user while you watch as yours.
- Safeguards. Unsaved grid edits are never overwritten, forms only show a notice, refresh loops are blocked, and the socket stays on localhost.

Measured on the generated showcase application: four source edits reload the page in 241–291 ms, from file write to the page load event. A typo shows its error in 176 ms. One grid save refreshes 10 dashboard regions in another session within 57 ms. It is a design aid, not Oracle evidence. Read [Live updates over WebSocket](local-preview.mdlive-updates-over-websocket).

 Review mode: point at what should change

In the local preview, Review on the developer toolbar (or Alt+Shift+C) lets you click a region, item, button, report column or the page and write what should change. Comments are stored in the project's Git-ignored .apexrest/review/comments.json. Numbered pins and a panel keep them on the page. Edit in the same form changes a title, label, heading, format or sequence directly in the source.

Any agent reads the comments with apexrest preview comments or apexrest_preview action:comments:

- each bound comment carries the component's patch target (for example column:employees.SALARY);
- it also carries the page file's current digest and whether the file changed since the comment.

The agent applies the comment with project patch and that digest, then resolves it. A file that changed in the meantime is never overwritten. Read [Review comments](local-preview.mdreview-comments).

 Semantic edits and recipes

- project context returns one page's regions, columns, items and buttons with ready target names, plus the page file digest.
- project patch changes titles, labels, headings, formats, sequences, and a report's SQL together with its columns, in one atomic, digest-bound edit that keeps every other byte.
- project insert adds scaffold-defined regions, items and refresh dynamic actions to an existing page.
- project scaffold generates native pages from one JSON spec, including a report with a modal create/edit form, editable interactive grids, master–detail grids and faceted search. Editable regions require an authorization scheme, one primary key and lost-update detection.

The recipes were compiled, imported and checked in the browser on a local APEX 26.2 application. Source edits are not compiler or import evidence; validate and ship as usual. See the [scaffold reference](../plugins/apexrest-apex/skills/apexrest-work/references/scaffold.md).

 APEX 26.2: import only what changed

Update a page and its shared list of values without re-importing the rest of the application. APEXREST compares the saved baseline, local edits and a fresh server export. It preserves remote-only changes and blocks conflicts before writing.

| Import mode      | Use it for                                                                                                  |
| ---------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| auto (default) | Let the planner select eligible changed pages/shared components and explain when a full import is required. |
| files          | Import an explicit list, including required changed dependencies; never expand it to a full import.         |
| full           | Request the existing complete application import.                                                           |

Partial imports require:

- an existing dev/test application and a trusted sync baseline;
- APEX 26.2 sources and target;
- the reviewed SQLcl 26.3 compiler on a direct connection.

APEX 26.1 keeps full imports. See [APEX 26.2 partial imports](apex-26.2.md).

 Safe deployment

A plan binds sources, configuration, toolchain and target, and expires after 30 minutes. Apply then:

- re-checks identity and drift;
- keeps a checksummed APEXlang snapshot of the selected scope or the full application;
- freezes the sources;
- records migration history and ownership in a local durable store under APEXREST_HOME.

A clean supported APEX installation is enough: APEXREST creates no service tables. Coordination is local to one managed home, so independent machines need external serialization, such as one CI deploy job. An unknown outcome is never retried blindly. Production targets always block deployment and restore. Read [deployment safety](deployment-safety.md).

![Deployment flow: inspect once, edit coherent changes, validate, review the bound plan, back up and import, then verify.](assets/deployment-flow.svg)

 Oracle access

SQLcl runs in one of two modes: cli (a subprocess) or mcp (the official SQLcl stdio server). The database transport is either direct (the Oracle listener) or ords (REST-Enabled SQL over HTTPS, no port 1521). ORDS requires cli mode and plugin-level credentials kept in private local files, never in chat:

sh
apexrest connection add dev-read --ords-url https://ords.example.invalid/ords/app_user/ --ords-username app_user --password-file /path/to/local/file
apexrest sqlcl configure --mode cli --database-transport ords --json
apexrest connection test dev-read --json


ORDS also enables the [Codex Cloud setup](codex-cloud.md), where the bundled CLI runs inside the Cloud container and reaches your database over HTTPS. See [SQL through ORDS](ords.md).

 Work in one session

Describe the change in the conversation, or invoke the work skill: $apexrest-work in Codex, /apexrest:apexrest-work in Claude Code. The skill follows the cycle below. Every project-scoped tool takes the absolute project directory as project.

1. Project.
   - New app: apexrest_project action:init with directory and template (blank-app or customer-crm) generates real Oracle sources.
   - Existing app: action:inspect. apexrest_apex_sync action:status shows a working copy.
2. References. Use at most three lookups per change: apexrest_reference mode:search with short terms, kind and limit:3, then mode:read on the chosen ID. mode:select adds optional Decisions ranking.
3. Edit and preview. Edit .apx files under the application source directory, keeping .apex/apexlang.json, Oracle IDs, authentication and authorization. apexrest_preview action:start serves the pages locally without a database. Previewing is not validation.
4. Ship. For ordinary authorized edits, make one apexrest_ship mode:apply call with env and userRequest (your literal instruction). The runtime then compiles, plans, records an exact-plan grant, backs up, imports, verifies and removes the grant. importMode:auto selects eligible changed pages and shared files, files binds exact paths, and other or global changes use the full application.
5. Review when needed. Use standalone apexrest_apex_validate for diagnostics, or mode:plan for an explicit review. Skip these duplicate calls during ordinary edits.
6. Wait for completion. If the call is still running after waitSeconds, read apexrest_job with the returned jobId. Never rerun ship to fetch a result.
7. Verify when requested. apexrest_browser_open returns the URL. The agent then opens it in the selected browser and checks rendering, navigation and the changed interaction.
8. Report. Files changed, validation result, ship status and runId, pages verified in the browser, and anything not verified with its reason.

An explicit request to create, update or import an identified DEV/QA/TEST application is the authorization for step 4, and the agent does not ask again. Production targets always block deployment and restore. Read the canonical [deployment safety](deployment-safety.md) rules.

 Tools

| Tool                     | Purpose                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| ------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| apexrest_project       | init, adopt, inspect, scaffold, context, patch, insert, connection_add, connection_list, connection_test; passwords only through a private passwordFile or ignored local envFile |
| apexrest_reference     | Offline Oracle APEXlang references, component recipes and UX patterns: mode:search, mode:read and optional Decisions mode:select                                                                   |
| apexrest_metadata_read | Allowlisted, paginated metadata reads; requests[] batches up to 8 scoped queries with one target verification                                                                                          |
| apexrest_apex_validate | Real Oracle compiler on a staging copy, in-process, with structured diagnostics (file, line, column, type, message, validValues, hint); sourceDir validates another APEXlang folder      |
| apexrest_ship          | mode:plan validates and plans; mode:apply records a plan-bound grant, backs up, imports and verifies in a detached worker; mode:recover resumes a stopped run                                    |
| apexrest_apex_sync     | Working source and trusted baseline for an existing dev/test app: init, status, refresh, invalidate                                                                                              |
| apexrest_browser_open  | Resolve the configured application URL for the host in-app browser (alias codex); opening is not verification                                                                                          |
| apexrest_preview       | Local preview: setup once, start serves page URLs on loopback, check renders every page and lists unsupported features, comments and resolve for review comments, stop, status             |
| apexrest_job           | status (waits up to 120 s, reports phase) and cancel for an existing jobId                                                                                                                       |
| apexrest_artifact_read | Bounded, sanitized text of a registered artifact                                                                                                                                                         |
| apexrest_peer_review   | status shows the other vendor CLI and the review mode; review asks it for a read-only, schema-checked verdict bound to a plan digest or a plan-less source review                                    |
| apexrest_status        | doctor probes SQLcl, Java and the host without downloads; project returns the read-only status snapshot (settings, connections, sync, jobs, deployments, grants)                                     |

Validation, planning, references, metadata and sync run inside the MCP server process on a pooled SQLcl engine. ship apply runs in a detached worker, so a database write survives host termination. The CLI keeps granular commands (project, connection, apex, deploy, jobs, compose, sqlcl, dependencies, preview) plus ship, status, job and reference; run apexrest --help.

 Skills

| Skill                      | Use                                                                                                                         |
| -------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| apexrest-work            | Create or change an application end to end: the cycle above                                                                 |
| apexrest-apexlang        | Write or edit APEXlang with pinned Oracle references, component and pattern recipes, contract notes and compiler validation |
| apexrest-safety          | Authorization, trust, plan drift, unknown outcomes when apexrest_ship or apexrest_job is blocked or fails               |
| apexrest-oracle-sync     | Maintainer check/sync of official Oracle inventory, source hashes, new release discovery and full MCP retrieval coverage    |
| apexrest-setup           | Doctor, dependency installation, SQLcl mode and ORDS transport, connection references and the project status snapshot       |
| apexrest-pattern-catalog | Maintainers only: add reviewed UX patterns to the bundled catalog from an identified application                            |

Invoke a skill as $apexrest-work in Codex or /apexrest:apexrest-work in Claude Code, or describe the change and let the host select it. The skills are host-neutral, and reference files load on demand. Compiler readiness does not imply SQL, import or browser verification.

title: Install
text:
Install APEXREST

This page installs APEXREST in Codex or Claude Code and connects it to a target. Follow the four numbered steps in order: register the plugin, let it install Java and SQLcl, optionally add the apexrest command, then connect a target.

 Before you start

- Keep Node.js 24 LTS on PATH (supported range: Node 24–26).
- The repository ships the built bundle under plugins/apexrest-apex; ordinary installation requires no TypeScript build.

 1. Register the plugin

Codex (desktop or CLI with native plugin support):

sh
codex plugin marketplace add apexrest-dev/apexrest
codex plugin add apexrest-apex@apexrest
codex plugin list --json


Claude Code:

sh
claude plugin marketplace add apexrest-dev/apexrest
claude plugin install apexrest@apexrest
claude plugin list


Then:

- Start a new session after registration: hosts cache the skill and tool catalog.
- For a local checkout (git clone https://github.com/apexrest-dev/apexrest.git), pass the checkout path to marketplace add.
- Neither route creates an apexrest shell command; see step 3.

 2. Install Java and SQLcl

1. In the new session, ask the agent to check your setup:

   > Use APEXREST to check my setup. Report the compiler, connection and target checks that still need attention.

2. The setup skill ($apexrest-setup in Codex, /apexrest:apexrest-setup in Claude Code) runs the doctor and, when tools are missing, the bundled installer.

You can also run the installer yourself from a checkout:

sh
node plugins/apexrest-apex/runtime/apexrest.mjs dependencies install --dry-run --json
node plugins/apexrest-apex/runtime/apexrest.mjs dependencies install --yes --accept-oracle-license --json


- Read the preview, including the [Oracle terms](https://www.oracle.com/downloads/licenses/oracle-free-license.html), before the second command; --accept-oracle-license records that separate consent.
- Tools install under ~/.apexrest (or APEXREST_HOME).
- Without a project the managed SQLcl is the 26.1 baseline. Add --project PATH (or run from the project root, the folder that holds apexrest.json) to install what the project's toolchain lock pins, such as SQLcl 26.3 for [26.2 projects](../../docs/apex-26.2.mdrequirements).
- Application verification uses the host in-app browser.

 3. Optional: the apexrest command

The CLI exposes the same operations for scripts and Codex Cloud. There is no interactive terminal menu. Choose one way to get the command:

| Way                                     | What it gives you                                                                                                                  |
| --------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| npm install -g apexrest               | The apexrest command. Check the installed npm version for feature compatibility.                                                 |
| Managed installation (apexrest setup) | Also installs the tools, registers Codex and creates ~/.apexrest/bin/apexrest (or apexrest.ps1 and apexrest.cmd on Windows). |
| Current checkout runtime                | node plugins/apexrest-apex/runtime/apexrest.mjs --help. Use it for the [26.2 partial-import workflow](../../docs/apex-26.2.md).  |

With npm:

sh
npm install -g apexrest
apexrest --help


With managed installation, add the launcher to PATH:

sh
export PATH="$HOME/.apexrest/bin:$PATH"
apexrest --help


The [CLI guide](../../docs/getting-started.mduse-the-cli) covers persistent PATH configuration and the command list.

 4. Connect a target

For a direct connection:

sh
apexrest sqlcl configure --mode cli --database-transport direct --json
apexrest connection list --saved --json
apexrest connection add dev-read --sqlcl-name 'Development connection' --json
apexrest connection test dev-read --json


- Saved direct connections come from SQLcl's own store; --saved lists or tests it without an APEXREST reference.
- For ORDS over HTTPS, use connection add --ords-url ... --ords-username ... --password-file PATH and sqlcl configure --database-transport ords; see [SQL through ORDS](../../docs/ords.md).
- In the conversation, the agent registers references with apexrest_project (connection_add, connection_list, connection_test) and never asks for a password in chat.
- Application work also needs an explicit project environment; follow [Getting started](../../docs/getting-started.mdconnect-and-configure).

Successful plugin installation alone does not prove database access.

 Codex Cloud

Use the [Cloud setup guide](../../docs/codex-cloud.md) for a repository-backed cloud task:

1. Copy its example scripts into the application repository.
2. Configure the environment and Secret.
3. Use the CLI launcher for ORDS HTTPS operations.

The example does not register the plugin or verify native Cloud MCP discovery.

 Uninstall

| Installation   | Commands                                                                                      |
| -------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Codex          | codex plugin remove apexrest-apex@apexrest, then codex plugin marketplace remove apexrest |
| Claude Code    | claude plugin uninstall apexrest@apexrest, then claude plugin marketplace remove apexrest |
| Managed        | apexrest dependencies uninstall --yes and apexrest plugin uninstall (tools first)         |
| Global npm CLI | npm uninstall -g apexrest                                                                   |

- Projects, backups, saved connections, cache and external runtimes are preserved; see the [removal guide](../../docs/getting-started.mdremove-the-plugin-and-managed-tools).
- npm removal does not unregister a plugin or remove managed tools.

 Builds and verification scope

For plugin development or reproducible packaging from the checkout:

sh
npm ci --ignore-scripts
npm run plugin:sync
npm run site:build
npm run release:dry-run


- dist/releases/install-local.txt contains generated local bundle hashes and Bash/PowerShell installation commands.
- Packaging does not publish a release.
- [Implementation status](../../docs/implementation-status.md) describes local checks and the required connected, host and platform qualification.

title: Getting started
text:
Getting started

This guide takes you from plugin installation to a first change shipped to a development or test Oracle APEX application. It is for anyone who installs APEXREST in Codex or Claude Code for the first time.

You install the plugin, let it install Java and SQLcl, configure a direct SQLcl or ORDS HTTP(S) connection, then describe the change you want in the conversation. The repository and the npm package both include the built runtime, so no Git build, TypeScript compilation or npm ci is needed for installation.

 The path at a glance

| Step | What you do                                            | Section                                                                                    |
| ---- | ------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| 1    | Confirm the requirements                               | [Prerequisites](prerequisites)                                                            |
| 2    | Register the plugin in your host                       | [Install in Codex](install-in-codex) or [Install in Claude Code](install-in-claude-code) |
| 3    | Ask the agent to check the setup                       | [Check the setup](check-the-setup)                                                        |
| 4    | Install the missing Oracle tools                       | [Install Java and SQLcl](install-java-and-sqlcl)                                          |
| 5    | Register connection references and describe the target | [Connect and configure](connect-and-configure)                                            |
| 6    | Create a new application or adopt an existing one      | [Create or adopt a project](create-or-adopt-a-project)                                    |
| 7    | Ask for a change; the agent edits, ships and reports   | [Edit, validate, ship and verify](edit-validate-ship-and-verify)                          |

Two other starting points:

- Already using APEX 26.2? Start with [partial imports: update a page and its shared components](apex-26.2.mdquick-start-from-an-updated-checkout). Use the updated checkout runtime and the reviewed 26.2 compiler. dependencies install --project PATH installs SQLcl 26.3 from the project's toolchain lock; without a project it installs the 26.1 baseline.
- Working in a cloud task? See [Codex Cloud](codex-cloud).

 Which version this guide describes

This guide describes the current 2.9.0 source bundle, including APEX 26.2 partial imports.

- Install from the source repository for these features.
- Check the version and capabilities of a separately published npm package.
- See [release notes](release-notes.md) and [implementation status](implementation-status.md) for the current scope and qualification requirements.

 Prerequisites

| Requirement                                                    | When it is needed                                                                                  |
| -------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Codex with native plugin support, or Claude Code               | Plugin registration and the host-provided browser controls                                         |
| Node 24 LTS on PATH (supported range 24–26)                  | Starting the CLI and the MCP runtime                                                               |
| Java 21 and matching SQLcl                                     | 26.1 uses SQLcl 26.1.2; [26.2](apex-26.2.md) uses SQLcl 26.3; ORDS needs a JDK with jdk.compiler |
| Existing supported Oracle APEX target                          | APEX 26.1 full imports or qualified APEX 26.2 full/selected-file workflows                         |
| Saved direct SQLcl connection or plugin-local ORDS credentials | Authorized access to the configured target through the selected transport                          |

What you do not need:

- A clean APEX installation is enough for ordinary deployment.
- APEXREST service tables, utPLSQL and a provisioned sandbox are not prerequisites for an application-only import.

What installation does not include: Oracle binaries, browser credentials or a database account.

 Install in Codex

1. Open a terminal where Node 24 and the Codex CLI are available.
2. Run:

   sh
   node --version
   codex --version
   codex plugin marketplace add apexrest-dev/apexrest
   codex plugin add apexrest-apex@apexrest
   codex plugin list --json
   

3. To find the installed plugin in the desktop app, open Plugins and look for APEXREST for Codex and Claude Code.
4. To invoke a skill, use @ in the message box or $apexrest-work.

The plugin adds no sidebar or menu button. If the tools are not listed, see [troubleshooting](troubleshooting.mdthe-plugin-is-installed-but-tools-are-missing).

 Install in Claude Code

The same bundle carries a Claude Code manifest (.claude-plugin/plugin.json, plugin name apexrest) and the repository root holds .claude-plugin/marketplace.json.

1. Run:

   sh
   claude plugin marketplace add apexrest-dev/apexrest
   claude plugin install apexrest@apexrest
   

2. Start a new Claude Code session after installation.

| Situation                                         | What to do                                                    |
| ------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Install from a local checkout                     | Pass the checkout path to marketplace add.                  |
| Try a checkout for one session without installing | Start claude --plugin-dir <checkout>/plugins/apexrest-apex. |

The manifest declares the six skills and the MCP server node ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/runtime/mcp.mjs; no global MCP registration is needed. The node on the PATH of the shell that starts claude must be Node.js 24 or newer.

 Check the setup

In a new session, ask:

> Use APEXREST to check my setup. Report the compiler, connection and target checks that still need attention.

The agent calls apexrest_status with detail: "doctor". The doctor:

- probes the host, SQLcl and Java without downloads or database calls;
- reports the SQLcl mode (cli or mcp) and the database transport (direct or ords).

What the doctor does not prove:

- A detected tool is not a validated compiler or a live connection.
- A successful registration or plugin listing alone does not prove that the MCP server started.

 Install Java and SQLcl

Missing SQLcl or Java is a reason to install, not to stop. The setup skill ($apexrest-setup in Codex, /apexrest:apexrest-setup in Claude Code) runs the bundled installer. You can also run it yourself from a checkout or the installed plugin directory:

1. Preview the installation:

   sh
   node plugins/apexrest-apex/runtime/apexrest.mjs dependencies install --dry-run --json
   

2. Read the preview first. It lists versions, destinations, download hosts and the [Oracle terms](https://www.oracle.com/downloads/licenses/oracle-free-license.html).
3. Run the installer only after accepting those terms; --accept-oracle-license records that separate consent:

   sh
   node plugins/apexrest-apex/runtime/apexrest.mjs dependencies install --yes --accept-oracle-license --json
   

4. Rerun the doctor afterwards.

| Option                  | Effect                                                   |
| ----------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| --offline             | Uses cached downloads.                                   |
| --home, --cache-dir | Select managed storage.                                  |
| --project             | Installs the versions the project's toolchain lock pins. |

Tools install under ~/.apexrest (or APEXREST_HOME). A custom --home must also be set as APEXREST_HOME for later CLI and MCP processes.

The installer does not provision APEX, install utPLSQL or change database connections.

 Managed runtime installation and the launcher

apexrest setup combines dependency installation with Codex registration and creates the apexrest launcher. Direct codex plugin add or claude plugin install does not create that launcher.

| Platform    | Launcher                          |
| ----------- | --------------------------------- |
| macOS/Linux | ~/.apexrest/bin/apexrest        |
| Windows     | apexrest.ps1 and apexrest.cmd |

1. From a reviewed checkout, preview and then run the setup:

   sh
   node plugins/apexrest-apex/runtime/apexrest.mjs setup --dry-run --json
   node plugins/apexrest-apex/runtime/apexrest.mjs setup --yes --accept-oracle-license --json
   

2. Add the launcher to PATH for future shells (APEXREST never edits shell startup files):

   sh
   export PATH="$HOME/.apexrest/bin:$PATH"
   apexrest --help
   

   In PowerShell, invoke & "$env:USERPROFILE\.apexrest\bin\apexrest.ps1".

| Option          | Effect                                                            |
| --------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| --native-only | Registers the plugin with the existing runtime without downloads. |
| --codex-home  | Selects a Codex profile.                                          |
| --codex       | Selects the Codex executable.                                     |

A foreign or ambiguous marketplace stays blocked with MARKETPLACE_OWNERSHIP_CONFLICT.

npm install -g apexrest provides the same command through npm's global bin directory.

Reuse a managed setup in Claude Code. Managed setup registers Codex only, but its payload contains both host manifests and marketplaces. To reuse it in Claude Code:

1. Add the native.destination returned by setup as the marketplace path.
2. Install apexrest@apexrest.

Both MCP bindings use the managed Node executable and home; Claude resolves its own cached runtime path. Direct repository installations instead inherit APEXREST_HOME from the launching shell.

 Connect and configure

APEXREST stores connection references, not passwords. You choose the SQLcl mode and database transport once per managed home, register connection references, then give the agent the target identity.

The commands below use the apexrest command; see [the launcher](managed-runtime-installation-and-the-launcher).

 Option A: direct Oracle listener

Saved direct connections come from SQLcl's own store; create them interactively in SQLcl first.

sh
 Direct Oracle listener: map saved SQLcl connections.
apexrest sqlcl configure --mode cli --database-transport direct --json
apexrest connection list --saved --json
apexrest connection add dev-read --sqlcl-name saved-read-connection --json
apexrest connection add dev-deploy --sqlcl-name saved-deploy-connection --json
apexrest connection test dev-read --json


- --saved lists or tests SQLcl's store without an APEXREST reference.
- --mode mcp selects the official SQLcl stdio server (sql -mcp) instead of the SQLcl subprocess; existing sessions keep their mode.

 Option B: ORDS over HTTP(S)

Use ORDS HTTP(S) when the listener on port 1521 is unreachable. Use the existing database account and the schema's ORDS URL. The password is read from a private local file (owner-only, not a symlink) and kept at plugin level under $APEXREST_HOME/credentials/.

sh
apexrest connection add dev-read --ords-url https://ords.example.invalid/ords/app_user/ --ords-username app_user --password-file /path/to/local/file --json
apexrest sqlcl configure --mode cli --database-transport ords --json
apexrest connection test dev-read --json


ORDS requires cli mode. See [SQL through ORDS](ords.md).

 In the conversation

The agent registers references with apexrest_project action:connection_add (name plus sqlclName, or ordsUrl, ordsUsername and passwordFile) and checks them with connection_list and connection_test. It never asks for a password in chat.

 Describe the target environment

Give the agent the non-secret target identity for an environment:

> Configure an APEXREST test environment using the connection references dev-read and dev-deploy. The workspace is YOUR_WORKSPACE, parsing schema YOUR_SCHEMA, application ID YOUR_APPLICATION_ID, database unique name YOUR_DB, service YOUR_SERVICE, and application URL https://your-host.example/ords/r/workspace/app/. Verify that the read connection matches this identity.

Replace every placeholder with the actual target. No environment is invented by project initialization. Follow [configuration](configuration.md) for the exact environment schema, task authorization and allowed origins described in the [safety rules](deployment-safety.md).

 Create or adopt a project

Choose one of the two routes.

 New application

Name a new or empty directory and a template:

> Use APEXREST to create a blank application in a new sales-app project. Configure the identified test target, add a dashboard using real source measures, then ship it to that target and verify it in the browser.

The agent calls apexrest_project action:init with directory and template (blank-app or customer-crm). Initialization generates real Oracle sources and rejects nonempty directories.

 Existing application

> Use APEXREST to initialize an existing-app project in a new sales-app directory and adopt the identified test application as a working copy. Preserve all Oracle IDs, .apex metadata, unrelated pages, shared components and authentication. Add the requested dashboard, ship it into that same app and verify the result.

- Adoption (action:adopt with env, appId and workingCopy) exports into a new local directory and fails rather than overwrite local edits.
- Keep the generated Oracle metadata under version control and reuse the working source for later changes; see [existing applications](existing-app.md).
- The CLI equivalents are apexrest project init DIR --template existing-app and apexrest project adopt --env dev --app-id ID --working-copy --json.

 Review the target

- No manual folder trust list is required.
- An identified DEV/QA/TEST app task authorizes its import.
- Production deploy/restore is forbidden.

Read the [current safety rules](deployment-safety.md) before database work.

 Edit, validate, ship and verify

Describe the change, or invoke the work skill ($apexrest-work in Codex, /apexrest:apexrest-work in Claude Code). The work skill drives one cycle per change:

1. Inspect the project.
2. Read at most three references.
3. Edit the .apx sources.
4. Use one apexrest_ship mode:apply call to compile, plan and apply.
5. Report confirmed server completion.
6. Inspect requested pages with the selected browser. Browser checks run only when requested.

Standalone validation is for diagnostics and a separate plan is for explicit review. The steps are listed in the [features page](features.mdwork-in-one-session).

 APEX 26.2 partial imports

For an existing qualified APEX 26.2 application:

1. Initialize a sync baseline before editing.
2. Use importMode:auto to select eligible changed files, or importMode:files with an explicit page/dependency list.
3. Review importSelection.resolvedMode, selected files and any full-import reasons before applying.

The [partial-import guide](apex-26.2.md) gives matching CLI plan/apply examples and explains conflicts, backups and readback. APEX 26.1 continues to use full imports.

 Authorization and safety

Your explicit request to create, update or import an identified development/test application is the authorization for the apply step. The agent does not ask the same permission twice.

The runtime:

1. records the request as a deploy grant bound to the exact project, target and plan digest;
2. imports with a checksummed backup of an existing app, and with identity and drift checks;
3. verifies the import;
4. removes the grant.

Limits:

- Plans expire after 30 minutes.
- Unrelated schema writes, authentication changes, other targets and production are outside that scope.
- A failed or unknown write outcome requires diagnosis or reconciliation before any retry; see [deployment safety](deployment-safety.md).

 Verification

- For a page or dashboard, the agent reconciles the read-only sources and confirmed server import.
- It inspects the imported page in the selected browser only when requested.
- Browser observations are recorded separately from compiler and import results.
- Application verification uses the host in-app browser.

See [testing](testing.md).

 Use the CLI

Every MCP operation has a CLI command with --json output and the same exit codes. There is no interactive terminal menu.

| Exit code | Meaning              |
| --------- | -------------------- |
| 0         | success              |
| 1         | failed               |
| 2         | input                |
| 3         | dependency           |
| 4         | approval             |
| 5         | conflict             |
| 6         | unknown or cancelled |

| Help command                | Shows                                                                                                        |
| --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| apexrest --help           | The commands.                                                                                                |
| apexrest <command> --help | Only that command's usage and options, for example apexrest ship --help or apexrest preview stop --help. |
| apexrest deploy --help    | A command group.                                                                                             |

A typical cycle:

sh
apexrest status --detail doctor --json
apexrest project inspect --project ./crm --detail summary --json
apexrest reference search metric card --corpus components --limit 3 --json
 One ordinary authorized ship call compiles and plans before applying.
apexrest ship --project ./crm --env dev --mode apply --user-request "Add the order status report to the dev app" --json
apexrest job status JOB_ID --wait-seconds 30 --project ./crm --json
 Only when browser verification was requested:
apexrest browser open --project ./crm --env dev --json


What the commands do:

- ship --mode plan validates with the Oracle compiler, reads the target and writes .apexrest/plans/ship-<id>.json for review.
- --mode apply and granular deploy/restore refuse production targets.
- The granular commands (deploy plan|apply|status|restore-plan, apex export|generate|sync|diff, jobs status|cancel, compose plan|materialize, status) remain available.
- apexrest apex validate --source-dir PATH compiles any APEXlang folder that holds application.apx, also outside a project: it uses the folder's own .apex/apexlang.json, else that of the nearest project application, and otherwise fails with MMD_METADATA_REQUIRED.
- The CRM template includes schema changes, so its import needs authorization for that schema scope; verify its interactions in the selected browser when requested.

Project paths:

- When calling project-scoped MCP tools, pass the absolute application project directory as project: the MCP server starts in its plugin directory and rejects missing or relative paths.
- CLI examples resolve --project from the terminal's working directory.

 Codex Cloud

For a cloud task, follow [Run APEXREST in Codex Cloud](codex-cloud.md). It provides a pinned CLI bootstrap, setup/maintenance scripts and ORDS HTTPS configuration for a Linux container. Plugin registration in this guide applies to desktop and CLI hosts; the Cloud example uses the CLI only.

 Remove the plugin and managed tools

Codex:

sh
codex plugin remove apexrest-apex@apexrest
codex plugin marketplace remove apexrest


Claude Code:

sh
claude plugin uninstall apexrest@apexrest
claude plugin marketplace remove apexrest


Managed installation has its own ownership-checked commands:

| Command                                 | Effect                                                                                                                          |
| --------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| apexrest dependencies uninstall --yes | Removes recorded managed tools while preserving external runtimes, projects, backups, SQLcl connections and the download cache. |
| apexrest plugin uninstall             | Removes the managed Codex registration and plugin files (--keep-runtime retains them).                                        |

Uninstall tools first when removing both. Start a new session after removal.

Uninstalling never deletes application projects, backups, credentials, deployment history or database deployments.

 Next steps

- Read [deployment safety](deployment-safety.md) before operating a target.
- Read [security](../SECURITY.md) before sharing artifacts.
- Read the [verification status](implementation-status.md) before selecting this build for production work.
- The [documentation index](index.md) links every guide and evidence record.

title: Documentation
text:
Documentation

![APEXREST pencil and ruler symbol](assets/apexrest-logo.svg)

APEXREST is a plugin for Codex and Claude Code that builds, runs, ships and verifies Oracle APEX applications from APEXlang source: six skills, twelve MCP tools and the apexrest CLI over one runtime. Pick the task you have; each row leads to one guide.

 Start here

| Goal                                                 | Guide                                           |
| ---------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| Understand the product and what it can do            | [README](../README.md), [Features](features.md) |
| Install in Codex or Claude Code and connect a target | [Getting started](getting-started.md)           |
| See what the plugin changes, in a measured story     | [Field report](apex-design-race.md)             |

 Build and change an application

| Goal                                                     | Guide                                                     |
| -------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| Implement an APEX change in the current conversation     | [Work in the current session](chat-workflow.md)           |
| Bring an existing application into source control        | [Existing applications](existing-app.md)                  |
| See and click through pages without an Oracle database   | [Local preview](local-preview.md)                         |
| Find a component, parameter contract and APEXlang recipe | [Component catalog](component-catalog.md)                 |
| Reuse a UX composition across components                 | [Pattern catalog](pattern-catalog.md)                     |
| Start from a public Oracle sample page                   | [Public APEXlang templates](internet-template-sources.md) |
| Select the checks for a change, verify in a browser      | [Testing](testing.md)                                     |
| Resolve setup, compiler, ship or job failures            | [Troubleshooting](troubleshooting.md)                     |

 Run and deploy

| Goal                                                          | Guide                                             |
| ------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
| Import only the changed pages and components on APEX 26.2     | [APEX 26.2 partial imports](apex-26.2.md)         |
| Learn the plan, grant, import and recovery model              | [Deployment safety](deployment-safety.md)         |
| Deploy without service tables                                 | [Clean APEX deployment](clean-apex-deployment.md) |
| Configure environments, connections and policy                | [Configuration](configuration.md)                 |
| Connect over HTTP(S) when the Oracle listener is unavailable  | [SQL through ORDS](ords.md)                       |
| Run the CLI in a Codex Cloud container with ORDS              | [Codex Cloud](codex-cloud.md)                     |
| Read the read-only development status snapshot                | [Development status](status.md)                   |

 Understand and extend

- [Architecture](architecture.md): packages, the persistent SQLcl engine, jobs and durable state.
- [Host integration](codex-integration.md): Codex and Claude Code manifests, ownership and verification scope.
- [Programmatic automation](codex-automation.md): what each tool executes without a model.
- [Oracle APEXlang coverage](oracle-apexlang-coverage.md): the pinned Oracle 26.2 inventory.
- [Composer](composer.md): compose source from experimental blocks (CLI only).
- [Plugin qualification harness](plugin-qualification-harness.md): how host installations are qualified.
- [Contributing](../CONTRIBUTING.md): local workflow, validation and review requirements.
- [Security and privacy](../SECURITY.md): credentials, code trust, reports and recovery.

 Current status

- [Implementation status](implementation-status.md): implemented capabilities and verification limits.
- [Acceptance matrix](acceptance.json): implementation, verification, evidence and blockers for each requirement.
- [Next actions](next-actions.md): open qualification and implementation work.
- [Changelog](../CHANGELOG.md) and [release notes](release-notes.md): changes, breaking changes and distribution.

 Prepare a release

Read [publisher setup](publishing.md) and [release notes](release-notes.md). A source-repository installation and a published, signed stable release are different distribution states. Local packaging never publishes, tags or provisions infrastructure.

title: Field report: with and without the plugin
text:
Developing with the APEXREST plugin is 2 times faster than classic skill-based development, and here is why

_A field report from 6–7 November 2026. Every figure comes from recorded runs on a local Oracle database. Each setup ran once; the limits are listed at the end._

This report compares two recorded runs of the same task: one agent builds an Oracle APEX application with Oracle's APEXlang skill and SQLcl, the other with the APEXREST plugin. It is for readers who want to see, in measured terms, what the plugin changes and where its limits are.

 In short

- The plugin run took 10 min 4 s; the classic run took 22 min 11 s (2.2 times faster).
- The plugin run imported the application 2 times instead of 8, because design iterations ran in the local preview.
- Model cost was $5.01 against $8.04 (−38%), an estimate at API prices.
- Both dashboards look comparably professional. The plugin does not make the agent a better designer; each design iteration costs less.
- Each setup ran once, and run-to-run variation is large. Read [Limits of the experiment](limits-of-the-experiment) before quoting a figure.

 The task

A Claude Code agent (model claude-opus-5-5, effort high) received the same task twice: build an [Oracle APEX](https://apex.oracle.com/) application called Bitcoin Price Monitor on tables that already held a month of hourly prices. The application had five parts:

- a dashboard with the latest price, the 24-hour change and a 7-day price chart;
- a price history report;
- an alerts page with a modal form to create, edit and delete alerts;
- an alert events page with a filter and an "acknowledge all" button;
- a navigation menu.

A separate requirement covered design: open the dashboard in Chrome, review it as a designer and keep fixing it until it looks professional (a clear price hierarchy, a colored change, even spacing, a readable chart), then import the application again and check once more.

Both runs started from the same empty application, with the same database (Oracle AI Database 26ai Free, APEX 26.2, ORDS and SQLcl 26.3), the same model and the same browser. Only the toolset differed.

 Two toolsets

The classic run had Oracle's official APEXlang skill (a description of the text format an APEX application can be written in) and SQLcl (Oracle's tool for compiling and importing). To see any change, the agent has to compile the application, import it into APEX on the database server, reload the page in the browser and look.

The APEXREST run had the plugin with these tools:

1. apexrest_reference: the component library. Its select mode returns, for every named component in one request, a working APEXlang block from Oracle's sample applications, whole-page examples and entry skeletons.
2. apexrest_apex_validate: the Oracle compiler, whose diagnostics carry a Fix: hint taken from the property contract.
3. apexrest_preview: a local APEX renderer on Node.js. It reproduces the Universal Theme and, with env, runs the pages' SQL and PL/SQL on a DEV/QA/TEST database, rolling the transaction back after every request. When an .apx file is saved, the open page reloads automatically.
4. apexrest_ship: delivery in one call: compile, plan, back up, import into the development application and verify that the import reached the right target.

 Results

![Where the time went in the two runs. Without the plugin: about 8 minutes of building, then about 14 minutes in the edit, compile, import and reload loop, with 8 imports. With APEXREST: about 3 minutes of building, design polishing in the local preview, 2 imports, finishing at 10.1 minutes.](assets/apex-design-race-timeline.svg)

|                                 |                  Without the plugin | With APEXREST |       Difference |
| ------------------------------- | ----------------------------------: | ------------: | ---------------: |
| Total time                      |                         22 min 11 s |    10 min 4 s | 2.2 times faster |
| Agent turns                     |                                 192 |           121 |             −37% |
| Imports into APEX               | 8 (+1 attempt without confirmation) |             2 |    4 times fewer |
| Browser actions                 |                                 124 |            63 |             −49% |
| Model cost (API price estimate) |                               $8.04 |         $5.01 |             −38% |

Both applications compile without errors and were imported into the development database. The dashboards look comparably professional: the plugin does not make the agent a better designer, but each design iteration costs less.

![The finished dashboard built without the plugin: a price card, a green 24-hour change, an amber events count and a 7-day line chart scaled from $100,000 to $110,000.](assets/apex-design-race-without-plugin.png)

![The finished dashboard built with APEXREST: a large price card, a green 24-hour change badge, an amber open-events count with a "Review events" link, and a 7-day chart scaled from $100,000 to $110,000.](assets/apex-design-race-with-plugin.png)

 Why the plugin run is faster

 1. References in one request instead of reading files

The classic agent studied the APEXlang skill with dozens of shell commands that read its reference files, and built, compiled and first imported the application after a little over 8 minutes.

The plugin agent asked for everything it needed in one apexrest_reference mode:select call: a chart, cards, an interactive report, a modal form, a switch and buttons. It received working blocks from Oracle samples to adapt instead of reconstructing syntax from a description. Its first page was written after about 1.5 minutes, and at about the 3-minute mark it was already viewing it in the browser.

Fewer files read means fewer tokens in the context of every later turn, which reduces both time and cost.

 2. A design loop without imports

This is the main source of the difference. In the classic run every design change went through the full loop:


edit .apx → compile with SQLcl → import on the APEX server → reload the page → check


After the first import this loop ran 7 more times, and one more import attempt never reported success. Design polishing took about 14 of the 22 minutes, nearly 2 minutes per iteration on average.

With the plugin the loop shrinks to:


edit .apx → automatic apexrest_preview reload → check


apexrest_preview renders pages locally with the Universal Theme and real data from the DEV database, so an iteration takes seconds. The APEX server takes no part in the loop, and rolling back the transaction after every request ensures the preview changes no data.

In that time the agent fixed what a designer usually fixes: a generic banner, four identical cards, a chart whose Y axis started at zero, raw timestamps on the axis and an unneeded legend. Walking through the other pages, it noticed that the alert filter rendered _below_ its report instead of above it and moved it. All of this happened before the first import, at about 6.5 minutes.

![The same dashboard in the local preview with live data. The developer toolbar at the bottom shows diagnostics, session state and the live-reload status.](assets/apex-design-race-local-preview.png)

 3. Delivery in one call

apexrest_ship mode:apply combines compilation, plan, backup, import and verification in one call. The agent does not have to write and run SQLcl import scripts and then check the result separately. The plugin run therefore had 2 imports, both with an unambiguous result.

 4. Fewer turns and browser actions

Each iteration of the classic loop costs several agent turns (compile, import, check the result) and several browser actions (reload, sign in, navigate to the page). Moving the iterations into the local preview cut agent turns by 37%, browser actions by 49% and cost by 38%.

 Limits of the local preview

The local preview is for design, not for final acceptance. Its charts are drawn by its own renderer, not by the Oracle JET library that APEX uses. Therefore:

- chart initialization JavaScript functions that APEX runs are not applied locally. apexrest_preview lists them under notAppliedLocally and shows a visible note under the chart reminding the agent to check it in the imported application;
- the tooltip format can differ locally from Oracle JET.

![The local preview with a red-bordered note under the chart: the chart's initialization JavaScript function is not applied locally; check its axes, formats and tooltips on the imported application.](assets/apex-design-race-preview-note.png)

The tooltip is exactly why the plugin run needed a second import: in real APEX the agent saw that the tooltip showed only the date and a rounded price, added the hour and the exact price and imported again. That is why the plugin's workflow ends with a final check of charts in real APEX.

 Limits of the experiment

- One run per setup. Run-to-run variation is large: another plugin run on the same task took 13 min 36 s (1.6 times faster than the classic run) and cost $4.15.
- Different instructions. The plugin agent's instructions named its tools and required checks in the local preview; the classic agent was pointed at Oracle's skill.
- Synthetic data and a local target. The test used Oracle Database Free on the same machine. Neither agent clicked buttons that change data (delete, "acknowledge all") in the browser.
- Model cost is an estimate at API prices for the Claude model only.

 Conclusion

When design is finished in a browser, most of the time goes into the loop of edit, import, reload and check. APEXREST removes the server import and the syntax lookup in reference files from that loop. In this test the agent imported the application 2 times instead of 8, finished 2.2 times faster and spent 38% less. The final check in real APEX stays, because that is where the application runs.

 Related

To try it: [Getting started](getting-started.md), more on the [local preview](local-preview.md), and how imports stay safe in [deployment safety](deployment-safety.md).

title: Work in a conversation
text:
APEX work in the current session

This page describes how the agent implements an Oracle APEX change inside the current Codex or Claude Code conversation: which tools it calls, in which order, and what it reports. Read it when you want to follow or review that cycle.

 Before you start

- Describe the change in the conversation, or invoke the work skill ($apexrest-work in Codex, /apexrest:apexrest-work in Claude Code).
- The [work skill](../plugins/apexrest-apex/skills/apexrest-work/SKILL.md) implements the change in that conversation with its existing context, model and permissions.
- There is no plugin task registration, startup call or panel.
- The [APEX 26.2 workflow](apex-26.2.md) in this source checkout adds partial imports for page and supported shared-component changes. Existing 26.1 projects keep their full-import behavior.

 The cycle

1. Project.
   - New app: apexrest_project action:init with directory and template (blank-app or customer-crm); it generates real Oracle sources.
   - Existing app: action:inspect (summary) for source directories and environments; apexrest_apex_sync action:status shows a working copy.
   - For 26.2 partial imports, establish a trusted checkpoint with action:init before editing.
   - Configured identities and local sync status are not verified live targets.
2. References, at most three lookups per change.
   - apexrest_reference mode:search with short English terms, kind and limit:3, then mode:read the chosen ID.
   - Use the project's release profile, or explicit version: "26.2" for 26.2 sources.
   - Routes and contracts are in the [APEXlang skill](../plugins/apexrest-apex/skills/apexrest-apexlang/SKILL.md).
3. Edit .apx files under the application source directory.
   - Keep .apex/apexlang.json, Oracle IDs, authentication and authorization.
   - Edit related components together and never leave placeholders.
   - For layout and UX work, apexrest_preview action:start serves the pages locally without a database (see the [local preview](local-preview.md)); it is a design aid, not validation.
4. Ship ordinary authorized edits with one apexrest_ship mode:apply call, env and userRequest (the user's literal instruction).
   - Both hosts use the same compiler, plan, grant, backup, import and readback implementation.
   - importMode:auto selects eligible changed pages/shared files; files binds an exact application-relative list; global or unsupported changes require full.
5. Review when needed.
   - Standalone apexrest_apex_validate is for compiler diagnostics.
   - mode:plan is for an explicit review of selection, dependencies, reasons, risks, sources and target.
   - Neither is a required extra call before an ordinary apply.
   - A separate mode:apply prepares a fresh plan; granular deploy apply consumes the particular saved plan when exact-plan review is required.
6. Wait.
   - The identified DEV/QA/TEST app task authorizes its necessary import; the runtime records and removes the exact-plan grant.
   - If the call is still running (waitSeconds default 25), read apexrest_job action:status with the returned jobId.
   - Never rerun ship to fetch results.
7. When requested, verify visibly changed pages.
   - Call apexrest_browser_open for env, then open the returned URL with the selected browser's controls (host in-app browser of Codex or Claude Code, legacy alias codex, or the user-selected browser).
   - Check rendering, navigation and the changed interaction, following the [browser verification rule](testing.mdbrowser-verification).
   - Opening a page is not verification.
8. Report files changed, validation result, ship status and runId, pages verified in the browser, and anything not verified with its reason.

 Example: an explicit plan request

For a Home page that uses a changed status LOV, an explicit plan request looks like this; replace the paths with the actual application-relative paths and preserve the user's actual request:

json
{
  "project": "/absolute/path/to/application-project",
  "mode": "plan",
  "env": "dev",
  "importMode": "files",
  "files": ["pages/p00001-home.apx", "shared-components/lovs/status.apx"],
  "userRequest": "Update the Home page and status LOV in the identified development application"
}


 File imports: requirements and behavior

File imports require all of the following:

- an existing dev/test application;
- a trusted sync checkpoint;
- the reviewed 26.2 source/target and SQLcl 26.3/MMD tuple;
- direct SQLcl CLI transport inside the runtime.

Codex and Claude Code can invoke this path through apexrest_ship over MCP.

What planning and import do:

- Planning compares the checkpoint, local edits and a fresh server export. It preserves remote-only edits and blocks unequal edits to the same component.
- The effective application is compiled with the selected page and LOV together.
- Dependencies are not silently added: an explicit files request never widens or falls back to full.
- Page-only changes use native selected-page exports. Supported shared files disclose full APEXlang observation because Oracle rejects their native selected export.
- The retained backup and readback cover only the selected files, and the checkpoint preserves local dependency context.
