- [Deployment safety](deployment-safety.md): production marks and the local-target check that commit mode uses.

title: Component catalog
text:
Component catalog

Find a component, inspect its parameters and adapt its APEXlang recipe to your application. This page is for developers and agents who look up a component before writing APEXlang, and for maintainers who refresh the catalog.

The catalog is bundled with APEXREST since 1.1.0 and works offline, without a project or a connection to the reference application. It covers the Universal Theme 26.1 Reference application, including distinct component hosts and examples; it is not a claim to cover every capability of Oracle APEX.

Browse the component list and examples in [Universal Theme Reference](https://apex.oracle.com/ut).

 What the catalog contains

| Content                         | Version | Read more                                                                           |
| ------------------------------- | ------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Compiler-checked recipe catalog | 26.1    | [Adapt a recipe](adapt-a-recipe)                                                   |
| Official Oracle inventory       | 26.2    | [Oracle APEXlang coverage](oracle-apexlang-coverage.md)                             |
| Public Oracle page examples     | 26.2    | [Public page templates and ready recipes](public-page-templates-and-ready-recipes) |

Version rules:

- For an explicit version:26.2, corpus:components resolves the complete [official Oracle inventory](oracle-apexlang-coverage.md) by default, including native/plugin variants and all properties.
- With kind:template, it searches 1,350 original APEXlang page examples from 33 public Oracle applications.
- The local compiler-checked recipe catalog remains independently bound to 26.1.
- Passing project only supplies context. Without version, corpus:components and corpus:patterns still return the recipe and pattern catalogs, labelled with their own 26.1 version, even when the project's toolchain.profile is 26.2.

 Search and read

Search from the CLI, then read the catalog or a returned ID:

sh
apexrest docs search --corpus components --query "metric card" --kind template --version 26.1 --limit 3 --json
apexrest docs read --id component:catalog --json


The equivalent MCP call is apexrest_reference with mode: "search":

json
{
  "mode": "search",
  "corpus": "components",
  "query": "metric card",
  "kind": "template",
  "version": "26.1",
  "limit": 3
}


Read the returned ID with apexrest_reference mode: "read" (id). Follow nextOffset for the rest of a document and nextResultOffset for more search matches. The CLI alias apexrest reference search|read maps to the same docs commands.

 How search behaves

- Parameter and recipe documents are separate, so a request does not load an entire component family.
- English and Ukrainian search aliases resolve to the same versioned records. Plural, singular and inflected forms match the same stem.
- The existing reference search defaults to corpus: "apexlang". Existing Oracle IDs keep their meaning.
- Search matches any of the query terms (at least half must match).
- Ready recipes whose title starts with the query rank above their overview contracts.
- Property-name lookups such as pageItemsToSubmit return the parameter contract.
- Records with readiness: "unresolved" are hidden unless includeUnresolved: true is set. An exact ID always resolves.

 What a result page contains

| Field or option                           | Behavior                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| ----------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| code                                    | The first hit of a page carries the recipe's primary apexlang block, read from its checksum-verified document. It is bounded to 2,500 characters, with truncated: true and the full length when a read must continue. |
| include: "code"                         | Attaches code to every hit.                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| include: "metadata"                     | Attaches code to none.                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| requiresReferences, relatedReferences | Resolve up to three linked IDs to { id, title, kind } (titles of oracle: or pattern: targets are null). docs.read resolves up to sixteen.                                                                         |
| Page budget                               | The page budget of 7,000 bytes is unchanged: later snippets shrink first, then inline code, and code is dropped before any hit is omitted.                                                                                  |

 Metric Cards width

Metric Cards with display: report use Universal Theme's report template, which gives each card a fixed 12.5rem width. This matches APEX itself, so three such regions with columnSpan: 4 show narrow cards with empty space beside them. When the cards should fill their columns, use the partial Metric Card recipe (display: partial).

 Public page templates and ready recipes

The catalog offers two kinds of starting point: public Oracle pages for reference, and dependency-closed recipes that compile on their own.

 Public Oracle pages (26.2, reference only)

The [internet source inventory](internet-template-sources.md) records the reviewed repositories, exact revisions, licenses and exclusions.

- The public page library includes Cards, Charts, Calendar, Interactive Grids, Maps, Master Detail, Reporting, Dynamic Actions, Approvals, Search, Customers, Opportunities, Poll, QAsk, Strategic Planner and Team Calendar.
- Every page retains its original source bytes, source URL, SHA-256, UPL notice and required application dependency guide.
- Page-number filtering is not a security or runtime readiness classification.
- The 1,350 page records contain 1,349 distinct source hashes: Customers and Opportunities share the same help-dialog source. Both records retain their own application dependency context.

sh
apexrest docs search --corpus components --version 26.2 --kind template --query "calendar drag drop" --limit 3 --json
apexrest docs read --id oracle:26.2:public-template/catalog --json


Public pages have readiness:reference: they can depend on sample tables, APIs, plug-ins, assets, shared objects and destination pages. To use one:

1. Read the linked dependency inventory.
2. Adapt the complete dependency set.
3. Compile in the target application.

They are not standalone ready recipes, and their source authentication/configuration must not replace an existing application's security.

 Dependency-closed recipes (26.1)

The separate 26.1 catalog adds 30 dependency-closed recipes:

- 12 dynamic actions, eight computations, seven validations, Area/Donut charts and a Classic Report with CASE/IF/LOOP directives.
- They use synthetic data and have exact-source attribution (29 Oracle UPL adaptations and one MIT adaptation with its complete notice).
- Offline compilation uses SQLcl 26.3 while retaining the original 26.1.0+3102 MMD; this does not upgrade the recipe's APEX version.
- SQL execution, import and browser verification remain not-run.

The 2026-11-01 expansion adds 93 more dependency-closed recipes adapted from official Oracle sources: 67 from the oracle/skills 26.1 generation templates and 26 from oracle/apex 26.2 sample applications, including the new Faceted Search Patterns, Forms Patterns and Sample Directory Search applications. They cover:

- 16 chart variants (bar, stacked, dual axis, bubble, scatter, Gantt, status meter gauge, stock, combination, links, tooltips, zoom, series colors, 3D, densification);
- nine map layers and controls;
- nine calendar variants;
- nine faceted search layouts;
- processes, dialog and message dynamic actions, button behaviors and item variants;
- Rich Text Editor, Geocoded Address and Display Image items;
- Help Text and Breadcrumb regions, static-content layouts, report variants and an editable Interactive Grid.

Evidence and limits of the expansion:

- All use synthetic data, retain exact UPL source attribution and passed the same SQLcl 26.3 offline compilation with the 26.1 MMD.
- The editable grid and sectioned form do not save data until a project table and row-processing process are added.
- Geocoded Address calls Oracle's geocoding service at runtime.
- SQL execution, import and browser verification remain not-run.

sh
apexrest docs search --corpus components --version 26.1 --kind template --query "gantt chart" --limit 3 --json
apexrest docs search --corpus components --version 26.1 --kind template --query "conditional field visibility" --limit 3 --json
apexrest docs search --corpus components --version 26.1 --kind template --query "template directives" --limit 3 --json


 Adapt a recipe

1. Inspect the current project's source, theme and MMD.
2. Select the correct host. A Media List list template and a Media List template component have different contracts, as do classic Comments reports and Comments template components.
3. Read the selected recipe, its parameter document and its required Oracle contracts.
4. Adapt page and item names, DOM IDs, SQL column mappings, keys, shared references and AJAX submitted items together.
5. Compile the complete adapted application before the existing authorized deployment workflow.

Synthetic example data documents the required shape; it is not a connection to your business data. Editable controls require the declared table or API contract.

 What ready means

- A recipe marked ready has a complete local dependency set and real offline compiler evidence for its declared scaffold and MMD.
- SQL execution, import and browser verification are separate fields. not-run is not a pass.
- An unsupported example remains discoverable with an explicit reason.
- A template option present in the reference application does not alone establish that an arbitrary APEXlang composition compiles.

 Optional OpenAI Decisions selection

Before composing a page, the host can select several useful references in one operation. The [features page](features.mddecisions-api-choose-components-before-generating) gives the measured effect and its limits.

sh
apexrest docs select --project /absolute/project --request "Interactive grid with editable rows, filters and summary cards" --json


The equivalent MCP call is apexrest_reference with mode:"select", an absolute project, and request.

| Argument  | Rule                                                                                |
| --------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| request | A nonempty concise description of UI needs, at most 4,000 characters.               |
| version | Optional. Overrides the project profile.                                            |
| limit   | Defaults to six and accepts 1–8.                                                    |
| project | Absolute for the MCP call. CLI selection defaults to the current project directory. |

The final APEXlang is composed by the current Codex or Claude Code model.

 Configure selection

Selection is local unless decisionApi.enabled is true in apexrest.json, or the project has no decisionApi and the [machine-wide default](configuration.mdmachine-wide-settings) is on (apexrest settings configure --decision-api on). The selection result reports settingsSource (project, global or default). The same settings can turn the whole catalog off.

json
{
  "decisionApi": {
    "enabled": true,
    "apiKeyEnv": "OPENAI_API_KEY",
    "envFile": ".env",
    "timeoutMs": 3000
  }
}


This is an optional configuration fragment.

| Key         | Default          | Rule                                                                 |
| ----------- | ---------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| enabled   | false            | Disabling the option prevents credential reads and network requests. |
| apiKeyEnv | OPENAI_API_KEY | The named environment variable that supplies the key.                |
| timeoutMs | 3,000            | Allowed: 250–10,000. The timeout includes response-body reading.     |
| envFile   | —                | Optional and project-relative.                                       |

Where the key comes from:

- The environment variable takes precedence. Otherwise the named variable is read from that regular, user-owned, Git-ignored and untracked ENV file, parsed literally.
- Never put the key itself in project configuration or tool arguments.
- Configure the variable in the plugin process environment, or use the private file when the desktop host does not inherit shell variables.

 How selection works

1. Local retrieval builds up to 64 candidates using English/Ukrainian aliases and individual term/phrase matches, without ordinary search's half-term requirement.
   - For 26.1 it uses compatible components and patterns.
   - For 26.2 it uses official inventory contracts and public page examples.
   - Unresolved and incompatible records are excluded.
2. One POST https://api.openai.com/v1/decisions request with gpt-6-luna asks an independent predicate question for each candidate.
3. Valid probabilities of at least 0.5 are ranked descending, with local order retained on ties.

Only the supplied description and bounded public catalog metadata leave the host. Sources, history and database contents are not read for the request. See [OpenAI Decisions documentation](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/decisions).

 What selection returns

data.results contains local reference records with dependency links and the top-hit code block when available; full documents use mode:read.

- The threshold is an initial heuristic, not a calibrated confidence guarantee.
- The candidate shortlist can miss a relevant component; the host can supplement it with local search.
- ready and reference retain their original verification meanings.

data.selection reports method (local or openai-decisions), version, candidate count, duration, and, after an API attempt, model/API duration and validated usage when returned. Missing measurements are omitted.

 Fallback and errors

- fallbackReason distinguishes disabled selection, no candidates, missing/unreadable credentials, timeout, HTTP/network failures, refusal, malformed answers and no confident match.
- These conditions return local candidates without automatic network retries.
- Cancellation stops the operation.
- Catalog or selected-document integrity failures remain errors.
- Ordinary search/read always remain local.

 Measured results

Local fixtures verify contracts and recovery only.

Live selection run, 2026-10-29.

- The run exercised four fixed English/Ukrainian scenarios across 26.1/26.2, with 20 successful warm-process measurements per scenario.
- Full MCP selection median/p95 ranged from 1.01–1.15 / 1.59–1.90 seconds.
- All 80 successful measured responses included the declared component/contract groups and stayed release-isolated.
- Of 92 total attempts including initial calls and warm-ups, 89 used Decisions and three fell back on HTTP errors. Those failures remain in the denominator and are excluded from successful API latency statistics.
- Backend prompt-cache hits were observed; these are not cold-backend measurements or a general accuracy/SLA claim.
- Private samples and actual usage are in docs/evidence/decisions/live-benchmark.json.

26.1 page-generation pilot.

- A separate pilot used the same gpt-6.1-sol / xhigh model, task and scaffold, with three runs per flag.
- Mean active time including all repairs was 344.31 s disabled versus 178.05 s enabled.
- All six final sources passed the offline Oracle compiler and the same 46 checks.
- The enabled cohort includes one timeout/local fallback.
- Mean generator tokens were 59,453 versus 35,277, with another 42,242 Decisions tokens across two successful calls; timeout usage is unknown.
- Mean known combined usage was therefore 59,453 versus at least 49,358 tokens per page.
- The fixed first-two-ready-template policy and common completion reference pack are documented in private docs/evidence/decisions/page-ab/comparison.md.
- An adaptive native host can supplement local search, so this one-page pilot does not establish general authoring speed or token savings.
- SQL checks used a declared synthetic SQLite subset; connected Oracle and browser behavior were not exercised.

 Source and compatibility

Source. The initial source is Universal Theme 26.1 Reference: APEX 26.1.4, Universal Theme 26.1, SQLcl 26.1.2 and MMD 26.1.0+3102. The inventory includes 122 pages, 987 regions, 539 template options and 164 Universal Theme component attributes. Documentation and helper regions are classified; they are not all reusable recipes.

What a record holds.

- The catalog combines an application snapshot, allowlisted APEX metadata, matching compiler metadata and pinned Oracle APEXlang references.
- Parameters retain their full context, value mappings, defaults, conditions and provenance.
- Region appearance and component-template options are separate.
- Current selections, defaults and presets are distinct; DEFAULT is a marker, not a CSS class.

Versions.

- Catalog revisions bind source and content hashes.
- The manifest records APEX, theme and MMD separately.
- Select the matching version and inspect compatibility before adapting a recipe.
- The catalog does not silently substitute a different target build.

 Maintenance and distribution

This section is for maintainers. Ordinary catalog search never refreshes the database snapshot.

 Capture and rebuild the catalog

Source capture is a separate maintainer operation with an explicit saved SQLcl connection, application, workspace and schema. It verifies target identity before exporting or reading application metadata. Capture writes private local research files; it performs no application import or business-table writes.

1. Set REFERENCE_CONNECTION, REFERENCE_APPLICATION_ID (a numeric ID), REFERENCE_WORKSPACE and REFERENCE_SCHEMA to the approved read-only source.
2. Capture to a new private directory outside the repository, then normalize the reviewed snapshot:

   sh
   node scripts/capture-component-snapshot.mjs --connection "$REFERENCE_CONNECTION" --application "$REFERENCE_APPLICATION_ID" --workspace "$REFERENCE_WORKSPACE" --schema "$REFERENCE_SCHEMA" --compiler /path/to/sqlcl/lib/apexlang-compiler.jar --output /tmp/apexrest-component-snapshot-new
   node scripts/capture-component-snapshot.mjs --snapshot /tmp/apexrest-component-snapshot-new --publish resources/components/source
   npm run catalog:verify
   npm run catalog:build
   npm run catalog:check
   npm run build
   

3. Review any source-count diff, unresolved recipe and version mismatch before packaging.

catalog:verify invokes SQLcl without a database connection and validates every supported recipe against its exact scaffold. It records file hashes and compiler output; it never executes prerequisite SQL. For faster local iteration, node scripts/verify-component-recipes.mjs --changed rechecks changed inputs; the builder still requires valid evidence for every ready recipe.

 Check the public page library

npm run templates:check verifies the public page library, exact file membership, source bytes, attribution and dependency links. To reproduce it:

1. Download the immutable archive identified in resources/public-templates/26.2/source-lock.json.
2. Run node scripts/build-public-template-catalog.mjs --archive /path/to/archive.zip.

The importer enforces its reviewed archive hash and never runs upstream code. Ordinary builds are offline. Per-recipe public provenance is validated separately by the component builder; MIT recipes must include a retained license notice, whose completeness is reviewed during intake.

 What the package contains

- The reviewed package contains factual metadata, original explanations, reusable examples and source attribution.
- It excludes raw application exports, deployment credentials, private URLs and the compiler bundle.
- A new source snapshot is reviewed through its inventory and content diff before it replaces the bundled revision.
- Preserve existing IDs where their meaning is unchanged.

 Related

- [Pattern catalog](pattern-catalog.md): UX compositions across components.
- [Public APEXlang templates](internet-template-sources.md): the reviewed public sources.
- [Oracle APEXlang coverage](oracle-apexlang-coverage.md): the pinned Oracle 26.2 inventory.
- [Features](features.mddecisions-api-choose-components-before-generating): the measured effect of Decisions selection.

title: Pattern catalog
text:
Pattern catalog

Find a reusable Oracle APEX UX composition and adapt its APEXlang recipe to your application. This page is for developers and agents who reuse a pattern, and for maintainers who add patterns from another application.

 When to use

- Use the pattern catalog when you need the layout, data flow and interaction between several components.
- Use the [component catalog](component-catalog.md) when you need an individual building block. The two catalogs are separate.
- Both are local resources used by the agent through the existing reference tools.
- Pattern lookup needs no database connection, catalog UI or automatic insertion step.

 Search and use

 Search

sh
apexrest docs search --corpus patterns --query "search" --kind template --version 26.1 --limit 3 --json


The equivalent MCP call is apexrest_reference with mode: "search":

json
{
  "mode": "search",
  "corpus": "patterns",
  "query": "search",
  "kind": "template",
  "version": "26.1",
  "limit": 3
}


Read a returned pattern: ID with apexrest_reference mode: "read" or apexrest docs read --id ID --json. Follow nextOffset for the needed continuation and nextResultOffset for more matches.

 How search behaves

- English and Ukrainian search names refer to the same records. Inflected forms (панель показників, панелі показників) match the same stem.
- The default corpus remains apexlang. component: and existing Oracle reference IDs retain their meaning.
- Search matches any of the query terms (at least half must match).
- A ready recipe whose title starts with the query ranks above its pattern contract. For example, simple dashboard returns the composition with its primary apexlang block inline.
- Unresolved variants and concepts are hidden unless includeUnresolved: true is set. An exact ID always resolves.

| Field or option                           | Behavior                                                                                                                                                                              |
| ----------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| code                                    | The primary apexlang block, bounded to 2,500 characters with truncated and length.                                                                                              |
| include: "code"                         | Attaches code to every hit.                                                                                                                                                         |
| include: "metadata"                     | Attaches code to none.                                                                                                                                                              |
| requiresReferences, relatedReferences | Resolve linked pattern: IDs to { id, title, kind } (three per hit, sixteen on read). component: and oracle: targets keep title: null and are read through their own corpus. |
| Page budget                               | Pages stay within the existing 7,000-byte budget.                                                                                                                                     |

 Adapt a pattern

1. Inspect the current project's source, APEX version, theme and MMD before choosing a recipe.
2. Read its data contract and required component:/oracle: references.
3. Adapt page and item names, DOM IDs, keys, SQL projections, submitted items, actions and shared references together.
4. Merge the composition into the existing application without copying the source application's authentication or configuration.
5. Compile the adapted application and use the existing authorized deployment and browser-verification workflow.

 Read coverage

- Read coverage with pattern:source/<sourceId>/review, then a page decision with pattern:source/<sourceId>/review/page-<id>.
- Search the patterns corpus with family: "coverage" to find these records.
- Coverage means all observed pages and meaningful variants were reviewed. It does not mean every possible combination of template options has a separate recipe.

 Sources and evidence

 Reviewed sources

The catalog reviews two sources on APEX 26.1.4 and Universal Theme 26.1:

| Source                                                  | Pages |
| ------------------------------------------------------- | ----: |
| [Universal Theme Reference](https://apex.oracle.com/ut) |   122 |
| Oracle APEX UX Pattern Catalog                          |    28 |

- Every captured page has an explicit review of its structural and behavioral variants.
- Individual components, visual options, documentation, inert controls and empty concepts remain distinct from reusable compositions.
- Public records contain safe source attribution, compatibility and content hashes.
- Raw exports and private target details stay outside the package.
- Redistribution rights are unverified; the catalog uses factual metadata and original recipes without copying source prose, JavaScript or assets.

 Counts

The [local manifest](../resources/patterns/manifest.json) records:

| Item              | Count |
| ----------------- | ----: |
| Reviewed pages    |   150 |
| Variant decisions |   818 |
| Pattern contracts |    58 |
| Recipes           |    84 |

Sixty-nine recipes contain original implementations and bound offline SQLcl compiler evidence; 15 remain explicit unresolved variants or concepts. Source attribution and compiler records remain part of the functional catalog.

 What ready means

- A ready recipe has a complete declared local dependency set and real offline compiler evidence for its scaffold and MMD.
- Source inspection, compilation, SQL execution, import and browser verification are separate results.
- not-run does not imply a pass.
- Unsupported behavior or unresolved dependencies remain explicit.
- Synthetic examples establish an input shape, not the user's business schema or a runtime guarantee.

 Limits

The observed sources and original recipes have concrete limits:

- The UX source form pages demonstrate structure without configured business-data DML. Original form recipes can declare a separate fixture SQL script; executing that script needs an authorized target and is not part of offline compilation.
- The UX source AI example has no configured provider. The catalog does not claim a working AI integration or create credentials.
- List/tree recipes explicitly distinguish native page navigation from original selection-and-refresh variants. Source application JavaScript is not copied; each recipe declares its own supported interaction.
- Empty master-detail concepts remain unresolved until a complete composition and its evidence exist.
- Placeholder  links, action names without handlers, legacy mobile samples and application-specific extensions do not become working recipes through compilation. Their limits and unresolved variants remain visible in the page reviews.

 Add patterns from another application

This section is for maintainers.

 Before you start

- Invoke $apexrest-pattern-catalog (Codex) or /apexrest:apexrest-pattern-catalog (Claude Code) to add or refresh catalog entries from an identified APEX application. The skill handles catalog maintenance; ordinary use of an existing pattern follows $apexrest-apexlang.
- Maintainer capture/build helpers run from the [APEXREST source repository](https://github.com/apexrest-dev/apexrest). An installed plugin can search existing patterns without that checkout.
- Do not edit the installed plugin cache or assume repository scripts are bundled beside its skills.
- Access to a source application alone does not grant permission to distribute its code.
- Catalog maintenance does not publish a release or authorize an application import.

 1. Capture the source

Set PATTERN_CONNECTION, PATTERN_APPLICATION_ID, PATTERN_WORKSPACE and PATTERN_SCHEMA to the approved read-only source. Set PATTERN_SOURCE_ID to a stable non-sensitive slug; it is required in both capture modes. Capture to a fresh private directory:

sh
node scripts/capture-pattern-snapshot.mjs --connection "$PATTERN_CONNECTION" --application "$PATTERN_APPLICATION_ID" --workspace "$PATTERN_WORKSPACE" --schema "$PATTERN_SCHEMA" --source-id "$PATTERN_SOURCE_ID" --compiler /path/to/sqlcl/lib/apexlang-compiler.jar --output /tmp/apexrest-pattern-snapshot-new


Capture verifies the live identity before reading metadata and exporting source. It performs no import or business-table writes.

 2. Review the snapshot

- Review the private snapshot, select compositions, replace application-specific details and confirm redistribution rights.
- Use a stable source ID across refreshes. New applications add separate sources; equal page names must not overwrite another source's patterns.
- Review source drift, removed entries, ID collisions and compatibility changes before merging.
- Preserve existing IDs when their meaning is unchanged.
- Keep raw snapshots private and publish only reviewed metadata, original or authorized recipes and safe attribution.

 3. Normalize the snapshot

Normalize the reviewed snapshot with the same source ID:

sh
node scripts/capture-pattern-snapshot.mjs --snapshot /tmp/apexrest-pattern-snapshot-new --publish resources/patterns/source --source-id "$PATTERN_SOURCE_ID"


- Normalization writes source/<sourceId>/snapshot.json and inventory.json.
- Existing source IDs are refused unless --replace is supplied for a reviewed refresh of the same source.

 4. Curate patterns and reviews

Curate patterns and recipes in resources/patterns/recipes/registry.json before verification, preserving their source links and the other sources' entries. Inspect the current builder schema when adding records.

Keep captured facts immutable. The registry takes two maps:

| Map                     | Required  | Purpose                                                                                                                  |
| ----------------------- | --------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| sourceClassifications | Optional  | Classify new or reclassified pages as pattern, group, primitives, documentation, scaffolding or placeholder. |
| sourceReviews         | Mandatory | One entry for every page of every source, keyed by source ID and string page ID.                                         |

For example, this excerpt describes one reviewed page:

json
{
  "sourceClassifications": {
    "example-source": { "10": "pattern" }
  },
  "sourceReviews": {
    "example-source": {
      "10": {
        "sourceSha256": "<copy inventory page provenance.sha256>",
        "classification": "pattern",
        "patternIds": ["pattern:example/review"],
        "componentIds": ["component:regions/standard"],
        "reason": "A reviewed composition connects the listed regions and actions.",
        "variants": [
          {
            "name": "Primary interaction",
            "disposition": "pattern",
            "patternIds": ["pattern:example/review"],
            "reason": "The included recipe implements the observed interaction."
          }
        ]
      }
    }
  }
}


Rules for the review entries:

- Replace the illustrative digest and IDs with actual inventory and catalog values, and review every remaining page.
- sourceSha256 must equal that page's exact provenance.sha256.
- Variant dispositions are pattern, component, visual, documentation and unresolved.
- Inventory nested declarations, anonymous branches, quoted keys, repeated keys with their parent context, shared dependencies and every meaningful action or state.
- A button label,  link or template name alone does not prove working behavior.
- Record actual source examples with page IDs and exact inventory component keys; keep unsupported behavior explicit.

The builder rejects:

- missing or stale reviews;
- unknown pages or source anchors;
- unclassified pages;
- patterns absent from their source-page reviews.

Every page classified as pattern needs a pattern reference. A placeholder is not a working recipe.

 5. Verify and build

After curation, run:

sh
node scripts/verify-pattern-recipes.mjs
node scripts/build-pattern-catalog.mjs
node scripts/build-pattern-catalog.mjs --check


- Verify every recipe declared ready, rebuild the catalog and check deterministic output, dependencies, evidence hashes, bounded retrieval and package portability.
- The verifier also accepts --changed, --filter=REGEX and --catalog=DIR; the builder accepts an optional catalog directory.
- A focused verification run does not waive evidence requirements for other ready recipes.
- Update this guide with the catalog counts.

 Related

- [Component catalog](component-catalog.md): individual building blocks and their recipes.
- [Implementation status](implementation-status.md), the [acceptance matrix](acceptance.json) and [next actions](next-actions.md): current evidence and remaining work.

title: Public APEXlang templates
text:
Internet APEXlang template sources

This page lists the public Oracle APEXlang .apx sources that were reviewed for the reference library: the exact revisions, licenses, counts and exclusions. It is for anyone who starts from a public Oracle sample page or needs to check where a recipe comes from.

- The source inventory was checked on 2026-10-11 and refreshed on 2026-10-14 and 2026-10-15 using web discovery, GitHub repository and code search, live GitHub recursive trees, immutable source archives and license text.
- It covers Oracle APEXlang .apx sources.
- Source counts describe files and applications, not independently verified ready components.

| Source family                                                           | What it contributes                                                     |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [Official Oracle APEX applications](official-oracle-apex-applications) | The 1,350-page public reference library and 26 compiler-checked recipes |
| [Official Oracle skills examples](official-oracle-skills-examples)     | Example applications, a scaffold and 67 compiler-checked recipes        |
| [Community sources reviewed](community-sources-reviewed)               | Seventeen licensed discovery candidates                                 |
| [Exclusions and search limits](exclusions-and-search-limits)           | Sources that are not additional ready template content, and why         |

 Scope and verification

- Oracle APEX 26.2 contributes 33 complete source applications, 2,961 .apx files and 1,506 page files at one pinned commit. The page reference intake selects 1,350 page files with page numbers greater than 0 and less than 9999. This numerical filter excludes global pages and high-numbered pages; it does not by itself identify every login, administration or scaffolding page.
- The Oracle skills repository contains 456 .apx files across its 26.1 and 26.2 example applications and scaffold. Its three 26.2 example applications contain 242 .apx files, including 94 page files. Versioned copies and scaffold duplicates are not additional unique templates.
- Seventeen licensed community candidates were inspected separately: seven on 2026-10-11 and ten more on 2026-10-14. They are discovery candidates, not automatically accepted ready recipes.  Dependencies and adaptation

The full application payloads total 49,883,949 uncompressed bytes.

What the pages depend on:

- Many examples use EBA_DEMO_ tables, supporting SQL packages, shared LOVs, breadcrumbs, authorization schemes, plug-ins, static files or external REST endpoints.
- Charts, reports and maps may require database features or seeded sample data.
- Some sample pages perform writes, reset sample data, or change authentication behavior. Source inclusion is not authorization to run those actions or install supporting objects.

For a reusable recipe:

1. Preserve provenance and license.
2. Choose the actual component rather than a navigation-only sample page.
3. Resolve shared references.
4. Replace sample-schema SQL with a documented synthetic projection or explicit project data contract.
5. Preserve the destination authentication.
6. Run the required Oracle compiler checks.

Import and browser evidence remain separate. Do not remove source-declared MMD requirements or silently claim 26.1 compatibility for 26.2 examples.

A useful dependency-light extraction candidate is [Dynamic Actions: Debounce and Throttle](https://github.com/oracle/apex/blob/fbe095e4c6e783b3fa930ffae927e4826e549190/sample-apps/sample-dynamic-actions/apexlang/sample-dynamic-actions/pages/p00021-debounce-and-throttle.apx). Its interaction is client-side, but breadcrumb and authorization references still require adaptation. Most richer reporting, card and chart examples require their source data contract.

title: Testing
text:
Testing and verification

This page lists the checks that exist for APEXREST and for an application you ship with it, and what each one establishes. Read it to select the checks for a change or to verify a deployed page in a browser.

APEXREST develops and deploys Oracle APEX applications. Keep these boundaries in mind:

- Application verification uses the host in-app browser.
- The plugin provides no automatic application unit, SQL, API or UI test runner, browser installation or saved authentication state.
- Oracle compiler validation and read-only metadata checks remain development/deployment checks.
- Browser observations are separate from compiler and import outcomes.

 When to use

| You are                                            | Read                                                  |
| -------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| Shipping a page or dashboard change                | [Application-only changes](application-only-changes) |
| Asked to verify a deployed change in a browser     | [Browser verification](browser-verification)         |
| Changing the APEXREST repository itself            | [Local development checks](local-development-checks) |
| Qualifying a host installation or an Oracle target | [Host and Oracle checks](host-and-oracle-checks)     |
| Looking at a failed check                          | [Diagnose and rerun](diagnose-and-rerun)             |

 Application-only changes

For an ordinary authorized page or dashboard change:

- Ship with one call. Use one apexrest_ship mode:apply call; it validates with the real Oracle compiler before import.
- Validate while editing. Use standalone apexrest_apex_validate for editing diagnostics. apexrest_ship validates again when planning, so a separate identical compilation immediately before it is unnecessary unless you are diagnosing a change.
- Reconcile source queries when needed. Use authorized read-only checks (apexrest_metadata_read).
- Report confirmed server completion.
- Inspect the page in the selected browser only when the user requests it.

Design iteration before shipping. The [local preview](local-preview.md) (apexrest_preview) renders and runs the pages on Node.js and SQLite; check lists every unsupported feature. It is a design aid: it does not replace compiler validation, an import or browser verification on the target.

When browser verification is requested. Exercise the requested positive and negative interactions through the built-in or user-selected browser. Application writes need their own authorized scope and disposable test data. Compiler and metadata checks do not establish authenticated UI behavior.

 Browser verification

This rule applies when the user requests browser verification. Ordinary confirmed server deployment is success without this step.

1. Select the browser. The project preference .apexrest/panel/preferences.json (browserMode: host|codex or a user-selected browser name, default codex, the legacy alias of host) selects the host's in-app browser; apexrest_browser_open accepts a bounded browser name in browserMode for one call. The development status snapshot stays inside the host; only application pages open in the selected browser.
2. Resolve the page. After a successful ship, call apexrest_browser_open with env. It returns the configured URL for the host browser controls. The resolved URL is a handoff, not evidence.
3. Inspect the affected page.
   - Open it with the browser controls.
   - Complete authorized login in that browser if needed, using an ignored/untracked local ENV credential source when available without echoing values.
   - Wait for the relevant asynchronous regions to finish loading, then exercise the changed controls and navigation.
   - For dashboards, check date ranges, filter submission, chart refresh, reconciled values and a real empty state.
   - For forms, check the relevant validation, save and cancel behavior.
   - Inspect layout at the viewports relevant to the change.
   - Opening a page is not verification; a login screen or a transient chart-loading state is not evidence that the feature works or is broken.
4. Record observations separately. Report what was observed per page, apart from compiler and import results. Record missing browser controls, incomplete authentication, an unavailable deployed change or an unreachable target as missing verification with its reason; never describe it as passed.
5. Keep evidence sanitized. Screenshots and page text can contain business data, URLs and session identifiers; review them before attaching them to a report or issue.

 Local development checks

These commands verify the repository implementation, not applications through the plugin:

| Command                                    | What it establishes                                                   |
| ------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| npm run lint                             | Formatting and source conventions                                     |
| npm run typecheck                        | TypeScript consistency                                                |
| npm run schemas:build                    | Regenerate public JSON contracts from the authoritative input schemas |
| npm run schemas:check                    | Detect missing or stale public contracts without rewriting them       |
| npm run test:unit                        | Core and failure/concurrency fixtures                                 |
| npm run test:contracts                   | CLI/MCP contracts, both host manifest launches and tool parity        |
| npm run test:installers                  | Download, archive, integrity and platform fixtures                    |
| npm run test:packaging                   | Package schemas, containment, manifests and site checks               |
| npm run docs:check                       | Links, anchors and documented commands                                |
| npm run plugin:check                     | Checked-in bundle matches a fresh build                               |
| npm run site:build                       | Local documentation site generation                                   |
| npm run preview:corpus -- --archive PATH | Local preview over Oracle's public 26.2 applications                  |

Build with npm run build before checks that consume dist/.

The build checks schema freshness before replacing any release payload. After changing schema definitions, run npm run schemas:build and the applicable catalog refresh before building. Published schemas describe accepted input, including omitted runtime defaults; normalized records remain subject to their normal integrity checks.

What these checks do and do not cover:

- Packaging validates Claude Code manifests when its CLI is available.
- The host-parity contract resolves each manifest launcher from a relocated payload, compares the scoped ship/tool contracts and references, and checks shared managed connection state.
- Installer fixtures check both Node/home bindings and payload integrity.
- These do not start model sessions or import an application.
- GitHub local quality gates run only on pushes to main; release and Oracle integration workflows remain disabled.

 Preview corpus

preview:corpus renders every page of the 33 public Oracle APEX 26.2 applications in the [local preview](local-preview.md) and counts what it could not run by kind (placeholders, application calls, seed and SQL failures). Pass the pinned oracle/apex source archive that the public template catalog uses; the script checks its SHA-256 and writes the scorecard to docs/evidence/preview-corpus/. It measures the preview, not Oracle behavior.

 Fast-development clocks

node scripts/benchmark-fast-dev.mjs --project PATH [--reps 20] [--env ENV --connected-reps 3] [--out FILE] measures the clocks of [source revisions](architecture.mdedit-to-deploy-paths-and-clocks) on a temporary copy of the project:

- the source revision digest;
- server-side preview readiness after an edit, a burst save and a rename that keeps an older mtime;
- the cold and warm offline compiler.

With --env, it also runs at most five guarded ship applies of a page title on that DEV/QA/TEST target and records their phases.

node scripts/bench/export-direct.mjs --connection NAME --app ID --page N [--shared TYPE:ID] [--reps 5] [--out FILE] compares SQLcl apex export with APEX_EXPORT.GET_APPLICATION (read-only). node scripts/benchmark-preview-oracle.mjs --project PATH --env ENV [--pages 1,10] [--reps 5] [--out FILE] profiles connected preview requests (round trips, APEX sessions, main-thread blocking); every request is rolled back.

The benchmark only runs when invoked. Write its output under docs/evidence/. Rows it cannot run are marked not_run with their prerequisite.

 Host and Oracle checks

| Check                            | What it does                                                                                           | What it does not do                                                                        |
| -------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| npm run test:repository-plugin | Checks installation in an isolated Codex profile plus installed CLI/stdio MCP behavior.                | It does not invoke a model or establish that a host loaded this version in a conversation. |
| node scripts/oracle-smoke.mjs  | Runs Oracle source generation and validation with SQLcl without a database connection.                 |                                                                                            |
| npm run test:integration       | A repository harness for compiler, authorized deployment, grant removal and no-op export preservation. | It does not execute application test suites or browser automation.                         |

Runtime interaction remains a separate host-browser check.

 Plugin server cases

The reusable [APEX 26.1 plugin server cases](../tests/plugin-server/README.md) cover functional quality, diagnostic latency budgets and actual host-token checkpoints.

- The machine-readable catalog maps the current acceptance criteria and explicitly distinguishes automated harness cases from agent-led scenarios.
- Use the ignored test.env target and store sanitized reports in ignored docs/evidence/plugin-server/.
- APEX 26.2 has the separate apex-26.2.extensions.json catalog and separate evidence.
- The 26.1 catalog contains 67 baseline and quality/performance cases; agent, host and Bitcoin catalogs extend qualification independently.

 Integration harness

npm run test:integration defaults to prepare. It validates the application and saves a normal read-only deployment plan. It never imports during preparation. Configure:

- APEXREST_INTEGRATION_PROJECT
- APEXREST_INTEGRATION_ENV
- named SQLcl connections
- a supported non-production APEX target
- optional APEXREST_INTEGRATION_OUTPUT, a new private attempt directory under docs/evidence/

For one reviewed apply, also provide:

- APEXREST_INTEGRATION_MODE=apply
- APEXREST_INTEGRATION_ALLOW_WRITES=true, an execution switch which does not supply human consent
- APEXREST_INTEGRATION_USER_REQUEST, the actual scoped human instruction
- APEXREST_INTEGRATION_PLAN, the contained project-relative saved plan
- APEXREST_INTEGRATION_PLAN_DIGEST, its exact digest
- APEXREST_INTEGRATION_REVIEW, the separate local review record binding the canonical project, environment, plan bytes/digest and instruction hash
- APEXREST_INTEGRATION_CONFIRMATION when the plan requires exact remote-risk confirmation; the file contains the actual human instruction and exact plan digest

The harness checks review bindings, expiry, exact target and source preimages before connected work. The normal ship --mode apply --plan PATH safeguards remain active. It applies only that saved plan and verifies removal of its temporary grant. Another no-op, restore or recovery requires its own applicable reviewed plan; the harness never silently replans or repeats an unknown write.

APEXREST_INTEGRATION_EXPECT_NOOP=true additionally compares complete before/after export inventories, including Oracle metadata. It rejects plans with database scripts or restore operations. Every attempt retains its raw results and explicit per-scenario status under docs/evidence/; a passing happy path remains partial until the full connected matrix is complete. The harness never overwrites the canonical full-qualification report.

- Missing prerequisites remain blocked; recovery and fault injection require identified authorized targets.
- Independent managed homes/machines must be serialized externally.
- Browser observations stay separate from confirmed deployment completion.

 External release evidence

The default release gate requires nine source-bound reports. Three are local repository/compiler groups; six require actual external execution:

| Report                          | Required scope                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| ------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| composer-native-new-chat.json | A fresh native host discovers Composer and completes the composition workflow with the installed candidate.                                                                                    |
| composer-runtime.json         | Actual Oracle command/authorization, shared-resource ownership and authenticated browser qualification (CMP014, CMP016, CMP027).                                                         |
| native-codex-compat.json      | Native macOS arm64 Codex and Claude host scenarios.                                                                                                                                            |
| native-linux-x64.json         | Native Linux x64 Codex and Claude host scenarios.                                                                                                                                              |
| native-win32-x64.json         | Native Windows x64 Codex and Claude host scenarios.                                                                                                                                            |
| oracle-integration.json       | Actual compiler/identity/plan/backup/import, no-op and existing-component preservation, drift refusals, reviewed restore, interruption recovery, contention and unsupported-component refusal. |

The exact required scenario IDs are maintained in [the external evidence contract](../scripts/lib/release-evidence.mjs), using the current host catalogs and acceptance matrix. Host golden tasks retain their catalog repetition and release-specific requirements. An ARM64 VM does not establish Linux x64 qualification, and hosted repository self-tests do not establish native model-host execution.

A passing external report records its kind, exact sourceDigest, mock: false, execution scope, ordered UTC start/completion times, actual platform/architecture/Node and tool versions, and a passing result for every required scenario. Native reports also identify fresh sessions, observed models/efforts and installed payload hashes. Each claim references nonempty regular proof files beneath docs/evidence/ by relative path and SHA-256. Browser evidence is separately disclosed and is required for Composer runtime qualification.

The readiness checker rejects malformed reports, mock/fixture claims, wrong platforms, missing scenarios and changed, missing or unsafe proof files. These checks validate declared scope and proof integrity; they cannot independently establish that execution occurred. An operator must inspect the actual native, Oracle and browser records before promoting a report. Preserve incomplete reports and failed attempts; never replace missing observations with fixture results or mark an unrun case passed. Ordinary application deployments do not inherit this release-qualification matrix.

 Diagnose and rerun

1. Classify the failure and inspect the bounded diagnostics, affected source and actual target.
2. Make a focused repair.
3. Repeat the affected compiler or browser check.
4. Report remaining limitations.

For an unknown write outcome, follow [reconciliation](deployment-safety.md) before retrying. Do not repeat a full import merely to renew an interactive browser session.

 Related

- [Troubleshooting](troubleshooting.md): fault codes and what to do for each.
- [Deployment safety](deployment-safety.md): plans, grants and recovery.
- [Local preview](local-preview.md): design iteration without a database.

title: Troubleshooting
text:
Troubleshooting

This page is organized by symptom. Find the message or fault code you see, then follow the actions in that section. It covers setup, connections, the compiler, deployment, jobs, browser verification and downloads.

 Before you start

1. Run apexrest status --detail doctor --json (or apexrest_status with detail: "doctor" in the conversation).
2. Use the reported capability or fault code to find the section below.
3. Every failed result carries nextActions; follow them before retrying.

A detected executable, a validated compiler, plugin discovery in the host and a working database connection are separate states. One of them working does not establish the others.

 Find your symptom

| Symptom or fault code                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | Section                                                                                                              |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| The apexrest command is not found                                                                                                                                                                                                    | [The apexrest command is missing](the-apexrest-command-is-missing)                                                  |
| SQLCL_CONNECTION_NOT_FOUND, a saved connection is not listed or fails its test                                                                                                                                                       | [Saved connections are missing or fail their test](saved-connections-are-missing-or-fail-their-test)                |
| No APEXREST tools in the session, APEXREST requires Node.js 24 or newer., a rejected project argument                                                                                                                              | [The plugin is installed but tools are missing](the-plugin-is-installed-but-tools-are-missing)                      |
| Compiler diagnostics, VALIDATION_UNCONFIRMED                                                                                                                                                                                         | [SQLcl is present but compilation fails](sqlcl-is-present-but-compilation-fails)                                    |
| PARTIAL_IMPORT_UNSUPPORTED, APEX_VERSION_MISMATCH, SYNC_COMPILER_CHANGED, IMPORT_CONFLICT, SYNC_SERVER_CHANGED, POST_DEPLOY_CONTENT_FAILED, LOCAL_RECONCILIATION_REQUIRED, auto resolves to full                     | [APEX 26.2 partial imports](apex-262-partial-imports)                                                               |
| SOURCE_DRIFT, TARGET_DRIFT, PLAN_EXPIRED, SYNC_REPLAN_REQUIRED, PLAN_TAMPERED, DATABASE_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED, DEPLOY_APPROVAL_REQUIRED, PRODUCTION_TRUST_, APPROVAL_, PASSWORD_FILE_UNSAFE, a production target | [General deployment checks](general-deployment-checks)                                                              |
| OUTCOME_UNKNOWN, JOB_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN, a jobId instead of a result                                                                                                                                                                | [A job is still running, failed or has an unknown outcome](a-job-is-still-running-failed-or-has-an-unknown-outcome) |
| An empty chart, a login screen, an external browser preference                                                                                                                                                                       | [Browser verification or charts do not work](browser-verification-or-charts-do-not-work)                            |
| PROXY_UNSUPPORTED, UNSAFE_CACHE_DIRECTORY, a cache miss with --offline                                                                                                                                                           | [Offline, proxy or download errors](offline-proxy-or-download-errors)                                               |
| LOCKED, LOCK_CORRUPT                                                                                                                                                                                                               | [Setup is locked or interrupted](setup-is-locked-or-interrupted)                                                    |
| PREVIEW_NOT_RUNNING, PREVIEW_COMMIT_REMOTE_REFUSED                                                                                                                                                                                 | [Local preview](local-preview.md)                                                                                    |

 The apexrest command is missing

Cause. apexrest setup (managed installation) and npm install -g apexrest create the apexrest command; codex plugin add, claude plugin install and installing tools alone do not.

Fix. Follow [the launcher instructions](getting-started.mdmanaged-runtime-installation-and-the-launcher), or run the bundled runtime from a checkout:

sh
node plugins/apexrest-apex/runtime/apexrest.mjs --help


- apexrest without arguments prints help.
- Use the current source bundle and run npm run plugin:sync after changing runtime source.
- If managed plugin files were removed, their launcher has no runtime to start; install again from a checkout or npm.

 Saved connections are missing or fail their test

Cause. connection add --sqlcl-name NAME records an APEXREST reference; it does not create a connection in SQLcl.

Fix.

1. Save the connection interactively in SQLcl.
2. Run apexrest connection list --saved --json to read that store.
3. Run apexrest connection test NAME --saved --json to test the exact saved name, including case and spaces.

ORDS references are tested with apexrest connection test REF --json after sqlcl configure --database-transport ords.

 SQLCL_CONNECTION_NOT_FOUND

When a referenced SQLcl saved name does not exist, plan, apply and reads fail with SQLCL_CONNECTION_NOT_FOUND (blocked), not a validation error: the application sources were not checked. Do one of the following:

- Create the saved connection in SQLcl (conn -save NAME -savepwd USER@HOST:PORT/SERVICE), then test it with apexrest connection test NAME --saved --json.
- Point the reference at an existing saved name with apexrest connection add REF --sqlcl-name NAME.

 Tools installed elsewhere, or credentials expired

- Check APEXREST_SQLCL, APEXREST_JAVA_HOME and APEXREST_HOME if tools were installed elsewhere.
- Repair missing or expired credentials in SQLcl.
- A successful doctor run does not establish database connectivity.

 The plugin is installed but tools are missing

| Check                                    | Action                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| ---------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| The session is older than the install    | Start a new session after installing or updating the plugin; hosts cache the skill and tool catalog.                                                                                   |
| The plugin is not listed or not enabled  | Check that the plugin is listed and enabled in the same profile: codex plugin list --json, or claude plugin list.                                                                  |
| The manifest or server in Claude Code    | claude plugin validate --strict <plugin-root> checks the manifest and /mcp shows whether the apexrest server started.                                                            |
| APEXREST requires Node.js 24 or newer. | The server exits with this message when the node on the PATH of the shell that started claude is older (for example an older nvm default); switch Node before starting claude. |
| A custom managed home                    | Plugin MCP servers inherit that shell's environment, so export APEXREST_HOME there when you use a custom managed home.                                                               |
| A rejected project argument            | Project-scoped tools reject a missing or relative project argument: pass the absolute directory that contains apexrest.json, never the plugin directory.                           |

The MCP server is node <plugin-root>/runtime/mcp.mjs, started by the host from the installed plugin directory with no downloads. Do not add a second global MCP server to conceal a failed installation.

No folder trust list is required; host filesystem permissions govern project access.

 SQLcl is present but compilation fails

 Select the right compiler

| Source profile                       | SQLcl             | Notes                  |
| ------------------------------------ | ----------------- | ---------------------- |
| The reviewed 26.1 workflow           | 26.1.2.132.1334 |                        |
| [26.2 partial imports](apex-26.2.md) | 26.3.0.260.1620 | With MMD 26.2.0+3479 |

The managed Java baseline is 21; APEXREST_JAVA_HOME selects an existing compatible runtime.

 Read the diagnostics

- apexrest_apex_validate returns structured diagnostics (file, line, column, type, message, validValues, hint): repair the named file and line and rerun.
- SQLcl can print an error and still exit zero, so validation requires a success marker and no error indication; otherwise it reports VALIDATION_UNCONFIRMED with the compiler output.

 The compiler session

- Offline validation and help reuse a pooled SQLcl process.
- Generation on 26.3 is isolated to avoid a verified compiler-state issue; 26.1 retains its established pooling behavior.
- A timed-out, cancelled or failed command kills its session and the next call starts a fresh one; a session idle for ten minutes is reaped.
- If the pool itself cannot start (for example after replacing the SQLcl installation), restart the host session so the MCP server restarts.

 What not to do

- Preserve Oracle-generated .apex/apexlang.json and component IDs.
- Never invent an MMD version or edit internal APEX tables to work around a compiler incompatibility.
- Use the references for the selected toolchain version and make a focused source correction.

 Ship, target or policy checks fail

 APEX 26.2 partial imports

| Symptom                                                         | Action                                                                                                                                                                               |
| --------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| auto resolves to full                                       | Read importSelection.reasons. Confirm the trusted sync baseline and eligibility; do not switch to files just to bypass a full-import requirement.                                |
| PARTIAL_IMPORT_UNSUPPORTED                                    | Check the exact source/compiler/target tuple, selected files and direct SQLcl cli transport. The APEXREST MCP tool supports partial imports; SQLcl's own mcp transport does not. |
| APEX_VERSION_MISMATCH or SYNC_COMPILER_CHANGED              | Verify the actual target and compiler. Follow the source-upgrade/export workflow and explicitly refresh the baseline; never rewrite the MMD version by hand.                         |
| IMPORT_CONFLICT or SYNC_SERVER_CHANGED                      | Reconcile local and server changes before planning again. A dirty refresh is not a merge, and a full import must not conceal a detected conflict.                                    |
| POST_DEPLOY_CONTENT_FAILED or LOCAL_RECONCILIATION_REQUIRED | The import may already be confirmed. Inspect the retained server/source snapshots and readback receipt, then reconcile; do not immediately import again.                             |

The [partial-import guide](apex-26.2.md) lists exclusions and the narrowly allowed readback transformations. OUTCOME_UNKNOWN still requires the recovery procedure below.

 General deployment checks

| Symptom                                                                | Action                                                                                                         |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Missing environment or identity mismatch                               | Check the selected env, connection, database/service, workspace, schema and application ID.                  |
| SOURCE_DRIFT, TARGET_DRIFT, PLAN_EXPIRED, SYNC_REPLAN_REQUIRED | Run apexrest_ship mode:plan again and review the new preview; plans expire after 30 minutes.               |
| PLAN_TAMPERED                                                        | The plan no longer matches the live target, history or sources; create and review a new plan.                  |
| DATABASE_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED                                       | The requested security change is outside task scope; describe the exact change and obtain its authorization.   |
| DEPLOY_APPROVAL_REQUIRED                                             | ship apply records the grant itself; for deploy apply, record a grant with this plan's exact planDigest. |
| Production target                                                      | ship apply is refused by design; production uses the protected external approval path.                       |
| PRODUCTION_TRUST_ or APPROVAL_                                   | Ask the runner administrator to check production-trust.json, the approval key and attestation.               |
| Missing service tables                                                 | None are required: coordination and migration history are local under APEXREST_HOME.                         |
| PASSWORD_FILE_UNSAFE                                                 | Use a regular, non-symlink password file; on POSIX, restrict it to its owner (chmod 600).                    |

Connection credentials belong in SQLcl's store or the private ORDS credential file. Do not put them in an issue or prompt. See [configuration](configuration.md) and the [safety skill](../plugins/apexrest-apex/skills/apexrest-safety/SKILL.md).

 A job is still running, failed or has an unknown outcome

 The job is still running

apexrest_ship returns a jobId when they exceed waitSeconds.

- Read apexrest_job action:status with that ID. It waits up to 120 seconds and reports the phase: validating, planning, backing_up, migrating, importing, verifying, syncing.
- Never rerun the operation to fetch its result.

 The job failed

- A completed job can still carry a failed operation result: read its diagnostics.
- A job whose worker never started is failed and needs a new job after the diagnostic is resolved.

 The outcome is unknown

OUTCOME_UNKNOWN, JOB_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN, an expired heartbeat or a lost import response mean the database may have changed. Do not blindly replay writes or clear ownership.

1. Inspect the deployment state, journal, target history and APEXlang snapshot (or legacy SQL backup) with apexrest deploy status --project PROJECT --run RUN_ID.
2. Use apexrest_ship mode:recover with the original run and user request for server-first readback. The runtime recognizes already-applied sources or safely replans remaining APEX metadata.
3. Database-operation uncertainty and conflicts require explicit review before a retry.

Limits of recovery:

- Cancellation never implies rollback.
- Restore has its own plan and exact approval and restores APEX metadata only.

See [deployment and recovery](deployment-safety.md).

 Browser verification or charts do not work

 The browser does not open the page as expected

- apexrest_browser_open returns the configured URL for the host in-app browser (host, legacy alias codex).
- Complete login in that browser and exercise the affected pages; opening a page is not verification.
- No external browser is launched and no saved authentication state or automatic application suite is used.
- If an old preference says external, change it to host or select browserMode:host for the call.

 A chart is empty or a region does not refresh

- Wait for asynchronous APEX chart regions to finish loading before judging an empty chart.
- After a filter action, verify that the relevant page items were submitted and every affected region refreshed.
- A loading overlay or an old tab with a pending navigation may require a fresh page inspection before changing source.

Record an unavailable browser or deployed change as missing verification with a reason, following the [browser verification rule](testing.mdbrowser-verification).

 Offline, proxy or download errors

| Symptom                       | Cause and action                                                                                                                                          |
| ----------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| A cache miss with --offline | --offline never falls back to the network; a cache miss is a dependency blocker. Preload the exact SHA-keyed vendor artifacts and client-tool archives. |
| An integrity failure          | A corrupt artifact fails integrity.                                                                                                                       |
| A download stalls or fails    | Each download attempt fails after 60 seconds without new data and is retried up to three attempts in total.                                               |
| PROXY_UNSUPPORTED           | A proxy is configured but the running Node cannot apply it: run with NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY=1 on Node 24 or later, or preload the offline cache.            |
| UNSAFE_CACHE_DIRECTORY      | The download cache is not owned by the current user or is group/world writable.                                                                           |

 Setup is locked or interrupted

| Symptom        | Cause and action                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| -------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| LOCKED       | Concurrent setup reports LOCKED. A proven dead process on the same host can be recovered through the dedicated recovery gate. Unknown ownership, another host or an interrupted recovery gate requires inspection; do not guess that a live lock is stale.                           |
| LOCK_CORRUPT | A lock file without a readable owner that is older than 30 seconds, usually left by an interrupted process. Confirm that no apexrest operation is running on any host, then delete the lock file named in the message and retry. There is no automated recovery command for this case. |

Native packages are copied through staging and atomic rename. A rerun probes completed components. Preserve unrelated plugins and the private managed state; deleting everything is not a normal repair step.

 Report a reproducible problem

Include:

- the plugin version;
- OS/architecture;
- the host (Codex or Claude Code) and its version;
- the exact sanitized command or tool call;
- the fault code;
- the smallest source example that reproduces the issue.

Distinguish local fixture results from Oracle or host observations. Review diagnostics for paths, credentials and business data before attaching them to [an issue](https://github.com/apexrest-dev/apexrest/issues). Use [private reporting guidance](../SECURITY.md) for sensitive findings.

title: APEX 26.2 partial imports
text:
APEX 26.2 partial APEXlang imports

Import a changed page and its shared list of values without re-importing the rest of the application. APEXREST selects eligible .apx files automatically or accepts an explicit list, validates dependencies using retained application context and fresh selected server sources, and preserves unrelated remote changes.

> Source version: this guide describes the 2.9.0 source bundle. Use its bundled runtime or plugin; a separately published package must be checked for feature compatibility. APEX 26.1 projects use full imports.

 Choose an import mode

| Mode             | Planner behavior                                                                                                                      | When to use it                                                              |
| ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| auto (default) | Selects eligible application changes, or a database-only plan for pending scripts when the application is unchanged. Conflicts block. | Routine changes to an existing 26.2 development/test app.                   |
| files          | Imports only the listed files; rejects an ineligible selection and never widens it to full.                                         | A specific page, or a page together with changed shared dependencies.       |
| full           | Requests a complete application import through the existing safeguards.                                                               | Initial application creation or changes requiring the complete application. |
| none           | Plans pending migrations and changed package scripts without importing the application.                                               | Explicit database-only work.                                                |

- The CLI and the apexrest_ship MCP tool expose the same modes.
- The requirement to use direct SQLcl CLI describes how APEXREST connects to Oracle; it does not prevent using the feature through Codex or Claude Code's APEXREST MCP tools.
- SQLcl's own mcp execution mode and the ORDS transport are separate options and do not support partial import in this implementation.

 Generate routine pages

For supported reports, cards, charts, calendars, query forms and native page behavior on an Oracle-generated 26.1 or 26.2 Universal Theme starter, use one JSON specification containing verified queries, PL/SQL, column aliases/types and labels. project scaffold emits native APEXlang and navigation together. See the [specification guide](../plugins/apexrest-apex/skills/apexrest-work/references/scaffold.md). Partial import described on this page remains specific to 26.2.

sh
apexrest project scaffold --project /abs/project --spec-file catalog.json --env dev --json
apexrest ship --project /abs/project --env dev --mode apply --user-request "Create the catalog pages in the configured dev app" --json
