Scaffolding changes local sources only. It retains Oracle metadata and authentication, appends to a blank Home and refuses to replace unowned or manually edited pages. Unchanged pages it generated can be updated by re-running a specification. Ship remains responsible for compiler validation, exact planning and the normal deployment safeguards; a separate validate/plan call is unnecessary for routine generated output.

If a task requests server metadata and query observations on 26.2, supplying env also generates readback.sqlFile in private .apexrest/ storage. The 26.1 scaffold reports this helper as unavailable. After a successful import, the caller can run the generated file manually with the authorized SQLcl saved connection. It checks target identity and returns imported metadata, query row counts and bounded samples in a read-only transaction. It does not contain expected business values or a test verdict. Neither scaffold nor ship executes it or adds a deployment gate. Keep observation scripts outside application sources. Browser behavior is checked separately on request.

 Edit existing pages

apexrest project patch changes one property without rewriting the page: a page title, region title, item or button label, report-column heading or format mask, or a layout sequence. Only the value bytes of that property change, and a missing property or group is inserted in the file's own style. The edit is bound to the digest of the page file you read and checked again right before the atomic write; a dry run, or a call without the digest, returns the current digest and writes nothing.

sh
apexrest project patch --project /abs/project --page 10 --operations '[{"target":"column:customers.EMAIL","property":"heading","value":"E-mail address"}]' --dry-run --json
apexrest project patch --project /abs/project --page 10 --operations '[{"target":"column:customers.EMAIL","property":"heading","value":"E-mail address"}]' --expected-digest <currentDigest> --json


A source edit is not a compiler or import result; validate or ship afterwards. See the [patch guide](../plugins/apexrest-apex/skills/apexrest-work/references/patch.md).

 Requirements

| Requirement       | Reviewed support                                                                                        |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Target and source | Existing development/test application on APEX 26.2, with Oracle-exported 26.2 APEXlang sources.         |
| Compiler          | SQLcl 26.3.0.260.1620, Oracle-generated MMD 26.2.0+3479, and observed apex import -files support. |
| Connection        | SQLcl cli mode with a direct database connection.                                                   |
| Project           | Configured target identity, named connection references and a valid sync checkpoint.                    |
| Selection         | Supported new/modified page and shared-component .apx files, including required changed dependencies. |

APEX 26.2 requires SQLcl and ORDS 26.3 or later. APEXREST's partial-import gate deliberately accepts the exact reviewed compiler/MMD tuple and 26.2 target stream. Target releases are checked; a future version is not automatically qualified.

 Select the 26.2 toolchain

- Install the matching compiler with node "$APEXREST_CLI" dependencies install --project "$APEXREST_PROJECT" --json (or setup --project). The first run previews the plan; add --yes --accept-oracle-license to install. Both use the project's toolchain lock, also when run from the project root (the folder that holds apexrest.json; subfolders are not searched). Without a project the managed installer keeps the 26.1 baseline. APEXREST_SQLCL still selects an external compiler.
- Set toolchain.profile to 26.2 for authoring references and use the reviewed toolchains/toolchain-26.2.lock.json as the project's toolchain lock.
- Changing the reference profile alone does not install a compiler or upgrade source metadata.
- Existing project/toolchain changes require explicit refresh or re-establishment of the sync baseline.
- A new app generated by the selected 26.2 compiler records its profile and matching lock.

 Quick start from an updated checkout

The following examples assume a configured application project with an environment named dev. Replace the absolute paths and example page/LOV filenames with your project's values. These commands use the checkout runtime described in this guide.

 1. Configure SQLcl and initialize the baseline

sh
APEXREST_CLI="/absolute/path/to/apexrest/plugins/apexrest-apex/runtime/apexrest.mjs"
APEXREST_PROJECT="/absolute/path/to/application-project"

node "$APEXREST_CLI" sqlcl configure --mode cli --database-transport direct --json
node "$APEXREST_CLI" apex sync --project "$APEXREST_PROJECT" --env dev --action init --json


- Initialize the baseline before editing.
- Initial sync refuses conflicting local sources; retain and reconcile them rather than overwriting them.
- A freshly generated application is the exception for two rewrites Oracle makes on import: deployments/default.json gains the configured app.id, and an empty deinstall script and its reference are dropped. When those are the only differences, init adopts the server form of the affected files and lists them in normalized.
- After a successful full ship of local sources (for example after --action invalidate), init also adopts the server export when the local sources are exactly what that run imported to the same target and the target's update metadata is unchanged since that import. The differences are then Oracle's canonical rewrites of the imported bytes (unquoted names, inline sqlQuery, canonical slot names, dropped defaults, added identifiers). The adopted files are listed in normalized with rule last-import-rewrite, and normalizedFromDeploymentRunId names the run; its snapshot/ keeps the imported bytes. A local edit after the import, a server change, another target, a selected-file or restore run, or no recorded import still conflicts.
- SYNC_SOURCE_CONFLICT names each differing file in its diagnostics and lists them in addedFiles (local only), removedFiles (expected but missing locally) and changedFiles, up to 50 each with differingFileCount. During init, importProof says why the last import did not explain the difference: no-recorded-import, local-changed-since-import or server-changed-since-import.
- An already initialized ready working copy can be reused.

 2. Edit, then apply

After editing, ordinary authorized work needs one apply call: it compiles and plans before import. Use a separate plan preview only when review is useful:

sh
node "$APEXREST_CLI" ship --project "$APEXREST_PROJECT" --env dev --mode plan --import-mode auto --user-request "Update the Home page and status LOV in the configured dev application" --json
node "$APEXREST_CLI" ship --project "$APEXREST_PROJECT" --env dev --mode apply --import-mode auto --user-request "Update the Home page and status LOV in the configured dev application" --json


 3. Or import an explicit selection

For an explicit selection, list exact files. Shared components use a full APEXlang observation because native component export is not qualified on the tested server; the import still touches only these files:

sh
node "$APEXREST_CLI" ship --project "$APEXREST_PROJECT" --env dev --mode plan --import-mode files --files pages/p00001-home.apx shared-components/lovs/status.apx --user-request "Import only the Home page and status LOV into the configured dev application" --json
node "$APEXREST_CLI" ship --project "$APEXREST_PROJECT" --env dev --mode apply --import-mode files --files pages/p00001-home.apx shared-components/lovs/status.apx --user-request "Import only the Home page and status LOV into the configured dev application" --json


- Paths are relative to the configured application source directory.
- files requires a nonempty list; globs, path escapes, symlinks and duplicates are rejected.
- The MCP equivalents are importMode: "files" and files: ["pages/p00001-home.apx", "shared-components/lovs/status.apx"] on apexrest_ship.

 Apply a particular saved plan

- ship --mode apply prepares a fresh plan and then binds its grant to that plan; it does not consume the earlier preview file.
- To execute a particular saved plan, use the granular deploy plan / deploy apply flow with its exact-plan authorization.
- Once a plan is bound for apply, its selection cannot widen.

 What the planner checks

 Baseline, local edits and server export

The planner compares the saved baseline, local edits and fresh export of the selected server components.

- Local changes identify the intended update.
- Unselected remote changes are preserved on the server and are not fetched into local context.
- Unequal local/server edits to the same component block planning.
- Retained dependency context and the selected server sources form an effective application validated as a whole, so a selected page cannot depend on an unselected new local LOV missing from the server.
- Include required changed dependencies in the reviewed list.

Review importSelection.requestedMode, resolvedMode, files, supporting-component selections and reasons. The compact preview shows at most 50 selected paths; use the full saved plan for a longer list.

 Pages and shared components

- Fast native export mappings cover page files.
- Supported shared-component files also use selected imports, but Oracle 26.2 rejects native APEXlang LOV/list export selectors.
- Their plans therefore expose exportScope:full and shared-components-require-full-apexlang-observation: a full APEXlang read is filtered to the selected sources for conflicts, backups and readback. This is a performance limit, not a full import.

 What requires a full import or blocks

- Themes, templates, plug-ins, workspace components, static assets and authentication/authorization changes require a full import; explicit files mode refuses them.
- Deletions, initial application creation, production, database operations and unsupported transports can require a full plan or block the operation under existing safeguards.
- Known remote changes must be reconciled before an automatic full fallback.
- Explicit files mode never becomes full.
- Database scripts require a full application import and the local/remote safety policy; production deployment is forbidden.

 Backup, verification and recovery

 Plans and grants

- Version 4 plans bind the exact file list, source/configuration/toolchain hashes, target, fresh server export and validated effective tree.
- Existing saved plans keep their previous full-import semantics.
- The temporary deploy grant binds the whole plan digest.

 Exports and backups

- Page-only plan/apply uses native apex export -expComponents in the selected scope and never exports the complete application.
- Shared-component selections use the explicitly recorded full APEXlang observation; their retained snapshots and import scope remain selected.
- Existing pages need a selected export; new pages have a live ID collision check and no export when absent.
- The pre-apply selected export is also the backup source, avoiding a separate backup round trip.
- Backups record scope, exact files, checksums and absent components.
- Full changes use full APEXlang snapshots.
- Ordinary operation creates no SQL application dumps; explicitly requested restore of an existing legacy SQL backup remains compatible.

 Apply and concurrency

- Apply acquires managed-home schema ownership before the fresh drift comparison, freezes the effective tree and runs one SQLcl apex import -files command.
- Same-component changes after planning block; different-page edits do not.
- Independent homes/machines still require external serialization.
- There is no claim of a distributed atomic compare-and-import protocol.

 Readback verification

- After page imports, only selected APEXlang sources are exported and compared.
- Shared-component imports use a full APEXlang observation and compare only selected files; the observation scope is recorded separately.
- Qualified Oracle 26.2 default elision covers native select-list/region start-new-row, checksum page protection and bar-chart type; uniquely identified regions with explicit unique layout sequences and native chart axes/series may be reordered.
- Scalar strings, fenced code, nondefault security values and ambiguous identities stay strict.
- Unknown forms fail closed.
- Both hashes and rules are retained in readback-verification.json, alongside selected scope and an explicit indication that unselected server content was not checked.

 Checkpoint and recovery

- The checkpoint retains local dependency context plus verified selected sources; unselected local work remains dirty.
- Concurrent local edits are retained and require reconciliation.
- A confirmed import with failed readback is a verification failure; an unconfirmed write is outcome_unknown.
- Recovery reads only the original scope before deciding whether the result is already applied or needs a fresh plan.
- It does not blindly retry or roll back Oracle.

 Restore

- Selected APEXlang backup restore creates a separate exact plan and uses the same scoped compiler/import/readback flow.
- A creation backup records absence, so it cannot pretend to undo creation by importing an empty file set; component deletion needs a separately reviewed operation.
- Before/effective/readback snapshots, backups and journals remain durable and private.

 One apply call for routine edits

- Use one ship --mode apply call for a routine authorized edit. It includes compiler validation and planning; a separate validate and plan preview add duplicate work.
- Preview remains available when review is useful or a remote dangerous operation requires exact-plan confirmation.
- With a valid working-copy checkpoint and unchanged application files, auto checks local migration/package history. Pending migrations or changed packages produce a database-only plan; no APEX application import is scheduled. An explicit files selection never expands to database work.
- A local no-op (including unchanged applied database scripts) stops before Oracle calls and explicitly reports that server freshness was not checked. Changed applied migration checksums or unresolved migration outcomes block planning.
- Identity and release discovery share a read-only session, identical read/deploy connections reuse the fresh identity observation, and import help is cached by compiler installation.

 Other 26.2 support

- Validation reports advisory CodeScan findings and source-upgrade hints separately from compiler diagnostics. Scanner unavailability is explicit and does not convert compilation success into a scanner pass. Some findings are known false positives; see below.
- The new corpus covers provider APIs, unspecified versus explicit reasoning effort, secure agent navigation, Interactive Reports, workflow/task changes, charts and Universal Theme, DDS, managed credentials and deployment metadata.
- Six original recipe fragments have real offline compiler evidence. They do not establish provider availability, database policies, running-workflow migration, application imports or browser behavior.
- Effective deployment JSON preserves source defaults, subscription mappings and checksum salts while the configured target controls application/workspace/schema identity. Native Oracle Working Copies and application locking remain distinct from APEXREST's local sync state; API examples do not automatically create copies or acquire locks.
- Security readiness requires actual database capabilities, verified identity propagation, OCI IAM and network permissions. Credential/policy provisioning remains operator-managed. Database-backed Web Credentials do not enforce the Valid for URLs restriction; use the parsing schema's network controls.

 CodeScan known false positives

SQLcl 26.3 CodeScan reports three application-level rules on application.apx line 0 that APEX 26.2 sources cannot clear. Oracle owns the rules; APEXREST does not change or hide them. With SQLcl 26.3 and an MMD 26.2 source, staticAnalysis.findings keeps each finding and adds knownFalsePositive (policy, profile, reason, evidence) only when application.apx itself proves the setting. staticAnalysis.knownFalsePositives counts them, and knownFalsePositivePolicy names the table version (apex262-sqlcl263-codescan-v1, in packages/core/src/codescan-known-issues.ts).

| Rule                              | Marked when application.apx                                                                                    | Stays actionable when                                                                                     |
| --------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| APEX-002 non-public page access   | sets authentication { scheme } and authorization { scheme } (a component reference or mustNotBePublicUser) | either scheme is absent or empty                                                                          |
| APEX-009 session state protection | omits sessionStateProtection, omits its enabled (default Y) or sets enabled: true                          | enabled is false or another value                                                                     |
| APEX-031 substitution ambiguity   | leaves advanced.exactSubstitutions at its default Y                                                            | it sets exactSubstitutions (the compiler rejects true and accepts false with a deprecation warning) |

The source reader fails closed: duplicate groups or properties, unsupported source forms, a missing file, another file, another SQLcl release or another MMD release leave the finding unmarked. Findings marked knownFalsePositive need no source change; do not rewrite authentication, authorization or session state protection to clear them.

Reproduced offline on 2026-11-16 with SQLcl 26.3.0.260.1620 codescan -extensions apx -format json on copies of an MMD 26.2.0+3479 application. All three findings remained for every variant tried: application authorization with a component or mustNotBePublicUser; no application authentication/authorization; authorizationScheme (with and without authentication: required) on every non-public page; sessionStateProtection.enabled true, false, absent or invalid; every page-item checksum protection removed; and exactSubstitutions true, false or Y. Removing errorHandling and sessionManagement raised APEX-029 and APEX-024, which shows that application properties are read. This is local scanner evidence, not a security qualification of any application.

 Read-only capability diagnostics

For bounded read-only diagnostics, call apexrest_metadata_read with kind: "apex-capabilities", the configured parsing schema and env. Results include actual releases, visible public APIs, application lock/Working Copy observations, and explicit operator-verification requirements. Metadata visibility does not prove API execution or security enforcement.

 Major-version source upgrades

- Major-version source upgrades require a reviewed import/re-export into a separate directory, followed by explicit checkpoint refresh.
- Never edit .apex/apexlang.json to pretend that old sources use the new compiler.
- Keep old source and backup snapshots; an export with -force can remove its destination alias directory.

Sources: [APEX 26.2 release notes](https://docs.oracle.com/en/database/oracle/apex/26.2/htmrn/index.html), [file import rules](https://blogs.oracle.com/apex/introducing-file-level-import-with-apexlang-in-oracle-apex), [requirements](https://docs.oracle.com/en/database/oracle/apex/26.2/htmrn/about-release-notes.html), [deployment metadata](https://docs.oracle.com/en/database/oracle/apex/26.2/apxdc/understanding-apexlang-deployment-files.html), [source upgrade](https://docs.oracle.com/en/database/oracle/apex/26.2/apxdc/upgrading-apexlang-source-with-new-apex-release.html), [managed credentials](https://blogs.oracle.com/apex/using-dbms_cloud-credentials-with-resource-principal-and-dbtools-identity).

 Complete Oracle authoring inventory

The [official inventory coverage](oracle-apexlang-coverage.md) includes all 389 definition documents and the upstream layout/syntax catalog.

- Select version:26.2, search corpus:components and read the returned oracle:26.2:inventory/... ID through all pages.
- Every contextual property, enum and applicability condition is retained.
- Local 26.1 UX recipes remain separately version-bound.
- Full source coverage does not qualify database, provider, import or browser behavior.

 Related

- [Existing applications](existing-app.md): adopt an application and create the sync checkpoint.
- [Deployment safety](deployment-safety.mdapex-262-partial-imports): the canonical rules for partial imports, backups and recovery.
- [Configuration](configuration.md): toolchain.profile, environments and connections.

title: Deployment safety
text:
Deployment safety rules

These are the current APEXREST product rules for application and database work. Read this page to learn what the plugin may deploy, where, with whose authorization, and how it recovers from an interrupted import.

Three rules apply everywhere:

- Installation, a project configuration and a tool response never supply user consent.
- The host filesystem permissions govern access to the current project and other required directories. There is no folder trust list to maintain.
- Deployment is for DEV, QA and TEST targets only. Production deployment and restore are blocked.

 Environments and precedence

 What each target allows

| Target                                             | Application deployment                                | Database changes                                                                                                          |
| -------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| DEV (development or dev)                       | The identified application task authorizes plan/apply | Remote dangerous operations require exact-plan human confirmation                                                         |
| QA (qa)                                          | Same application workflow as DEV                      | Same remote confirmation rule                                                                                             |
| TEST (test)                                      | Same application workflow as DEV                      | Same remote confirmation rule                                                                                             |
| Actually local DEV/QA/TEST server                  | The identified task authorizes deployment             | All database/schema operations, including destructive changes, are allowed within the task without a separate risk prompt |
| Production-marked target, including a local server | Deployment and restore are blocked                    | No deployment through this plugin                                                                                         |

Read-only dictionary batches verify identity from the same session before any row is returned. Queries may execute together, but a mismatch discards the entire batch.

Target identity records capture workspace identifiers as exact decimal text. An old unsafe JavaScript number cannot establish the original Oracle identifier. Existing plans, fingerprints and recovery evidence retain their original bytes; APEXREST does not reconstruct an identifier from a rounded value.

After upgrading an older profile, regenerate saved plans. A clean working copy with a numeric workspace baseline can establish a fresh exact baseline through apexrest apex sync --env dev --action refresh --json, using its actual environment name. Dirty working copies remain protected. Explicit full read-only replanning on 26.2 observes a fresh exact identity without rewriting the old sync record. Reconcile held or unknown-outcome runs through their original runtime before upgrading; a mixed-format identity never releases their coordination or enables SQL replay.

 How a target becomes production

Production takes precedence over locality. A target is production when any of these is true:

- apexrest.json marks its environment kind: production.
- Its exact target digest appears in productionTargets in $APEXREST_HOME/production-trust.json.
- Its database's DB_UNIQUE_NAME appears in productionDatabases in that file. The match is case-insensitive. Every service name, workspace, schema and application on that database is production, and the configured name is verified against the live database before any write.

Further rules for production marks:

- Exact target digests include the service name and application ID, so mark whole production databases with productionDatabases.
- Changing an environment label does not remove a registered production mark.
- APEXREST reads this classification file and never edits it.
- Legacy approval keys may be present but are ignored: neither a signature, CI=true, a local grant nor human confirmation enables production deployment.
- Authorized read-only diagnostics and browser inspection remain available.

 How a target counts as local

- Locality is determined from the effective deploy connection, not baseUrl, an environment name or a project flag.
- Direct SQLcl uses the connected JDBC endpoint (show connection). ORDS uses the effective connection URL.
- A loopback endpoint must also identify a server on this host or in a currently running local Docker or Podman container.
- Remote container contexts, forwarded or unresolved server identities receive the remote rules.
- Missing locality evidence never grants destructive local privileges.
- The database/service/schema/workspace/application identity is verified independently before writes.

See the [Oracle SQLcl connection documentation](https://docs.oracle.com/en/database/oracle/sql-developer-command-line/26.1/sqcug/oracle-sqlcl-users-guide.pdf).

 Application authorization and exact plans

 Authorization

- An explicit request to create, update or import an identified DEV/QA/TEST application authorizes its necessary import.
- The agent completes the task without asking the same permission again.
- apexrest_ship records that instruction as a temporary deploy grant bound to the exact canonical project, target digest and plan digest.
- It preserves unrelated policy entries and removes its grant after the attempt.
- Legacy trustedProjects is optional ignored compatibility data.

 Exact plans

- Plans bind source, configuration, toolchain, target and import selection, and expire after 30 minutes.
- Source/configuration/compiler drift, target changes, a different project or a forged plan block apply.
- Regenerate a plan when sources or its validity change. This does not authorize a different application or unrelated work.

 Plan and apply

| Call                       | What it does                                                                                        |
| -------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| apexrest_ship mode:plan  | Compiles with Oracle, reads the target and saves a concrete local plan.                             |
| apexrest_ship mode:apply | Uses the application's task instruction. An optional plan selects an already reviewed saved plan. |

 Production refusal

- Production always fails with PRODUCTION_DEPLOY_DENIED before a grant or database write.
- A target marked in configuration or in the trust file (kind: production, its configured target digest or DB_UNIQUE_NAME) is refused before any connection is resolved or SQLcl starts. This applies to plan, apply, database-only and restore plans.
- The identity-based check of the observed target still runs later, so an environment labelled DEV that resolves to a production target is refused too.

 Actual dangerous database operations

 What counts as dangerous

SQL inspection distinguishes executable operations from comments and string data. Examples include:

- ALTER TABLE customers RENAME COLUMN old_name TO new_name
- DROP TABLE customers
- truncation
- DML
- privilege changes
- dynamic SQL
- executable program replacement

A remote plan shows databaseReview.operations: action, object, column/new name where relevant, consequences and dependency observations.

- A table deletion removes data and constraints and can invalidate dependent code.
- A column rename requires updating dependent SQL and application queries.
- Missing dependency visibility is reported as unavailable, never as no dependencies.

 Confirmation on remote targets

For remote DEV/QA/TEST targets:

1. Describe these concrete effects in chat and obtain explicit human confirmation.
2. Apply the same saved plan with confirmation: { planDigest, userRequest }, where userRequest is the human's actual confirmation.

The runtime checks the exact digest; confirmation cannot authorize another plan, target or changed SQL. The CLI accepts --confirmation as a JSON object. Local targets use the local policy above and need no separate dangerous-operation confirmation.

 Application metadata and authentication changes

- Deleting an APEX page or component is application metadata work and does not add a database-danger confirmation. The application backup protects that workflow.
- Authentication/authorization changes must remain within explicitly authorized task scope; the remote confirmation also binds any such reviewed risk.

 Migration and package inputs

- Migration and package inputs remain contained, frozen SQL/PLSQL files.
- Names, immutable checksums and ordered migration history are checked.
- SQL queries in migrations, including query-backed DDL, require confirmation on a remote target when the scanner cannot prove a name is a column or a side-effect-free built-in.
- SQLcl host commands, credential switching and unbound external scripts are unsupported even on a local server: local database permission is not permission to execute arbitrary host commands.
- SQLcl imports/scripts retain restriction level -R 2.
- DDL is not assumed transactional, and an APEX application backup does not restore business data.

 Backups and coordination

 Backups

- Ordinary imports use checksummed, target-bound, private APEXlang snapshots.
- Page changes retain only the selected pages; full imports retain the full application.
- A plan that exports the target keeps that export in private project storage. Apply reuses it as the backup only after proving it is the planned one: the target identity and migration history are read again and, with the kept files' digest, must reproduce the plan fingerprint. An altered or missing copy is ignored and apply exports as before.
- The export taken immediately before the first write must still equal the plan. That is the drift check, and it also proves the backup equals the content the write replaces.
- Restore uses a separate exact plan and a fresh snapshot; production restore is blocked.
- Legacy SQL backups can be restored when they contain one complete Oracle export (fNNN.sql) with the standard SQLcl wrapper and self-contained PL/SQL blocks. Split exports, external scripts, host commands and connection changes are unsupported. For a remote target, the restore plan identifies the SQL file for review and requires human confirmation of the exact plan before execution.
- Application backups restore APEX metadata, not business data.
- A creation snapshot records absence and cannot undo creation through an empty import; deletion requires a separately reviewed operation.

 Coordination

- Clean supported APEX requires no APEXREST control tables.
- Local durable migration history and schema ownership live under $APEXREST_HOME/deployment-control/.
- Runners sharing that home are serialized.
- Upgrade every runner sharing a managed home before enabling writes. Reconcile any interrupted earlier runs. If the home has older migration or package history, run a full read-only deployment plan (mode:plan, importMode:full) for each original environment against its original Oracle service. The plan registers the verified store without changing its history or ownership. New stores are blocked while old history remains unregistered, and changing a registered Oracle service is blocked because the runtime cannot prove the new service shares that history.
- Independent homes/machines require external serialization; changing or deleting durable history is not recovery.
- Preserve foreign/live ownership and unrelated local or server changes.

 APEX 26.2 partial imports

 Plan and import

- Eligible partial plans bind an exact page/shared-component file list, baseline, fresh server snapshot and validated effective tree.
- Pages use native selected export.
- Oracle 26.2 rejects native APEXlang LOV/list export selectors, so shared-component imports explicitly bind a full APEXlang source observation while retaining backups and readback comparisons only for the selected files.
- The runtime reuses the plan's kept observation as the backup source, freezes sources and executes one SQLcl apex import -files call.
- It never silently expands an explicit file import to a full import.
- A page file is the import unit; this does not claim child-region granularity.

 Readback and conflicts

- Readback checks selected files using the qualified formatting/default equivalence rules.
- Scalar values, fenced code, nondefault security and ambiguous identities remain strict.
- Both hashes, normalization rules and observation scope are retained.
- Unselected server freshness is not established by a selected comparison.
- A real mismatch remains a verification failure and enters reconciliation; successful command output does not mask a different result.
- Same-component conflicts block; other-component changes are preserved by selected import.
- Managed-home ownership is acquired before the fresh drift check; independent machines/homes require external serialization.

See [APEX 26.2 support](apex-26.2.md).

 Interrupted imports and recovery

 Automatic recovery

An interrupted/lost response is initially outcome_unknown. The runtime first reads the actual server and compares it with the reviewed desired and baseline sources.

| Server content                                    | What the runtime does                                                                                                                                                          |
| ------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| The desired result is already present             | Records recovered success without reimport.                                                                                                                                    |
| Still the baseline or a compatible partial result | Preserves evidence, reconciles the working checkpoint, releases only the stopped run's ownership and creates a fresh exact plan for the required remaining application import. |

The ship worker makes at most one automatic retry per attempt.

 An import Oracle rejects

When SQLcl runs the import to its end and reports an Oracle or compiler error, the batch has stopped and rolled back. The runtime does not rely on that: it exports the target again and compares it with the plan (allowing only this run's own completed migrations).

| Fresh read after the error                    | Result                                                                                              |
| --------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Target equals the plan                        | IMPORT_REJECTED (failed) with Oracle's message and located diagnostics; no recovery, no reimport. |
| Target differs, or the read fails             | OUTCOME_UNKNOWN, as before.                                                                       |
| The error is a lost or killed connection      | OUTCOME_UNKNOWN, as before: the server session's fate is not known.                               |
| APEXREST stopped SQLcl (timeout, cancel, ...) | OUTCOME_UNKNOWN without automatic recovery, as below.                                             |

 Confirm a reviewed database reconciliation

A run that was interrupted while it ran migrations or package scripts ends as database-review-required. mode:recover never replays SQL, so the run keeps the target's deployment ownership (TARGET_LOCKED) until a person has inspected the database.

After the inspection, the person states the outcome of every script of the run:

sh
apexrest deploy reconcile --project /abs/project --env dev --run <run id> --statements '[{"file":"src/database/packages/0010__api.sql","outcome":"not_applied"}]' --user-request "<what the person checked and did>" --confirm <run id>:<plan digest prefix>


- applied records the script as applied, and the next plan skips it. not_applied (also after a manual cleanup) leaves it out of the history, and the next plan runs it again.
- Without --confirm, or with a wrong value, the command changes nothing and prints the expected <run id>:<plan digest prefix> and the run's scripts.
- The command refuses:
  - a missing or extra script;
  - another environment or a changed target;
  - a production-marked target;
  - a run that finished;
  - a run started on another host;
  - a run whose process is still alive.
- It never connects to the database. It records the statement and the released owner in reconciliation.json next to the run and adds reconciled to the run journal; the run's own state.json is kept. It then releases the run's ownership; create a fresh plan next.
- It is a CLI command, not an MCP tool: the statement is the person's.

 When APEXREST stopped SQLcl

When APEXREST itself stopped SQLcl before Oracle confirmed the outcome — a timeout, cancellation, the output limit or an unconfirmed batch — the call it had sent can still be running on the server, so no automatic recovery or retry runs. The result names the run and the cause, and apexrest_ship mode:recover is used once no APEXREST session remains on the target.

SQLcl write sessions (imports, migrations, packages, restores) may run for up to 60 minutes; read sessions keep a 3-minute limit.

 Recover a stopped run

- apexrest_ship mode:recover with the original run UUID and task instruction resumes that workflow after a stopped worker.
- CLI deploy status --run UUID remains read-only and reports the observed classification.
- Third-party content changes, live/foreign workers and local source/configuration drift block recovery.
- SQL migrations/packages and metadata restore scripts are never blindly replayed: their actual database effects and durable history require separate review.
- Production remains blocked.
- Cancellation never implies rollback.

 Completion and optional browser checks

- A confirmed server deployment without errors is success.
- Oracle compiler validation, target checks and applicable import integrity checks remain mandatory.
- Browser verification is performed only when the user requests it; it uses the built-in browser by default or the browser the user selects.
- An ordinary deployment has no browser approval or not_run caveat cycle.
- When a browser check is requested, report actual observed behavior separately; opening a URL alone is not evidence.
- No automated application suites are run and no browser is installed.

 Local ENV credentials and truthful evidence

 Local ENV credentials

- Credentials may be read from a local ENV file for an authorized target connection or browser login when the file is a regular, user-owned, Git-ignored and untracked file.
- Parse ENV as literal data; never source it as shell code or execute substitutions.
- Connection setup accepts envFile with optional urlKey, usernameKey and passwordKey (defaults: ORDS_URL, ORDS_USERNAME, ORDS_PASSWORD).
- Password values never appear in operation results, chat, logs or public artifacts.
- A browser login may consume the same authorized local source without a password-paste or folder-trust step; do not capture cookies/profiles or persist secrets in application source.

 Truthful evidence

- Report implementation, repository fixtures, Oracle compiler/import results and requested browser observations accurately.
- Generated verification output belongs in ignored docs/evidence/.
- A local build or import does not prove fresh native-host discovery or UI behavior.

 Related

- [APEX 26.2 partial imports](apex-26.2.md): import modes, requirements and readback rules.
- [Clean APEX deployment](clean-apex-deployment.md): local history and coordination without service tables.
- [Configuration](configuration.md): environments, connections and policy settings.
- [Existing applications](existing-app.md): adopt an application and work from a checkpoint.

title: Clean APEX deployment
text:
Deployment without service tables

Supported APEX installations require no APEXREST service tables or setup DDL. Deployment history and coordination are local. Read this page if you deploy from more than one machine or want to know where that local state lives.

 Before you start

- Local state belongs to $APEXREST_HOME/deployment-control/ and must persist between runs.
- Different machines/homes do not share a lock or migration history: the plugin does not provide cross-machine coordination.
- Use one durable deployment runner/home and serialize independent machines externally (for example a single CI deploy job).

 Implemented

| Area              | Behavior                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| ----------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Coordination mode | Plan and apply always use local durable coordination. No APEXREST control table is queried or created; there is no database-backed coordination mode.                                                |
| Legacy setting    | A legacy deploymentControl: "local" in old project files is accepted and ignored; other values are rejected.                                                                                       |
| Migration history | Local migration history records checksums and started before SQL execution. Successful migrations are not replayed; changed checksums and unresolved history stop a subsequent plan.               |
| Ownership         | Local ownership serializes apps sharing a DB/service/parsing schema within one managed home. A dead preparing owner may recover; writing ownership after an unknown outcome requires reconciliation. |
| Plans             | Plans bind the coordination scope and local store identity. Source/target drift, authorization, backups, readback verification and restore policy are retained.                                      |
| Agent skills      | The setup and safety skills state that APEXREST service tables are not prerequisites, so the agent proceeds with apexrest_ship without requesting them for ordinary deployment.                    |

 Verification scope

 Covered by local tests

Local tests cover:

- plan/apply with no control-table calls
- persisted migration history
- checksum rejection
- interrupted-write retention
- schema contention
- a separate Node runner
- dead-owner behavior
- store-change rejection

Oracle writes in these tests are explicitly fixtures, not connected deployment evidence. See [testing](testing.md) and [implementation status](implementation-status.md) for local check scope and remaining release gates.

 Not covered

These require their own integration evidence:

- connected imports
- restore
- migration failure injection
- authenticated host-browser interactions
- independent-machine concurrency

Required reports must match the current immutable source before release readiness can pass.

 Related

- [Deployment safety](deployment-safety.mdbackups-and-coordination): the canonical rules for backups, coordination and recovery.
- [Configuration](configuration.mddeployment-coordination): the coordination settings in a project.

title: Configuration
text:
Configuration and connections

This page describes the project file apexrest.json, environments, connection references, authorization policy and runtime variables. Use it when you set up a target or change how the plugin connects, reviews and deploys.

 Before you start

- Implementation uses the current host session (Codex or Claude Code) and its permissions.
- A project has one apexrest.json and one pinned toolchain lock, named by the required toolchain.lockFile (a path inside the project). project init creates both, copying the reviewed lock of the selected profile, with an empty environment map.
- Every target operation requires an explicit environment; the plugin never guesses a database, workspace or application ID.

 Optional project settings

| Setting             | Purpose                                                                                           | Values                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| toolchain.profile | Selects 26.1 or 26.2 authoring references                                                     | 26.1, 26.2                                                                                                                                                                           |
| decisionApi       | Configures component selection only; overrides the [machine-wide default](machine-wide-settings) | enabled (default false), apiKeyEnv (default OPENAI_API_KEY), optional project-relative envFile, and timeoutMs (default 3000, range 250–10000)                                  |
| peerReview        | Enables cross-vendor review of saved ship plans                                                   | mode (off default, advisory, required), vendor (auto default, codex, claude), optional model passed to the peer CLI, and timeoutSeconds (default 600, range 60–1800) |

- toolchain.lockFile: setup and dependencies install with --project, or run from the project root (the folder that holds apexrest.json; subfolders are not searched), install and record the Node.js, Java and SQLcl this lock pins. Its entries must match a lock shipped with the plugin.
- toolchain.profile: existing projects without it retain 26.1 behavior; selecting a profile does not upgrade a database or rewrite Oracle source metadata. See [APEX 26.2 support](apex-26.2.md) for the matching compiler lock and partial-import requirements.
- decisionApi: the key comes from the process environment first, then the explicitly configured private ignored ENV file. Selection falls back locally on API/credential failures; ordinary reference search/read remain local. See [Decisions selection](component-catalog.mdoptional-openai-decisions-selection) for configuration and CLI/MCP examples.
- peerReview: see [Peer review](cross-vendor-peer-review).

 Verification browser preference

- The verification browser preference (host in-app browser, alias codex) is stored per project in .apexrest/panel/preferences.json.
- The default {"browserMode":"codex"} is the legacy name of host and behaves identically.
- apexrest_browser_open accepts browserMode to override it for one call.
- apexrest_status detail:project reports the current value.

 Machine-wide settings

apexrest settings holds settings for every project and host on this computer, in APEXREST_HOME/settings.json (default ~/.apexrest):

sh
apexrest settings status --json
apexrest settings configure --decision-api on --catalog on --json


| Option                    | Effect                                                                                                                                              |
| ------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| --decision-api on\|off  | Default OpenAI Decisions selection for projects whose apexrest.json has no decisionApi. A project decisionApi always wins.                    |
| --api-key-env NAME      | Environment variable holding the key for the global default (OPENAI_API_KEY). The global default never reads an ENV file; that stays per project. |
| --decision-timeout-ms N | Timeout for the global default, 250–10000 (3000).                                                                                                   |
| --catalog on\|off       | off turns off reference search, read and select for every host: they return CATALOG_DISABLED and agents continue without lookups.               |
| --usage-log on\|off     | Enables private, bounded usage records for backend elapsed time and reported token counters. Disabled by default.                                   |

settings status also reports, without any database, network or credential read:

- whether the key variable is set in the calling process (never its value);
- the bundled catalog sizes;
- recent projects in recent-projects.json: a successful operation with --project makes that project current; status reads do not.

Recent projects stay on the computer and are written only when APEXREST_HOME already exists. Set APEXREST_USAGE=0 to disable recent-project recording and usage logging. The repository test runner sets it.

 Local token and time logging

Enable logging for both hosts that share this managed home, then inspect the most recent entries.

sh
apexrest settings configure --usage-log on --json
apexrest usage status --limit 20 --json
apexrest settings configure --usage-log off --json


The owner-private APEXREST_HOME/usage-log.json retains at most 1,000 entries and 2 MiB. Retention removes the oldest entries first. Each backend operation records elapsed wall time, SQLcl time, host identity when known and success or failure. Composite action routing records one outer operation. Settings and log-inspection commands do not create timing entries. A logging failure does not change the operation's outcome.

Decisions selection records the input, cache-read, cache-write, output, reasoning-output and total token counters supplied by its API response, with the model and source. Cache reads and writes must fit within input, reasoning tokens must fit within output, and total must equal input plus output. Inconsistent API counters remain unavailable in the log. Each operation without token counters reports their unavailability. A CLI or MCP process cannot observe the host model's token consumption.

For actual native-host accounting, explicitly import JSON output from one completed native CLI run.

sh
 Capture each run using the host's own JSON output option.
codex exec --json 'Your task' > /private/path/codex-run.jsonl
claude -p --output-format json 'Your task' > /private/path/claude-run.json

apexrest usage import --host codex --file /private/path/codex-run.jsonl --elapsed-ms 12345 --json
 For complete cumulative output from an initial Codex session and its resumed turns:
apexrest usage import --host codex --file /private/path/codex-session.jsonl --counter-mode cumulative-session --elapsed-ms 23456 --json
apexrest usage import --host claude --file /private/path/claude-run.json --json


The default Codex import accepts one completed turn from one identified thread. Multiple turns or resumed output require --counter-mode cumulative-session: this explicitly declares the cumulative counters observed in Codex CLI 0.160.0. The importer uses the final complete snapshot, rather than summing earlier snapshots; repeated announcements of the same thread are allowed. Different threads, counter decreases, dropped known counters, open turns and failed turns without completed usage are rejected. The native output does not identify its counter semantics, so historical per-turn formats cannot be inferred automatically. Wait for all included native runs to finish before importing.

New Codex imports retain an opaque SHA-256 session identity and counter mode, without the raw session ID. A different overlapping capture of the same retained session is rejected by default. Explicit cumulative snapshots can replace one previous cumulative entry when every known counter and the whole-session measured elapsed time are nondecreasing. An identical snapshot adds nothing. Historical entries without that identity remain unchanged; do not reimport their overlapping work. Deduplication and overlap checks cover the retained log.

Claude imports use one final result's counters, normalizing input to include cache reads and writes. A synthetic failed login result with no provider-backed usage remains unavailable. Genuine reported error-phase usage is retained. Models reported by the host are retained. Claude's reported duration is preserved. Supply --elapsed-ms only with elapsed time measured by the caller for the exact included work; for a resumed cumulative Codex session, sum its measured native phases without idle time. An absent duration remains unavailable.

Exact input contents are deduplicated within the retained records. Host-run totals and plugin-operation measurements have separate scopes and token sources. Summing the same work across those scopes would count it twice. Logging retains no prompt, completion, tool arguments, source path, database identity, credentials or session ID, and it calculates no cost. The explicit import reader accepts bounded, owner-controlled regular files up to 8 MiB and reads no other host history. Captured native output can contain task content, so keep the capture private.

 Native job waits

Codex MCP requests accept waitSeconds up to 30 for apexrest_ship and apexrest_job, leaving headroom below [Codex's default 60-second tool timeout](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/extend/mcp?surface=cli). The advertised field schema and request validator share the limit. Larger values are rejected before project loading or work starts. Ship defaults to 25 seconds, and job status defaults to an immediate read. CLI job status and Claude retain their existing 120-second maximum.

The MCP protocol client name identifies known Codex and Claude clients. Managed launchers supply APEXREST_HOST=codex|claude for unfamiliar client names. A recognized protocol identity takes precedence for this wait policy. An unrecognized client without that registration retains the generic limit of 120 seconds. Check its client timeout before choosing a longer wait.

These values cap observation waits. Planning, compilation and apply preflight can run in process before a background job exists. Plan responses retain their usual shape. Workers can continue after an observation ends. Poll the original jobId and reconcile a lost outcome before requesting another execution.

 Configure an environment

Add an entry such as environments.dev to the generated apexrest.json:

json
{
  "kind": "development",
  "readConnectionRef": "dev-read",
  "deployConnectionRef": "dev-deploy",
  "workspace": "YOUR_WORKSPACE",
  "parsingSchema": "YOUR_SCHEMA",
  "applicationId": 123,
  "baseUrl": "https://your-host.example/ords/r/workspace/crm/",
  "databaseIdentity": {
    "dbUniqueName": "YOUR_DB",
    "serviceName": "YOUR_SERVICE"
  },
  "allowedOrigins": ["https://your-host.example"],
  "expectedMarker": "apexrest-crm"
}


- These are placeholders, not a working target. Use the actual database unique name and service, workspace, parsing schema and app ID.
- expectedMarker can identify the expected application during browser inspection.
- allowedOrigins lists approved application origins. Adding an origin does not grant permission to mutate its data.

 Schema rules

- The generated schemas/project.schema.json is the exact public schema. Unknown fields are rejected.
- Existing project files may still contain retired tests and database.testsDir fields: loading ignores these fields; remove them when updating configuration.
- Old plans must be regenerated against the current configuration.
- Source, migration, package, artifact and toolchain paths must remain inside the project.

 List and test saved SQLcl connections

Checking database access requires no project or APEXREST alias:

sh
apexrest connection list --saved --json
apexrest connection test 'Development connection' --saved --json


- These commands read the SQLcl store directly and test the exact saved name with a read-only identity query.
- If the store is empty or credentials are missing, configure them in SQLcl.
- You can then register references for a project environment as described below.
- CLI commands without --saved use those references; in the conversation, apexrest_project action:connection_list and action:connection_test do the same.

 SQLcl mode and database transport

| Setting            | Values                                                     |
| ------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| SQLcl mode         | cli subprocess or mcp, the official SQLcl stdio server |
| Database transport | direct listener or ords                                |

- Both are saved per managed home with apexrest sqlcl configure --mode cli|mcp --database-transport direct|ords --json; apexrest sqlcl status --json reads them.
- For HTTP access when the listener is unreachable, configure plugin-level ORDS URL, username and password and select the ords transport. See [SQL through ORDS](ords.md).
- The saved SQLcl connections below apply to direct access.

 Save connection references

1. Create named connections interactively in SQLcl's local connection store.
2. Register their names:

   sh
   apexrest connection add dev-read --sqlcl-name saved-read-connection
   apexrest connection add dev-deploy --sqlcl-name saved-deploy-connection
   apexrest connection test dev-read --json
   

- The examples assume the [managed CLI launcher](getting-started.mduse-the-cli).
- APEXREST stores connection names rather than passwords.
- A read connection can use fewer privileges than its deploy counterpart.
- Removing an APEXREST reference with connection remove preserves the SQLcl store entry.
- Never put credentials in apexrest.json, environment examples, prompts or issue reports.

 Application authorization

 Authorization and grants

- There is no folder trust step. The plugin may use the selected project and other required directories within host filesystem permissions.
- Legacy trustedProjects in $APEXREST_HOME/policy.json is optional ignored compatibility data.
- The private policy retains exact-project/target/plan temporary grants; an identified DEV/QA/TEST application task authorizes its necessary import without repeated confirmation.
- Configuration and tool output do not grant consent.

 Environment kinds

Supported environment kinds are development (or dev), qa, test and production.

| Target                              | Rule                                                                                        |
| ----------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Production-marked targets           | Never deploy/restore, including when local or given a signature.                            |
| Actual local non-production targets | Allow all task-scoped database changes without a separate risk prompt.                      |
| Remote targets                      | Remote dangerous operations require a described exact plan and explicit human confirmation. |

See the canonical [deployment safety rules](deployment-safety.md) for locality, precedence, backups, interrupted-import recovery and confirmation fields.

 Local ENV credentials

- Connection setup may use envFile with optional urlKey, usernameKey and passwordKey from a regular user-owned, Git-ignored and untracked local ENV file.
- It is parsed as literal data and values are never returned in operation results.
- Authorized requested browser login may use such local credentials without a paste/trust step; never persist browser cookies/profiles.
- For passwordFile, the private regular file must physically resolve inside the managed home, working directory or a configured project. The reader checks the opened file's identity and enforces owner-only permissions on POSIX.

 Cross-vendor peer review

Claude Code and Codex can review each other's APEX changes.

 Run a review

1. The host agent prepares a plan with apexrest_ship mode:plan.
2. It calls apexrest_peer_review action:review plan:<planPath>.
3. The runtime runs the other vendor's CLI in the project directory with the user's existing sign-in (ChatGPT or OPENAI_API_KEY for Codex; Claude subscription or ANTHROPIC_API_KEY for Claude Code). APEXREST never handles those credentials.
4. The reviewer receives the plan preview, database operations and a bounded Git diff of the deployable sources and returns approve or changes_requested with findings.
5. The verdict is written to .apexrest/reviews/<planDigest>.json.

| Host        | Peer command (read-only)                                                            |
| ----------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Claude Code | codex exec --sandbox read-only --ephemeral --output-schema …                      |
| Codex       | claude -p --restricted --tools Read,Grep,Glob --strict-mcp-config --json-schema … |

 How the peer CLI is found

- vendor: auto picks the opposite of the detected host (APEXREST_HOST, then the MCP client name sent at initialization, then the host's own environment); pass vendor explicitly when detection is unavailable.
- On Windows the CLI is found on absolute PATH entries (never in the project folder): a native codex.exe or claude.exe runs directly, and an npm-installed codex.cmd or claude.cmd shim runs the Node script it points to, without cmd.exe.
- APEXREST_CODEX_BIN and APEXREST_CLAUDE_BIN override the CLI; a .js, .mjs or .cjs override runs through Node.

 Review local-only work

- Local-only work without an Oracle target can still be reviewed: omit plan (CLI apexrest peer review without --plan).
- The reviewer then receives the list of application and database sources and the Git diff, and the verdict is written to .apexrest/reviews/source-<sourceDigest>.json.
- A source review is advisory only; it never satisfies the required apply gate, which needs a review of the exact saved plan.

 Gate modes

Gate modes apply to apexrest_ship mode:apply (and the CLI ship --mode apply):

| Mode       | Behavior                                                                                                                               |
| ---------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| off      | No review state is read.                                                                                                               |
| advisory | Apply proceeds and reports peerReview status (approve, changes_requested or missing).                                          |
| required | Apply fails with PEER_REVIEW_REQUIRED or PEER_REVIEW_CHANGES_REQUESTED unless an approving review of the exact plan digest exists. |

In required mode:

- A fresh plan created by apply itself is never reviewed, so review the saved plan and apply that path.
- The reviewer must be the other vendor: a review by the host agent itself (for example vendor: claude from Claude Code) is refused with PEER_REVIEW_SAME_VENDOR and does not satisfy the gate.

 Limits of peer review

- Before the reviewer runs, the saved plan must match its own digest and pass the same local checks as apply (sources, configuration, toolchain, project, target and lifetime); otherwise the review fails with PLAN_TAMPERED or the apply-time code and nothing is recorded.
- The optional focus text is passed to the reviewer as a fenced request from the reviewed agent, not as review rules.
- Interrupted-import recovery is not gated.
- The gate is a single-user workflow control, not a security boundary: the host agent can edit local files.
- apexrest_peer_review action:status (CLI apexrest peer status) reports which CLIs are installed and signed in.
- Peer runs use the other vendor's subscription limits or API billing; headless Claude usage (claude -p) is subject to Anthropic's current plan terms.

 Deployment coordination

- Coordination is always local and is not configurable: durable migration history and schema ownership live in $APEXREST_HOME/deployment-control/, scoped to the database identity and parsing schema.
- No APEXREST service tables are needed or created.
- Plans bind the store identity.
- Deleting the local history or silently switching to a fresh home is not a recovery procedure.
- The local store serializes runners that share one managed home.
- Independent machines or homes are not coordinated: preserve one durable deployment runner/home and serialize other machines externally, for example through a single CI deploy job.
- Database-backed coordination was removed. For older project files, deploymentControl is still accepted only with the value "local" and has no effect; any other value is rejected. Remove the field when convenient.

See [Clean APEX deployment](clean-apex-deployment.md).

 Application verification

- When the user requests browser verification, use the built-in or user-selected browser to inspect the requested interaction.
- Confirmed error-free server deployment is success without a mandatory browser step.
- Compiler, metadata and import checks remain separate.
- The plugin has no automatic application test runners or saved browser-authentication state.
- Repository self-tests validate the plugin implementation.

See [testing](testing.md).

 Runtime configuration

| Variable              | Purpose                                                           |
| --------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| APEXREST_HOME       | Private managed runtime, policy, connections and deployment state |
| APEXREST_SQLCL      | Explicit reviewed SQLcl executable                                |
| APEXREST_JAVA_HOME  | Java runtime selected for SQLcl                                   |
| APEXREST_RESOURCES  | Trusted host override for bundled resources                       |
| NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS | Additional certificate authorities for Node connections           |

 Deployment speed-up switches

Four switches turn off the deployment speed-ups described in [architecture](architecture.mdpersistent-sqlcl-engine); each restores the previous behavior when set to 0:

| Switch                      | Speed-up it turns off                                       |
| --------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| APEXREST_CONNECTED_READS  | One connected SQLcl server for the reads of a plan or apply |
| APEXREST_WARM_IMPORT      | The prepared import server                                  |
| APEXREST_CAPABILITY_CACHE | The capability files in the managed home                    |
| APEXREST_PREWARM          | The background compiler preload in the MCP server           |

 Trust, proxies and paths

- These overrides belong to the trusted local host, not project-controlled inputs.
- The bootstrap supports Node 24 environment proxies through --use-env-proxy.
- Vendor downloads honor HTTPS_PROXY/HTTP_PROXY and NO_PROXY through Node's environment proxy support; when a proxy is configured but this Node cannot apply it, setup fails with PROXY_UNSUPPORTED instead of bypassing the proxy.
- Paths with spaces and Unicode are supported; quotes, substitutions and control characters in SQLcl tokens are rejected.

 Related

- [Deployment safety](deployment-safety.md): the canonical authorization, plan, backup and recovery rules.
- [SQL through ORDS](ords.md): the ords database transport.
- [APEX 26.2 partial imports](apex-26.2.md): the 26.2 toolchain and import modes.
- [Development status](status.md): read the current configuration and connections.

title: SQL through ORDS
text:
SQL through ORDS

This page shows how to reach the database over HTTP(S) through ORDS instead of the Oracle listener. Use it when the listener, commonly on port 1521, is unreachable but the schema's ORDS endpoint is available.

 When to use

- Select the ords database transport (apexrest sqlcl configure --mode cli --database-transport ords) when the Oracle listener is unreachable but the schema's ORDS endpoint is available.
- This is a plugin-wide preference for new operations. Existing operations keep their selected transport.
- Direct Oracle connections remain available when you switch back.

 Configure the connection

1. Create a local password file. See [Password file rules](password-file-rules).
2. Save an APEXREST connection reference with the schema URL, the database username and the password file. Use apexrest connection add, or apexrest_project action:connection_add with ordsUrl, ordsUsername and passwordFile in the conversation.
3. Select the ords transport.
4. Test the reference.
5. Add the corresponding dev-deploy reference before deploying.

sh
apexrest connection add dev-read \
  --ords-url https://ords.example.invalid/ords/app_user/ \
  --ords-username app_user --password-file /path/to/local/ords-password.txt
apexrest sqlcl configure --mode cli --database-transport ords --json
apexrest connection test dev-read --json

 Return to the existing direct connection mappings.
apexrest sqlcl configure --mode cli --database-transport direct --json


The sample hostname and username are examples, not a configured or verified target.

The equivalent interactive Oracle connection is:

sql
connect -orest app_user@https://ords.example.invalid/ords/app_user/


 Account and URL

- Use the credentials of an existing Oracle database account allowed to access the schema through ORDS; no separate ORDS account is needed.
- Saving the reference configures the plugin to use that account.
- Use separate references for readConnectionRef and deployConnectionRef when their privileges differ.
- The URL identifies the REST-enabled schema, for example https://ords.example.invalid/ords/app_user/; its schema alias can differ from the database username.
- Use the schema URL provided by your administrator, rather than an APEX application URL or a /_/sql URL.
- The URL must use https:; plain http: is accepted only for localhost, 127.0.0.1 or [::1], because it would expose the database password.

 Password file rules

- Passwords never travel through chat or tool arguments: the CLI and the apexrest_project tool read a local password file rather than taking the password as a value.
- The file must be a regular file, not a symbolic link, and on POSIX it must be accessible only by its owner (chmod 600); otherwise the command fails with PASSWORD_FILE_UNSAFE.
- The password file must be a private regular file (mode 600) inside the managed home ($APEXREST_HOME, default ~/.apexrest), the project directory passed as project, or the current working directory; other locations are rejected so connection setup cannot read arbitrary private files.
- Omitting --password-file when updating a reference preserves the existing password for the same endpoint and database username; changing either requires credentials for the new identity.

 Where settings are stored

| Content             | Location                          |
| ------------------- | --------------------------------- |
| Transport           | $APEXREST_HOME/sqlcl.json       |
| Connection metadata | $APEXREST_HOME/connections.json |
| Passwords           | $APEXREST_HOME/credentials/     |

- These are plugin-level local files, normally under ~/.apexrest, rather than project files. Passwords are stored separately from the connection metadata.
- Secret files use owner-only permissions on POSIX; they are not an encrypted password vault.
- Do not copy them into source control or share them.
- SQLcl saved connections are used only for the direct transport; ORDS does not require saving a connection in SQLcl.

 Switch back to the direct transport

- When you switch back to the direct transport, the reference's saved SQLcl connection name (--sqlcl-name) applies again.
- Switching transport preserves both the direct mapping and the saved ORDS credentials for the reference.
- apexrest_status detail:project lists the references without secrets.

 APEXlang import and export

 How ORDS runs SQL and APEXlang

- ORDS uses SQLcl's OREST driver for SQL and metadata queries.
- The execution backend is CLI; selecting official SQLcl MCP together with ORDS is rejected explicitly. APEXREST's own MCP tools remain available.
- ORDS sessions keep one SQLcl process per call; the pooled SQLcl engine applies to offline compiler work and SQLcl mcp mode only.
- For metadata queries, the adapter initializes bind values with SQLcl's client-side VARIABLE ... = ... syntax. This avoids a separate EXEC request for an output bind, which the REST driver can reject with ORA-17283.
- APEXlang operations use the Oracle compiler and libraries from the selected SQLcl installation.
- A bundled Java helper handles APEXlang imports in one REST request so installation package state survives across compiled blocks.
- Exports use APEX_EXPORT and a CLOB containing the base64 ZIP to avoid the REST driver's unsupported BLOB output accessor. The ZIP preserves Oracle-generated APEXlang files and .apex metadata.
- Ordinary full backups retain APEXlang sources from this export path; legacy SQL exports remain available for explicit compatibility operations.
- Offline generation and validation retain the existing Oracle SQLcl commands.

 Limits and safety rules

- A missing ORDS configuration fails explicitly; the plugin never retries through the direct listener.
- The project's database, service, schema, workspace and application identity checks still apply.
- ORDS REST SQL commits successful requests and rolls back failed requests.
- Separate requests do not share database session state, and a failed later request cannot roll back an earlier successful one.
- Existing deployment approval, identity, backup, drift and unknown-outcome checks remain in place.
- A timeout or interruption after an import starts requires reconciliation before retrying.

 Prerequisites and verification

- Use SQLcl and APEX 26.1 or later for APEXlang, with the required workspace/schema privileges.
- ORDS must expose REST-Enabled SQL for the selected schema and accept the supplied database authentication.
- HTTPS is required for every non-loopback endpoint.

 Java for the import helper

- The Java helper requires a JDK 21 or newer containing jdk.compiler; the managed SQLcl JRE alone does not provide it.
- The adapter checks the configured Java first, then an already-installed JDK from JAVA_HOME or PATH.
- This fallback applies only to the helper and leaves SQLcl's managed JRE settings unchanged.
- If no suitable JDK is available, ORDS_JDK_REQUIRED blocks the operation before credentials or database requests are submitted.
- The adapter does not download Java or change runtime configuration automatically.

 Related

- [Configuration](configuration.md): environments, connection references and SQLcl mode.
- [Deployment safety](deployment-safety.md): the rules that still apply over ORDS.
- [Codex Cloud](codex-cloud.md): run the CLI in a container with ORDS.

Oracle references: [CONNECT and OREST](https://docs.oracle.com/en/database/oracle/sql-developer-command-line/26.2/sqcug/connect.html), [APEXlang prerequisites](https://docs.oracle.com/en/database/oracle/sql-developer-command-line/26.1/sqcug/prerequisites-apexlang.html), and [REST-Enabled SQL](https://docs.oracle.com/en/database/oracle/oracle-rest-data-services/25.3/orddg/rest-enabled-sql-service.html).

title: Codex Cloud
text:
Run APEXREST in Codex Cloud

This guide sets up APEXREST's bundled CLI inside the Cloud container, using ORDS over HTTPS for database access. It is for teams that want a Codex Cloud agent to run apexrest commands against a development/test database.

The example below adapts a project-specific Cloud bootstrap into reusable scripts. It does not register the plugin or expose its MCP tools and skills to the Cloud agent. Those integrations require their own host verification; see [host integration](codex-integration.md).

 Before you start

You need:

- an application repository connected to Codex Cloud;
- a local APEXREST checkout, to copy the example scripts from;
- a development/test ORDS schema URL over HTTPS, and a database account that already has authorized access to REST-Enabled SQL on that schema;
- a Cloud environment with Node.js 24, a Java 21 JDK, Git and Bash;
- a decision on credential retention: this example keeps a credential file in the container (see [step 2](2-configure-the-cloud-environment)).

The steps:

1. [Prepare your application repository](1-prepare-your-application-repository)
2. [Configure the Cloud environment](2-configure-the-cloud-environment)
3. [Set setup and maintenance commands](3-set-setup-and-maintenance-commands)
4. [Configure network access](4-configure-network-access)
5. [Verify from a Cloud task](5-verify-from-a-cloud-task)
6. [Give the agent project instructions](6-give-the-agent-project-instructions)

The bootstrap and connected workflow require verification in the actual Cloud environment. See [Verification scope](verification-scope).

 1. Prepare your application repository

1. Copy the files in [the Cloud example directory](examples/codex-cloud/) into scripts/codex-cloud/ in the application repository connected to Codex Cloud. Keep all files together. From your application repository, with a local APEXREST checkout available:

   sh
   mkdir -p scripts/codex-cloud
   cp /path/to/apexrest/docs/examples/codex-cloud/ scripts/codex-cloud/
   

2. Add these entries to the application's .gitignore before running setup:

   gitignore
   .codex/cloud/
   .apexrest/
   

3. Commit the example scripts and ignore rules to the repository's default branch used for Cloud cache preparation, and ensure they are also present on the task branch. Cloud checks out the task branch when resuming the cache; see [container caching](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/environments/cloud-environment).

Generated tools, credentials, logs, plans and backups must remain private. The scripts are documentation examples, not files automatically installed by the plugin or its npm package.
