 The pinned build

- The [version file](examples/codex-cloud/version.sh) pins a reviewed immutable checkout with manifest version 2.0.0.
- Setup verifies the commit and version, then uses plugins/apexrest-apex/runtime/apexrest.mjs; it needs neither an npm release nor a TypeScript build.
- Review and change both pins together when adopting another build.
- The bootstrap and connected workflow require verification in the actual Cloud environment.

 2. Configure the Cloud environment

1. Select your application repository in Codex Cloud environment settings.
2. Select Node.js 24 and Java 21 under package versions. Java must be a JDK with jdk.compiler, not just a JRE. Git and Bash must also be available.
3. Set the environment variables in the table below. Replace every target placeholder with values supplied for your development/test environment.
4. Add APEXREST_ORDS_PASSWORD as a Secret, not a normal environment variable or repository file.

| Variable                         | Value or purpose                                                                                                 |
| -------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| CODEX_CLOUD                    | 1; explicit opt-in to this example's Linux setup.                                                              |
| APEXREST_ACCEPT_ORACLE_LICENSE | 1 only after accepting the [Oracle terms](https://www.oracle.com/downloads/licenses/oracle-free-license.html). |
| APEXREST_PERSIST_CREDENTIALS   | 1 only if you authorize the credential retention described below.                                              |
| APEXREST_ORDS_URL              | Schema URL, for example https://ords.example.invalid/ords/app_user/.                                           |
| APEXREST_ORDS_USERNAME         | Database username, for example app_user; the schema alias may differ.                                          |
| APEXREST_CONNECTION_REF        | A local reference name, for example cloud-dev (the default).                                                   |
| APEXREST_EXPECTED_SCHEMA       | Optional exact expected parsing schema from the identity check.                                                  |
| APEXREST_EXPECTED_SERVICE      | Optional exact expected database service from the identity check.                                                |

The account must already have authorized access to REST-Enabled SQL on that ORDS schema. Use the schema URL, not an APEX application URL or the /_/sql endpoint; see [ORDS configuration](ords.md).

 Credential retention

Read this before you set APEXREST_PERSIST_CREDENTIALS=1.

- Cloud secrets are available during setup, then removed from the agent environment.
- This example deliberately retains a credential file for later CLI commands.
- Cloud container caching can retain that file, and Business/Enterprise caches can be shared by environment users. Use an environment whose users are authorized for that database account. See [OpenAI's Cloud environment documentation](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/environments/cloud-environment).

With APEXREST_PERSIST_CREDENTIALS=1, setup:

1. passes the secret through a temporary owner-only file to connection add --password-file;
2. removes the temporary file;
3. keeps the APEXREST credential under .codex/cloud/tools/credentials/ with POSIX mode 0600.

This is not an encrypted vault: the agent and processes running as the same user can read it. If this retention is unsuitable, do not enable the flag or use this connected example. Never print the secret, enable shell tracing, or include .codex/cloud/ in commits or shared artifacts.

 3. Set setup and maintenance commands

Setup script:

sh
bash scripts/codex-cloud/setup.sh


Maintenance script:

sh
bash scripts/codex-cloud/setup.sh --maintenance


 What setup does

Setup:

- checks the pinned checkout;
- previews and installs managed dependencies;
- prepares a private JDK;
- selects sqlcl configure --mode cli --database-transport ords;
- saves the connection;
- runs doctor plus a read-only database identity check.

It creates no application or business data and grants no deployment permission.

 What maintenance does

Maintenance reuses the installed build and credentials, refreshes Java proxy/CA settings and repeats the connection check. It does not reinstall dependencies.

| Situation                                        | Action                                                                                |
| ------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Missing build, changed pin or missing credential | Rerun setup with the secret available.                                                |
| Credential rotation                              | Update the Secret and rerun setup; retaining an old local credential is not rotation. |
| Incompatible setup changes                       | Use Reset cache.                                                                  |

 The launcher and cached containers

- The launcher restores APEXREST_HOME, APEXREST_JAVA_HOME and the selected Node executable on every invocation. A setup-only export would not persist into the agent phase.
- Cloud may resume a cached container and run maintenance; after incompatible setup changes, use Reset cache. See [environment lifecycle](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/environments/cloud-environment).

 4. Configure network access

Enable agent internet access for the exact ORDS hostname and allow POST, which REST-Enabled SQL needs even for read-only queries. Setup download access and agent-phase access are separate settings. See [OpenAI's agent internet access documentation](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/cloud/internet-access).

Setup also needs access to the canonical GitHub repository and the dependency download hosts shown by the installer preview.

 Why HTTPS and ORDS

- The example uses HTTPS because a Cloud HTTP proxy does not establish reachability to the Oracle listener on port 1521.
- Plain http: ORDS URLs are accepted only for loopback.
- The example makes no listener-connectivity assumption.

 Proxy and certificates

The [network helper](examples/codex-cloud/network.sh) enables NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY=1.

- Vendor downloads then honor HTTPS_PROXY and NO_PROXY.
- If a proxy is configured but the running Node cannot apply it, setup stops with PROXY_UNSUPPORTED rather than bypassing the proxy.

The [Java helper](examples/codex-cloud/setup-java.mjs):

- copies the environment JDK into .codex/cloud/java;
- writes proxy settings to its private conf/net.properties;
- imports the environment CA bundle from NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS into its private lib/security/jssecacerts;
- preserves the default trust roots and leaves the host JDK unchanged.

APEXREST strips Java option environment variables for Oracle subprocesses, so JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS alone is insufficient here.

Proxy rules for the helper:

- It accepts an HTTP proxy without URL credentials, reading https_proxy, HTTPS_PROXY, http_proxy, then HTTP_PROXY.
- Host/domain entries in NO_PROXY are mapped to Java; CIDR entries remain proxied.
- Unsupported proxy settings fail explicitly.
- Keep TLS certificate verification enabled; refresh the private truststore when the environment CA changes.

 5. Verify from a Cloud task

Start a task after successful setup and run these commands from the application repository. Replace cloud-dev if you chose another reference:

sh
bash scripts/codex-cloud/apexrest doctor --json
bash scripts/codex-cloud/apexrest sqlcl status --json
bash scripts/codex-cloud/apexrest connection list --json
bash scripts/codex-cloud/apexrest connection test --name cloud-dev --json
bash scripts/codex-cloud/apexrest --help


Check the actual JSON and exit codes:

- the selected mode must be cli;
- network transport must be ords;
- the connection identity must match your intended database/schema.

How to read the results:

- A successful doctor command is insufficient: it reports probes separately and does not test the database.
- Its nativeHost: requires-host-verification and database: not-configured fields do not override a separately successful connection test.
- A missing local Codex executable also does not by itself prevent direct CLI/ORDS operations.
- The connection reference belongs to APEXREST, not SQLcl's saved connection store; do not replace the command with sql -name cloud-dev or connection test --saved.
- Save only sanitized evidence; identity output can contain private target names.

 6. Give the agent project instructions

Add a short Cloud-specific section to the application repository's AGENTS.md:

markdown
 APEXREST in Codex Cloud

- Run APEXREST commands with bash scripts/codex-cloud/apexrest.
- Check doctor, SQLcl configuration and the configured connection identity first.
- Use SQLcl CLI with ORDS; this bootstrap does not register native plugin tools.
- Keep .codex/cloud/ and .apexrest/ private. Never print credentials.
- Do not run setup, native plugin registration or dependency downloads in every task.
- Use the configured project/environment and existing deployment safeguards.
- Report compiler checks, database checks and browser observations separately.


 Before application work

- Configure the target in apexrest.json, including workspace, schema, application ID, database identity and the correct read/deploy references.
- Follow the [safety rules](deployment-safety.md) and retain validation, backup, exact-plan authorization, drift and unknown-outcome protections from [configuration](configuration.md) and [deployment safety](deployment-safety.md).
- Installation and a successful connection test do not authorize an import.

 Deployment history and backups

- The example keeps local deployment history under APEXREST_HOME.
- Cloud caches are not durable backup storage or cross-container coordination: preserve private backups/history outside an expiring container and serialize runners before authorizing deployments.
- Do not reset away an unresolved operation's records or silently start fresh history against the same schema.

 Browser checks and native plugin features

- Browser dependencies are skipped. Browser checks require separately configured tools, authentication and actual observations.
- The CLI bootstrap does not establish that $apexrest-work or automatic skill/MCP discovery work in Cloud.
- The CLI equivalents of the work cycle are apexrest apex validate, apexrest ship --mode plan|apply --user-request TEXT and apexrest job status.
- Use the launcher for the documented flow and report unavailable checks explicitly.

 Troubleshooting

| Symptom                                                  | Action                                                                                               |
| -------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Setup exits with “Skipping Cloud setup”                  | Set CODEX_CLOUD=1 in environment settings.                                                         |
| Unsupported Node or no JDK compiler                      | Select Node 24 and JDK 21, then rerun setup.                                                         |
| Pinned checkout/runtime/credentials missing after resume | Rerun setup with the Secret; maintenance cannot reconstruct an uncached environment.                 |
| HTTP 401/403 or failed identity check                    | Verify the account, REST-Enabled SQL access, schema URL, expected identity and agent POST allowlist. |
| Java timeout or certificate error                        | Check proxy/CA settings and run maintenance; do not disable TLS.                                     |
| CLI works but no plugin tools or skills appear           | Native Cloud integration is not installed or verified by this example; continue through the CLI.     |

 Verification scope

Local script syntax and package checks do not establish an actual Cloud setup/resume, connected Oracle operation, native plugin discovery or browser session. Complete the checks above on the intended environment and record the resulting scope; see [implementation status](implementation-status.md) and [next actions](next-actions.md).

 Related

- [SQL through ORDS](ords.md): the schema URL and REST-Enabled SQL.
- [Configuration](configuration.md): environments, connections and policy.
- [Deployment safety](deployment-safety.md): the plan, grant, import and recovery model.
- [Host integration](codex-integration.md): what native plugin registration involves.

title: Development status
text:
Development status

The development status is one read-only snapshot of the local development state for an application project. Use it to see configuration, connections, pending changes, jobs and deployment history before you continue work in the [current conversation](chat-workflow.md).

 Read the status

| Request                                 | Tool call                                  | CLI                                                           |
| --------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Snapshot of the local development state | apexrest_status with detail: "project" | apexrest status --detail project or apexrest panel status |
| Probe of the local toolchain instead    | apexrest_status with detail: "doctor"  | apexrest status --detail doctor                             |

sh
apexrest status --detail project --project /absolute/application --json
apexrest status --detail doctor --json


- The snapshot is plain JSON for the host agent and the CLI.
- Use the application project containing apexrest.json, not the plugin source or installed cache.
- An unconfigured directory returns configured: false with the global settings only.
- There is no folder trust classification; reading status creates no state and starts nothing.

 Snapshot content

| Field                            | Content                                                                                                                                            |
| -------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| configuration, toolchain     | Project/environment identity and the toolchain lock digest                                                                                         |
| sqlcl, connections           | Saved SQLcl execution mode, MCP restrict level, database transport and the plugin-level connection references (no secrets)                         |
| preferences                    | browserMode: host\|codex for [browser verification](testing.md)                                                                                  |
| changes                        | git status --porcelain of the project, at most 80 entries; unavailable when Git is absent                                                      |
| sync                           | Local working-copy sync state per environment; server freshness is not-checked                                                                   |
| jobs, deployments, history | The 12 newest job and deployment records with status, phase, diagnostics and artifacts, and how many older records were omitted                    |
| permissions.activeGrants       | Unexpired local deployment grants for this project (operations, expiry, exact-plan flag); grants recorded by ship are removed after each attempt |

Details of the snapshot:

- Job and deployment history considers the newest 2000 records of each kind.
- Records over 2 MB or unreadable records are listed as unavailable so one broken record never hides the rest.
- Secrets are redacted from every field.
- A snapshot larger than the inline MCP limit is archived like any other result and readable through apexrest_artifact_read.
- The verification browser preference is read from .apexrest/panel/preferences.json ({"browserMode":"codex"} by default; codex is the legacy alias of host). Unknown keys in that file are ignored.

 Job status and phase

- Actual job failure remains failure after normal process exit: a job's reported status is the operation's own failed, outcome_unknown or cancelled outcome.
- A job whose worker never started is failed, not unknown, and needs a new job after its diagnostic is resolved.
- A lost heartbeat or mutation response can leave outcome_unknown; reconcile before retrying.
- Running jobs carry a phase (validating, planning, backing_up, migrating, importing, verifying, syncing) that is informative only.

 What the snapshot cannot do

The snapshot does not call Oracle, read the SQLcl connection store or verify target identity.

It cannot change settings, queue jobs, cancel jobs, grant authorization, or apply a plan. Use the explicit operations instead:

- apexrest sqlcl configure
- apexrest_project (connection_add)
- apexrest_apex_validate
- apexrest_ship
- apexrest_job (cancel)
- [apexrest_browser_open](testing.md)

Imports use the [deployment workflow](deployment-safety.md).

title: Supported versions
text:
Supported versions and verification

This page lists the versions and platforms the current source supports, and states what the local checks do and do not establish. Read it before you choose a toolchain or rely on a support claim.

 Supported versions

| Component         | Current source support                                                   |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Node.js           | 24–26; Node 24 LTS recommended                                           |
| Java              | 21, matching the selected SQLcl profile                                  |
| Oracle APEX       | 26.1 full imports; 26.2 full/eligible partial imports                    |
| SQLcl             | Pinned 26.1 and 26.2 profiles in toolchains/                           |
| Partial imports   | APEX 26.2, SQLcl 26.3.0.260.1620, MMD 26.2.0+3479, direct SQLcl CLI  |
| Hosts             | Codex desktop/CLI and Claude Code plugin manifests                       |
| Operating systems | macOS, Linux and Windows installer paths; WSL2 is a separate environment |

 What APEXREST provides

- The host owns model execution, context and permissions.
- APEXREST provides deterministic references, validation, planning, imports, browser handoff, jobs and status.
- It does not provision a database or manage an Oracle sandbox.

 Verification scope

- Local unit, contract, installer and package checks establish source/fixture behavior.
- Fresh native host discovery, connected Oracle imports and authenticated application/browser checks require their own authorized runs on each target/platform.
- Production deployment and restore are forbidden on every platform.
- Exact vendor artifacts and hashes are pinned in the packaged toolchain locks.
- New SQLcl builds and transport modes require qualification before extending support claims.

 Related

Read [implementation status](../../docs/implementation-status.md), [testing](../../docs/testing.md) and [next actions](../../docs/next-actions.md).

title: Architecture
text:
Architecture

This page explains how APEXREST is built: its packages, how a request runs, how SQLcl is kept alive, and where the Oracle, deployment and trust boundaries lie. It is for contributors and for anyone who needs to know why the plugin behaves as it does.

APEXREST is one policy-aware core behind three surfaces: a stdio MCP server for Codex and Claude Code, the apexrest CLI and six skills that tell the host agent how to use them. Twelve MCP tools expose bounded operations; the CLI keeps granular commands. Both surfaces validate inputs against the same strict Zod schemas in packages/core/src/operations.ts.

![APEXREST architecture from the agent through source, deployment planning, Oracle and verification.](assets/overview.svg)

 On this page

| Section                                             | What it explains                                                     |
| --------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [Surfaces and transports](surfaces-and-transports) | Where work runs and how the core reaches Oracle                      |
| [Components](components)                           | The packages and what each one is responsible for                    |
| [Request lifecycle](request-lifecycle)             | Short operations, jobs, detached workers and unknown outcomes        |
| [Persistent SQLcl engine](persistent-sqlcl-engine) | How SQLcl sessions are kept, shared, isolated and closed             |
| [Oracle boundary](oracle-boundary)                 | What real Oracle tooling does and what local data does               |
| [Deployment boundary](deployment-boundary)         | Plans, import modes, partial imports, apply, backups and recovery    |
| [Source revisions](source-revisions)               | One source identity for edit, preview, compiler and deployment       |
| [Trust and data handling](trust-and-data-handling) | What counts as executable input, what counts as data, and the limits |

 Surfaces and transports

- Where work runs. Implementation runs in the user's open conversation. See [host integration](codex-integration.md) for ownership and host boundaries.
- Component selection. apexrest_reference mode:select and docs select add advisory component selection before composition.
  - A compatible local shortlist feeds one optional OpenAI Decisions request when explicitly enabled in the project.
  - API failures return the local shortlist; search/read remain offline.
  - The host model owns final APEXlang authoring.
  - See [selection configuration and data flow](component-catalog.mdoptional-openai-decisions-selection).
- Oracle access. Oracle operations use SQLcl in one of two modes, over one of two transports. See [configuration](configuration.md) and [SQL through ORDS](ords.md).

| Setting   | Value    | Meaning                                                                 |
| --------- | -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Mode      | cli    | SQLcl runs as a subprocess.                                             |
| Mode      | mcp    | The official SQLcl stdio server, distinct from the APEXREST MCP server. |
| Transport | direct | The Oracle listener.                                                    |
| Transport | ords   | SQL over HTTP(S) through ORDS.                                          |

 Components

| Component                                 | Responsibility                                                                                                                                       |
| ----------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| plugins/apexrest-apex/skills/           | apexrest-work (the end-to-end cycle), apexrest-apexlang, apexrest-safety, apexrest-setup, apexrest-pattern-catalog, apexrest-oracle-sync |
| packages/mcp/                           | Stdio MCP catalog, structured output, in-process and detached job dispatch                                                                           |
| packages/cli/                           | CLI parsing and JSON output, backed by the same operation schemas                                                                                    |
| packages/core/                          | Configuration, connections, references, SQLcl sessions, deployment policy, browser handoff, jobs, artifacts and the status snapshot                  |
| packages/core/src/preview/              | Database-free [local preview](local-preview.md): APEXlang parser, theme export evaluation, renderer, SQLite shims, HTTP server and feature modules   |
| packages/installer/                     | Reviewed downloads, safe extraction, managed runtimes and Codex registration                                                                         |
| resources/, templates/, toolchains/ | Pinned references, component and pattern catalogs, project starters and toolchain definitions                                                        |

 How the plugin bundle is built

plugins/metadata.json drives the build in scripts/build-plugin.mjs. The build:

- writes the Codex manifest (.codex-plugin/plugin.json, .mcp.json), the Claude Code manifest (.claude-plugin/plugin.json) and both marketplace files;
- shares ESM runtime chunks;
- copies skills, reference fragments, schemas, templates and locks into one self-contained bundle.

npm run plugin:sync refreshes the checked-in copy under plugins/apexrest-apex and the repository marketplaces. MCP startup performs no dependency downloads and needs no extra global MCP registration.

 Request lifecycle

There are two kinds of operation:

- Short operations return one structured result (ok, status, runId, diagnostics, artifacts, nextActions, data).
- Long operations are jobs with a durable state.json, heartbeat and phase.

Where a long operation runs depends on the tool:

| Tools                                                                                                                       | Where they run                                                                                                                |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| apexrest_apex_validate, apexrest_reference, apexrest_metadata_read, apexrest_ship mode:plan, apexrest_apex_sync | Inside the MCP server process, reusing one OracleAdapter per managed-home settings digest.                                  |
| apexrest_ship mode:apply                                                                                                | Validates and plans in-process, then runs the apply phase in a detached worker so a database write survives host termination. |

The apexrest_ship mode:apply call waits up to waitSeconds (default 25, maximum 120; 25 and 30 for other long tools) and otherwise returns the jobId.

 Jobs, timeouts and unknown outcomes

- apexrest_job reads or cancels an existing job; the agent never restarts an operation to fetch its result.
- A lost heartbeat or an interruption during a write produces outcome_unknown, which never implies a rollback.
- Workers have a 15-minute deadline.
- SQLcl has separate process timeouts and classified diagnostics, including commands that print an error despite exit code zero.

 Development broker

apexrest dev start --project PATH starts one long-lived process for the project, dev status shows it with its running and waiting jobs, and dev stop stops it after its running jobs finish.

- What it runs. It runs the same durable job records as a detached worker, in a warm process, and its pooled read sessions survive between jobs. Plans, grants, backups, drift checks, the deployment lease and unknown-outcome handling are unchanged. Database write sessions keep their isolation per operation.
- Endpoint. It listens on a private OS-local endpoint, a Unix socket or named pipe, and accepts only requests carrying the token in its 0600 record under .apexrest/broker/. It exits after APEXREST_BROKER_IDLE_MINUTES (default 30) idle minutes.
- No double runs. Every runner claims a job exclusively (claim.json) before it runs. When a starter cannot confirm the broker took a job, it starts a detached worker as before; the job still runs once. A starter never marks a claimed job failed: its heartbeat decides the outcome.
- One apply per environment. ship.apply jobs of one environment run one at a time. When several are waiting and the newest plan is at least as recent as the others, only the newest runs and the others are recorded superseded, naming the job that applies their changes. A running import is never cancelled or changed.
- Unknown outcomes. A run with an unknown outcome keeps its deployment lease, so later writes to the same schema stay blocked (TARGET_LOCKED) until it is reconciled.

 Persistent SQLcl engine

SQLcl executes a piped script only after stdin EOF, so a long-lived engine uses SQLcl's own server mode (sql -mcp).

 Session pool

packages/core/src/sqlcl-session.ts keeps one server process per key for the lifetime of the MCP server process. The key is: executable, Java home, server arguments, connection name, working directory.

- Commands on one session are serialized.
- A key opens at most a configured number of sessions (two for /nolog work, one per saved connection) and queues the rest.
- A timed-out, cancelled, truncated or failed command kills its session.
- Idle sessions are unref'd, reaped after ten minutes and killed at exit, so a one-shot CLI call still exits naturally.

 What is pooled and what is isolated

| Work                                      | Process model                                                               |
| ----------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Offline validation and help in cli mode | Pooled.                                                                     |
| 26.1 generation                           | Keeps its established pooling behavior.                                     |
| 26.3 generation                           | A disposable process, to avoid the verified compiler-state leak.            |
| Connected sessions                        | One process per call (saved -name connections and ORDS connect -orest). |
| Connected batches in mcp mode           | Isolated in fresh servers.                                                  |

Two exceptions apply to deployment planning and apply on a saved connection in cli mode:

- Operation read scope (sqlcl-read-scope.ts). The read-only batches of one plan or one apply (identity, versions, metadata, exports) share one connected server.
  - Each observation is still a new query at the moment it is requested.
  - Every batch starts with ROLLBACK, a package-state reset and the session user's schema.
  - The server belongs to that operation only and closes with it; a failed batch closes it at once.
  - Writes and restricted scripts never run on it.
  - APEXREST_CONNECTED_READS=0 restores one process per read.
- Prepared import server (sqlcl-warm.ts). A full or selected-file APEXlang import runs on a server started at the beginning of apply with the same restriction level as the import process (-R 2 -mcp).
  - It loads the compiler with an offline apex validate while the target is observed and backed up.
  - It runs the one import with the import process's fail-stop preamble, an explicit COMMIT and the completion marker, and is closed.
  - Each start proves that the SQLcl build refuses HOST in server mode. When that proof, the warm-up or the connection fails, nothing has been submitted and the ordinary import process runs.
  - A selected-file import names its files relative to SQLcl's working directory, so its server starts in the run's frozen source directory, which is created empty and then filled in place.
  - SQL restores, database scripts, ORDS and mcp mode keep the import process.
  - APEXREST_WARM_IMPORT=0 disables it.
  - Its JVM starts while the target is observed, so it costs no time on the critical path (spawn 0 ms measured locally). It is not kept across imports: a server stays bound to one frozen import directory.
- Database scripts of one apply (sqlcl-warm.ts ScriptSession). When an apply has more than one migration or package script, they share one restricted server (-R 2 -mcp) on the saved direct connection.
  - Every start proves the HOST refusal before it connects.
  - Each script runs with the fail-stop preamble, an explicit COMMIT (as the process's final EXIT did) and its completion marker. History is recorded only after the marker.
  - After each script the session is reset: ROLLBACK, package-state reinitialization, current_schema set to the session user.
  - A script without its marker discards the server and is classified exactly like an interrupted process (OUTCOME_UNKNOWN, no replay). So does a transport failure, a cancellation or a failed reset. (In server mode an error drops the connection but leaves SQLcl running.)
  - Nothing submitted yet means the script runs in its own process. ORDS, mcp mode and single scripts keep one process per script.
  - APEXREST_SCRIPT_SESSION=0 disables it. Qualified with scripts/bench/session-reuse.mjs on SQLcl 26.3 and Oracle 23.26.4.

 Capability probe and diagnostics

- The capability probe (help apex, compiler version) runs once per SQLcl installation per process and is invalidated when the installation changes.
- Its answer is also kept for one day in $APEXREST_HOME/cache/sqlcl-capabilities/, keyed by the same installation marks, so a deployment worker does not start two JVMs for it. help apex import (selected-file support) is kept the same way. APEXREST_CAPABILITY_CACHE=0 disables the files.
- Compiler preload (MCP server). After the first successful tool call that names a project, the server validates that project's sources offline in the background on the pooled server, so the first real validation does not wait for a cold compiler. The result is discarded; validate, ship and preview calls wait for a running preload. Once per project per process; APEXREST_PREWARM=0 disables it.
- Connected timing requires separate qualification.
- Compiler output is parsed into structured diagnostics (file, line, column, type, message, validValues, hint).

 Environment switches

| Variable                      | Effect                               |
| ----------------------------- | ------------------------------------ |
| APEXREST_CONNECTED_READS=0  | Restores one process per read.       |
| APEXREST_WARM_IMPORT=0      | Disables the prepared import server. |
| APEXREST_CAPABILITY_CACHE=0 | Disables the capability cache files. |
| APEXREST_PREWARM=0          | Disables the compiler preload.       |

 Oracle boundary

- Application generation, export, validation and import use real Oracle SQLcl.
- APEXlang source is validated on a staging copy, preserving the working tree and Oracle .apex metadata.
- Reviewed version-aware references, the component catalog and the pattern catalog are local indexed data.
- Upstream router instructions and arbitrary scripts are not installed as agent authority.

The adapter:

- combines target identity fields in one fresh query;
- never caches live target state;
- overlaps independent compilation and read-only target work during planning.

All preflight tasks settle before an error is returned or a write begins.

 Deployment boundary

 Plans and import modes

A plan binds source, configuration, compiler/toolchain, target identity, target content and migration history and expires after 30 minutes. Both apexrest_ship and granular CLI planning accept importMode: auto|files|full|none (--import-mode in the CLI).

| importMode | Behavior                                                                                                   |
| ------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| auto       | Selects eligible 26.2 changed files or records full-import reasons.                                        |
| files      | Binds explicit application-relative paths without expansion or full fallback.                              |
| full       | Forces a complete application import.                                                                      |
| none       | A database-only plan: pending migrations and changed package scripts, no backup and no application import. |

- For none, identity, drift, history, lease and confirmation checks are unchanged.
- Applied migrations and package scripts unchanged since their last successful run (recorded in the local deployment-control store) are not executed again and add no database risk to a plan.
- The preview exposes requested/resolved mode, selected files, selected shared-component dependencies and reasons.
- APEX 26.1 uses full imports.

 Partial import requirements and scope

Partial planning requires all of the following:

- an existing dev/test application and trusted sync checkpoint;
- the reviewed APEX 26.2 / SQLcl 26.3.0.260.1620 / MMD 26.2.0+3479 profile;
- direct SQLcl CLI transport.

How the scope is chosen and bounded:

- The agent chooses automatic, exact-files or full mode from the intended change.
- Native page selectors export only selected pages.
- Shared-component file imports explicitly bind full APEXlang observation where native component export is unavailable; only selected files enter conflict checks, backups and readback comparison.
- Unsupported import families and global changes require a full import.
- Explicit selection never silently widens, and a conflict never causes fallback.

 How a partial plan is computed

partial-import.ts compares the saved baseline, local intent and freshly selected server content.

- It stages selected local files over retained dependency context and compiles that whole effective tree once.
- A local no-op makes no Oracle call.
- Identity/version queries are batched; identical read/deploy connections reuse the fresh identity result.
- Import-help capability checks share an installation-bound cache.

 Apply

1. Apply acquires local schema ownership before checking live drift.
2. The fresh pre-apply APEXlang export supplies the scoped backup.
3. Frozen sources reach one apex import -files call.
4. Selected readback records exact hashes, qualified normalization and verified scope; unselected server content is not claimed as freshly verified.
5. The checkpoint retains dependency context and verified selected sources, preserving unselected local work.

A separate full import observes the full server inventory and refuses to overwrite unreconciled remote edits. Independent homes/machines require external serialization.

 Backups, restore and recovery

- New backups use APEXlang, including full initial sync snapshots; ordinary flows do not create SQL application dumps.
- Selected restore uses a separate exact plan and the same scope.
- Creation backups record absence and do not masquerade as a deletion rollback.
- Explicit old SQL backups remain restore-compatible.
- Recovery reads original scope before resolving unknown outcomes.
- Exact-plan grants, identity, compiler, backup integrity and production refusal remain mandatory.

See [partial-import safeguards](deployment-safety.mdapex-262-partial-imports).

 Source revisions

A source revision is the digest of the canonical source inventory: the application folder, migrations, package scripts and the package manifests. It is the same value as a deployment plan's sourceDigest. A compiler result, a plan and a deployment therefore name the same thing, and apply refuses a plan whose revision no longer matches the sources (SOURCE_DRIFT). The configuration digest is bound beside it, as plans already do.

revision.ts records outcomes in <project>/.apexrest/revisions.json, each with the revision it was produced for:

| State               | Written when                                                                                                      |
| ------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| validated           | apex validate on the project application, and the full-plan compiler run, succeed.                              |
| importing (per env) | An apply starts its first database write.                                                                         |
| deployed (per env)  | An apply succeeds: import and readback are confirmed.                                                             |
| failed (per env)    | An apply fails. An unknown outcome writes nothing, so the import stays visible and the last deployment unchanged. |

An outcome replaces the recorded one only when its work started at or after the recorded work, so a late result is kept with its own revision and never marks a newer one. status reports the latest local revision and each state separately, marking a state current only when it is for the latest local revision.

sourceChange() compares two inventories. It lists the exact changed, added and removed files and the affected page ids; the scope is unknown when the global page, a shared component, the application or a database script changed. The compiler stages its own copy of the application and refuses a change while staging, so a validation result always belongs to the revision observed before staging.

A connected Composer plan reads dictionary metadata once per plan. Duplicate requests are removed, and up to eight requests share one target-verified round trip. Metadata is not cached across plans. The plan has no cheap signal of target DDL changes, and a cached snapshot is never evidence of fresh target state.

 Edit-to-deploy paths and clocks

| Path                    | Entry point                                                                             | Clock (start → end)                                    |
| ----------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| Scaffold / Composer     | project action:scaffold, compose.plan/materialize                                 | spec accepted → source written                         |
| Source edits            | the agent edits .apx files (no semantic edit service yet)                             | edit accepted → revision changed                       |
| Preview refresh         | preview/server.ts signature check per request and live.ts watcher (150 ms debounce) | file written → server returns the new HTML (not paint) |
| Compiler validation     | apex validate, the full-plan compile in deploy.ts                                   | staged snapshot → compiler result for that revision    |
| Plan / apply / readback | ship → deploy.ts plan and apply journal (approved … succeeded)                  | apply started → import and readback confirmed          |
| Browser verification    | only on request                                                                         | requested check → behavior observed                    |

scripts/benchmark-fast-dev.mjs measures these clocks on a temporary copy of a project; see [testing](testing.mdfast-development-clocks). The engineering targets are: a supported semantic property edit at p95 ≤ 250 ms; a warm local preview update at a median ≤ 1 s and p95 ≤ 2 s; a ready recipe to preview in about 1–3 s; a small native selected-page update investigated against a 2–5 s median stretch target. They are targets, not results.

 Trust and data handling

 Executable input and data

- Project SQL and APEXlang are executable inputs.
- No manual folder trust list is required; host filesystem permissions govern project access.
- Database descriptions, source comments, reference content and operation output are data, not instructions to expand permissions.
- Credentials stay in SQLcl's store, the private ORDS credential file; browser authentication belongs to the host.

 Filesystem, state and artifacts

- Filesystem operations reject traversal, symlinks and special files where the policy requires contained files.
- State uses atomic writes and exclusive ownership; subprocesses execute without a shell.
- Artifact readers expose bounded registered text and apply redaction.

These controls do not replace the host's permission boundary or production deployment refusal. See [security](../SECURITY.md).

 Oracle source contracts

Complete release-specific Oracle source contracts and maintainer synchronization are described in [Oracle APEXlang coverage](oracle-apexlang-coverage.md). Full documents are lazy-loaded and checksum-verified; summary indexes are routing data.

 Related

- [Host integration](codex-integration.md): manifests, ownership and host boundaries.
- [Programmatic automation](codex-automation.md): what each tool executes without a model.
- [Deployment safety](deployment-safety.md): the plan, grant, import and recovery model.
- [Configuration](configuration.md) and [SQL through ORDS](ords.md): modes, transports and connections.

title: Oracle APEXlang coverage
text:
Official Oracle APEXlang coverage

APEXREST includes every official APEX 26.2 inventory definition, with byte-exact paginated retrieval. This page records which Oracle sources are pinned, what was measured and what the inventory does not prove. It is for maintainers and for anyone who needs to judge a coverage claim.

- This establishes source-library completeness against an explicit upstream directory, not universal Oracle APEX platform support or deployed application qualification.
- Checked on 22 November 2026 against the official sources below.
- To look up a definition, go to [Read the inventory](read-the-inventory).

 Source and version matrix

| Layer                                | Exact source/version                                                                            | Current coverage and meaning                                                                                                                                         |
| ------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Oracle skills repository HEAD        | a1b574010841e9141dfeaa210d97c0f2cad5bf8d, 18 November 2026 13:14:12 UTC                       | Latest inspected commit (“APEXlang skill Nov 2026”, PR 141); flat skill layout; this is the reviewed 26.2 pin                                                       |
| Bundled Oracle 26.2 inventory        | Same a1b5740…; ZIP SHA-256 c8f869c5f0c30136fc7a998a6de7beeea81ec86dd2827f45c3115a247ca73de3 | 389/389 definition documents, 130 distinct declaration keywords, 32,187 document/group/property occurrences                                                          |
| Bundled Oracle 26.1 grammar/examples | b94ccf4dec34b27859c2378fa71ba2bad884f2fe, 22 September 2026 00:21:44 UTC                      | Pinned; Oracle no longer publishes the 26.1 generation skill (removed in November 2026); 5,530 reference records: 658 complete documents and 4,872 grammar fragments |
| Local component UX catalog           | 26.1@4a1e7d0265bb, Universal Theme 26.1 Reference/APEX 26.1.4                                 | 617 records; 270 recipes, 269 compiler-ready; independent 26.1 evidence                                                                                              |
| Local pattern UX catalog             | 26.1@d92b2cf4623f                                                                             | 406 records; 58 patterns and 84 recipes, 69 compiler-ready; 15 unresolved recipes and nine unresolved patterns                                                       |
| Installed offline compiler inspected | SQLcl 26.3.0.260.1620, actual MMD 26.2.0+3479                                               | Oracle compiler validation of the six local 26.2 recipes passed; no database, import or browser execution                                                            |

 Provenance

Primary provenance: [pinned revision](https://github.com/oracle/skills/commit/a1b574010841e9141dfeaa210d97c0f2cad5bf8d), [official 26.2 inventory](https://github.com/oracle/skills/tree/a1b574010841e9141dfeaa210d97c0f2cad5bf8d/apex/apexlang-26-2-inventory), [26.1 source pin](https://github.com/oracle/skills/commit/b94ccf4dec34b27859c2378fa71ba2bad884f2fe). Oracle publishes this material as repository commits; a date or Git commit is not an Oracle semantic release number.

 Official skills review

On 18 November 2026 Oracle reorganized the skills (PR 141):

- Layout. Skills moved from apex/apexlang/<version>/… to flat names under apex/: apexlang-26-2-inventory, apexlang-26-2-example-applications, the shared apexlang-compile and apexlang-deploy, and the [router](https://github.com/oracle/skills/blob/a1b574010841e9141dfeaa210d97c0f2cad5bf8d/apex/apexlang-router/SKILL.md). The maintainer scripts read both layouts.
- Router. It defaults to 26.2 when the release cannot be determined, and it refuses to substitute another release's skills.
- 26.1 generation. The skill is no longer published; the bundled 26.1 corpus stays pinned.
- 26.2 inventory. 234 of 389 documents changed:
  - property conditions are deduplicated and grouped, which shrinks the inventory from 16.9 MB to 7.3 MB;
  - 113 documents also add or reorder properties, for example the Show AI Assistant useResponse group and Alert and Confirm display options.
- Examples and catalog. Two 26.2 example files and the inventory catalog changed. No document was added or removed, and the license is unchanged.

The [maintainer skill map](../plugins/apexrest-apex/skills/apexrest-oracle-sync/references/oracle-skills.md) routes these official skills through APEXREST's validation and authorized deployment flow. Inventory checks and instruction checks remain separate.

 Release upgrades

The project skills now route release upgrades to oracle:26.2:guide/upgrade-audit. This local guide follows Oracle's [source-upgrade procedure](https://docs.oracle.com/en/database/oracle/apex/26.2/apxdc/upgrading-apexlang-source-with-new-apex-release.html):

1. Protect local/server changes.
2. Use an authorized full import.
3. Re-export in disposable staging.
4. Review deletions and metadata.
5. Isolate structural changes from feature edits.

 Checks on 22 November 2026

- The upstream check found the new pin and no unbundled release.
- The build reproduced the previous pin byte for byte before the update, then imported the new one; --check passes.
- Packaged MCP retrieval passed all 389 definitions and 1,106 paginated reads, with ordinary discovery queries and an empty unrelated query.
- Repository unit, contract and packaging tests passed.

Not checked: connected Oracle, recipe compilation, application/browser execution and fresh native-host loading.

 Complete inventory denominator

The denominator is every Markdown definition under apex/apexlang-26-2-inventory/assets/ at the pinned revision. The separate upstream inventory SKILL.md is retained as a reference catalog for syntax, application layout and containment; it is vendor data, not executable host policy.

 What the inventory holds

- The inventory includes workspace components, applications and shared components, page components, native plugin variants and template-component variants.
- Every document retains its original component keyword, parents/children, grouped properties, types, enums, defaults, requiredness, applicability and explanatory text.
- Repeated declarations or properties under different variants remain separate contexts.

 Storage and search integrity

- The source contains 7,311,610 inventory bytes.
- The largest definition, app/page/region/region.md, is 144,109 bytes; definitions of this size exceed the former inline entry limit.
- Definitions are therefore stored as individual files, checksum-verified when read and paginated through the actual apexrest_reference operation.
- The compact search index is only a routing summary and does not replace a contract.
- Search postings cover full document text and their own SHA-256 is bound in the snapshot.
- Missing or mismatched accelerators are rebuilt from complete integrity-verified documents.
- Accelerator changes invalidate cached search results; they cannot silently turn ordinary component/property queries into successful empty results.
- Legacy inline corpora derive postings directly when no independent accelerator digest exists.

 The 26.2 corpus

The former 26.2 source bundle selected only 27 inventory documents and omitted property groups from some of them. That selection has been replaced completely. There is one official authority for 26.2 property definitions; local guides and recipes are explicitly separate.

The resulting 26.2 corpus has 412 records:

| Records | Kind                              |
| ------: | --------------------------------- |
|     389 | Complete definitions              |
|       1 | Inventory catalog                 |
|       9 | Selected source examples          |
|       7 | Local guides                      |
|       6 | Original compiler-checked recipes |

 Read the inventory

Use these MCP arguments:

json
{ "mode": "read", "id": "oracle:26.2:inventory-catalog", "version": "26.2" }


json
{ "mode": "search", "corpus": "components", "version": "26.2", "query": "interactive grid", "limit": 3 }


Read the returned oracle:26.2:inventory/... ID and follow nextOffset until it is null. Related variant contracts link to their owning selector/component.

Redaction:

- Official definitions containing public password or authorization property/enum syntax retain those exact bytes; integrity-verified vendor pages alone bypass operation-output secret heuristics.
- Connection data, environment output, diagnostics and objects merely labeled as vendor data retain normal redaction.

Version rules:

- The default/project-absent profile remains 26.1.
- Local component: recipes and pattern: compositions remain bound to their independently verified 26.1 source. They do not silently become 26.2 contracts.
- An empty search is not proof that a platform feature is absent.

 Inventory, compiler and platform are different scopes

| Scope                                                      | Measured coverage                                                                                                                                                                                | Limit                                                                                                                  |
| ---------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Official inventory definition bytes                        | 389/389 included and available through MCP                                                                                                                                                       | Specific upstream revision and directory                                                                               |
| Inventory declaration keywords                             | 130 distinct componentType values                                                                                                                                                              | Multiple documents may describe one keyword with different variants                                                    |
| Inventory property occurrences                             | 32,187 document/group/name addresses                                                                                                                                                             | Includes repeated variant contexts; not 32,187 unique API features                                                     |
| Inspected compiler MMD                                     | 222 component definition IDs; 136 distinct keywords; 2,561 global property definitions, 2,528 referenced global IDs; 6,071 component/property bindings; 314 groups; 97 property types; 32 events | Separate compiler structure; these counts are not interchangeable with Markdown occurrences                            |
| Compiler-only keyword differences                          | attributes, chart, dataProfile, groupBy, pivot, printAttributes lack a separate inventory declaration document                                                                       | Some are represented within parent definitions; this does not prove missing runtime support                            |
| Local 26.2 recipes                                         | Six files plus generated scaffold compile against actual MMD 26.2.0+3479                                                                                                                       | Queries/provider calls/security enforcement/import/browser behavior require separate checks                            |
| Theme/component/plugin installation and Builder operations | Outside a complete-inventory claim                                                                                                                                                               | Actual plugins, themes, templates, workspace provisioning, privileges and dependencies need target evidence            |
| Business data, SQL/PLSQL runtime, APIs and administration  | Outside a complete-inventory claim                                                                                                                                                               | Tables, DML, grants, network/OCI/provider configuration, execution semantics and runtime authorization are independent |
| Target deployment and user experience                      | Unverified by this inventory change                                                                                                                                                              | Authorized import and authenticated browser observations remain separate outcomes                                      |

Compiler build:

- The installed compiler has resource directory labels including 26.2.0-11+3480; its inspected metadata content and default compiler MMD identify 26.2.0+3479.
- A containing directory name must not be used as the actual source schema build.
- Source metadata stays intact.
- The compiler is Oracle SQLcl, not an independent implementation bundled by the upstream skills.

Upstream skills and examples:

- Oracle's 26.2 repository has compile, deploy, inventory and example-application skills. Generation guidance remains in the 26.1 generation tree.
- The three upstream 26.2 example applications contain 257 source files; APEXREST imports nine selected examples, not all three applications.
- Upstream executable helpers are not copied or run as plugin policy.

 Current Oracle release context

- [Oracle announced APEX 26.2 on 6 October 2026](https://blogs.oracle.com/apex/announcing-oracle-apex-262); availability on a particular cloud/target is a separate fact.
- The [26.2 new-features reference](https://docs.oracle.com/en/database/oracle/apex/26.2/htmrn/new-features.html) describes changes including AI integrations and navigation, workflows, reports, security/data-source options and Universal Theme improvements. Inclusion of an inventory definition does not establish those integrations on an arbitrary target.
- [File-level APEXlang import](https://blogs.oracle.com/apex/introducing-file-level-import-with-apexlang-in-oracle-apex) requires matching 26.2 source/target and SQLcl/ORDS 26.3 prerequisites.
- Oracle documents [deployment-file structure and dependencies](https://docs.oracle.com/en/database/oracle/apex/26.2/apxdc/understanding-apexlang-deployment-files.html) and [source upgrades across releases](https://docs.oracle.com/en/database/oracle/apex/26.2/apxdc/upgrading-apexlang-source-with-new-apex-release.html).
- APEXREST's implemented transport/selection restrictions remain in the [26.2 guide](apex-26.2.md); this library synchronization does not widen them.
- SQLcl version context comes from [Oracle's changelog](https://www.oracle.com/tools/sqlcl/sqlcl-changelog.html).

 Maintenance and verification

Use the bundled [maintainer synchronization skill](../plugins/apexrest-apex/skills/apexrest-oracle-sync/SKILL.md) in the canonical source checkout. It requires no global skill installation or scheduled automation.

 Check upstream

sh
node scripts/check-oracle-apexlang-upstream.mjs


- The checker inspects repository HEAD, not only commits touching 26.2.
- Its ignored docs/evidence/oracle-upstream/upstream.json distinguishes full pinned-inventory differences, imported catalog/example changes, licensing and new official version directories.
- inventory-content-current may coexist with new-release-review-required; it never declares another release supported.
- Other unimported upstream skills/examples remain outside that comparison.

 Refresh the 26.2 source

Review the exact candidate archive/revision/SHA-256. For an authorized 26.2 source refresh:

sh
node scripts/build-apexlang-references-26.2.mjs ARCHIVE.zip --commit COMMIT --archive-sha256 SHA256
node scripts/build-apexlang-references-26.2.mjs ARCHIVE.zip --check
npm run build
node scripts/sync-repository-plugin.mjs
node scripts/verify-oracle-apexlang-coverage.mjs --archive ARCHIVE.zip


- --check is read-only and verifies all generated metadata and document bytes.
- A no-op rebuild must stay clean.
- Exact source and license hashes are retained in the lock/snapshot.
- New releases need an explicit profile/compiler/source review; the checker never automatically upgrades an application.
- Local recipe claims remain bound to their actual verification MMD even if a newly inspected example carries a different MMD.

 What the coverage helper checks

The exhaustive helper checks:

- archive/index/search provenance;
- ordinary component/property discovery (interactive grid, reasoningEffort, workflow);
- valid empty unrelated queries;
- every document, all 130 declaration keywords and all 32,187 property occurrences;
- exact-ID discovery and complete paginated reconstruction through the packaged MCP server.

Its ignored docs/evidence/oracle-inventory-coverage.json is local retrieval evidence.

Regression tests independently cover integrity failure, cross-release routing, public enum preservation, operation/diagnostic secret redaction, empty/incomplete/misrouted/missing accelerator recovery and synthetic future-release/license/catalog detection. Synthetic fixtures are not evidence that Oracle published a future release.

 What a refresh does not do

A source refresh remains distinct from publication, global plugin installation, database changes, provider setup and native host/browser qualification.

 Related

- [Component catalog](component-catalog.md): search and read the inventory with corpus:components.
- [APEX 26.2 partial imports](apex-26.2.md): the implemented transport and selection restrictions.
- [Implementation status](implementation-status.md), [acceptance](acceptance.json) and [next actions](next-actions.md).

title: Composer (experimental)
text:
Composer (experimental CLI)

Composer builds local APEXlang from exact executable blocks and explicit dataset/API contracts. This page is for developers who want to try composing an application from a blueprint with apexrest compose.

 When to use

- You have a blueprint (app.blueprint.yaml) and reviewed dataset/API contracts for your project.
- You want generated source that keeps Oracle .apex metadata, authentication, authorization and unmanaged source intact.
- You work from the CLI. Composer is available through apexrest compose; MCP reference search/read can inspect block and blueprint data.

Composer is experimental. See [Authoring and qualification](authoring-and-qualification) for what still needs work.

 Plan and materialize

1. Find and read the blocks and blueprints you need:

   sh
   apexrest docs search "report dialog" --corpus blocks --limit 3
   apexrest docs read --id block:crud/report-dialog@1.0.0
   apexrest docs read --id blueprint:crm@1.0.0
   

2. Replace fixture objects and authorization declarations with reviewed project contracts.

3. Choose a profile explicitly (see [Profiles](profiles)).

4. Create the plan:

   sh
   apexrest compose plan --blueprint app.blueprint.yaml --out plans/composition.json
   

   - Offline planning is the default. --mode connected --env NAME explicitly reads bounded parsing-schema metadata.
   - Planning compiles a complete staged application with real local SQLcl. It performs no import and no fixture SQL execution.
   - Missing keys, authorization, exact API signatures or supported adapters block planning.

5. Review the plan. Plans bind blueprint, source inventory, state, catalog/generator, configuration and toolchain digests. Review contracts, effects, allocations and preimages before materializing.

6. Materialize the plan:

   sh
   apexrest compose materialize --plan plans/composition.json --expected-digest SHA256
   

7. Materialized source then follows the normal validate/ship cycle.

 Profiles

| Version  | Contract                                                                                                                                                           |
| -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| @1.0.0 | The original blocks and CRM/Service Desk blueprints retain their 26.1 contract.                                                                                    |
| @1.1.0 | profile:apex262-ut262-mmd3479, vendor MMD 26.2.0+3479 and SQLcl build 26.3.0.260.1620. The blueprint files are crm-26.2.yaml and service-desk-26.2.yaml. |

- Composer rejects mismatched compiler builds/MMDs with PROFILE_COMPILER_MISMATCH. The error names:
  - the pinned build and MMD, and the installed ones;
  - the bundled profile and blueprints that match the installed compiler (for example the 26.2 blueprints for SQLcl 26.3.0.260.1620);
  - the pinned SQLcl to select with APEXREST_SQLCL instead.
- The 26.2 adapters emit the exact report type enums and stable numeric process execution mappings.
- Prior 26.1 compiler records do not qualify 26.2 or the current generator.
- No profile selection rewrites Oracle metadata.

 Contracts and security

Input validation. Strict YAML AST/schema validation rejects duplicate keys, aliases, tags, unsafe keys, escaping paths, symlinks and oversized input.

Entities require:

- scalar field types;
- an ordered key;
- explicit row-read authorization.

Connected row predicates may reference unquoted columns verified in the selected Oracle object's dictionary metadata. For source-only work, list any non-projected authorization columns in the authorization contract's predicateColumns. Write authorization expressions can use the supported server session binds and authorization functions.

Write adapters require:

- exact PL/SQL mappings;
- editable fields;
- version checks;
- write authorization;
- errors;
- caller-owned transaction semantics.

The API independently enforces row authorization and expected versions. A successful save returns authoritative key/version before dialog close.

Renderers. Native IR, modal forms, Cards and read views provide six experimental renderers and the CRM/Service Desk blueprints. They are bounded adapters with explicit dependencies.

Trust. Catalog data and previews remain untrusted text; search does not execute HTML, JavaScript or SQL. Bundled origin and package hashes do not establish live runtime qualification.

 Ownership and recovery

| Directory             | Kind    | Holds                                           |
| --------------------- | ------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| .apexrest-composer/ | Tracked | Ownership, locks and immutable generation bases |
| .apexrest/composer/ | Private | Staging, cache, plans, receipts and journals    |

- Merge. Three-way merge compares generated base, local source and new generated source. Overlap, unknown anchors and edited deletion targets block.
- Detach. Detach retains source.
- Removal. Removal deletes only confirmed unchanged owned files. Remaining or unknown consumers prevent cleanup.
- Materialization. Materialization freezes the plan, checks source drift and journals each write under a shared local project lock.
- Interrupted work. Interrupted work needs explicit resume/restore. Unknown concurrent bytes require reconciliation.
- Restore limits. Local restoration never rolls back business data.
- Preserve active bases and unresolved journals.

 Shared enum lists

Writable string fields with a supported literal enum use managed native shared LOVs. Identical ordered values in the same pinned profile share one immutable resource across form instances. Values must be distinct, nonempty literal text; use nullable for nullability. The shared adapter does not support markup, APEX substitutions or implicit defaults. Native entry nodes preserve punctuation, quotes and Unicode without a delimiter-based STATIC: encoding.

Existing numeric, temporal and otherwise valid string enumerations outside that adapter retain their text fields and server validation; the plan explains the shared-LOV limit. Empty, duplicate or explicitly empty-array enum declarations are rejected because they cannot establish the intended Oracle membership check.

APEX 26.1 keeps owned LOV declarations inside the native shared-components/lovs.apx container and preserves unrelated declarations and surrounding bytes. APEX 26.2 uses individual files. Resource state is optional, so reading historical state, saved plans and journals does not insert defaults or change their digests. Composer refuses unmanaged alias/name/path collisions and edits to an owned definition.

Changing values allocates another resource. Retired resources remain tracked and unchanged for detached or unknown consumers, with an explicit diagnostic. Automatic resource deletion and adoption are unsupported; at most 512 resources may be tracked within the existing document limits. Review any cleanup separately and preserve active ownership and recovery records.

 Authoring and qualification

To author a block package:

1. Use npm run composer:author for a contained source package, explicit license and reviewed ID/version. Capture produces declaration facts, not runtime equivalence.
2. Local packages require an independent tracked content-digest review.
3. Run the catalog/build and real offline compiler checks:

   sh
   npm run composer:catalog
   npm run composer:check
   npm run composer:verify
   

Limits:

- Source-only drafts require explicit --validation source-only and the project setting composer.allowSourceOnly. They remain unqualified.
- Managed string-enum LOV ownership has local preservation, legacy-state and both-profile offline compiler checks. Broader property/fault cases and authenticated Oracle/browser behavior still need qualification.
- Missing required qualification blocks release readiness.

 Related

- [Acceptance matrix](acceptance.json)
- [Testing](testing.md)
- [Next actions](next-actions.md)

title: Host integration
text:
Host integration: Codex and Claude Code

This page describes how APEXREST plugs into Codex and Claude Code: who owns what, which manifest files each host reads, and what an installation does and does not prove. Read it when you install the plugin in both hosts, change the manifests, or need to know where a host's responsibility ends.

APEXREST targets Codex (desktop and CLI) and Claude Code with one bundle: six host-neutral skills and twelve bounded MCP tools served by runtime/mcp.mjs. The host executes the user's task in the open conversation; APEXREST supplies deterministic Oracle/APEX operations through local stdio MCP and the equivalent CLI. Current host qualification requirements are listed in [next actions](next-actions.md).

 Ownership

| Owner    | Owns                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| The host | The conversation, model, permissions, browser controls and any native collaboration.                                                                                                        |
| APEXREST | Project configuration, pinned references and catalogs, Oracle adapters and the pooled SQLcl engine, deployment policy, browser handoff, recoverable jobs and the read-only status snapshot. |

 What APEXREST does not do

- APEXREST does not start host model sessions or maintain a parallel conversation context.
- There is no plugin work-start API, panel application, HTTP server or MCP UI resource.
- Optional project-scoped [Decisions selection](component-catalog.mdoptional-openai-decisions-selection) calls OpenAI to rank catalog candidates; the current host model still builds the final APEXlang.

Request implementation through the [work skill](chat-workflow.md) and use the domain tools when an actual operation is needed.

 Manifests

| Host        | Manifest in the bundle                                     | Marketplace                                         | Install                                                                                          |
| ----------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Codex       | .codex-plugin/plugin.json (apexrest-apex), .mcp.json | .agents/plugins/marketplace.json                  | codex plugin marketplace add apexrest-dev/apexrest; codex plugin add apexrest-apex@apexrest  |
| Claude Code | .claude-plugin/plugin.json (apexrest)                  | .claude-plugin/marketplace.json (repository root) | claude plugin marketplace add apexrest-dev/apexrest; claude plugin install apexrest@apexrest |

 What the two manifests share

- Both manifests point skills at the same ./skills/ directory.
- Both start the same MCP server: Codex with cwd: "." inside the plugin, Claude Code with ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/runtime/mcp.mjs.
- Claude loads the root MCP file first and then its inline entry for the same server name, as specified in the [Claude plugin manifest reference](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-referencemcpservers).
- The Codex manifest's three starter prompts invoke $apexrest-work, $apexrest-setup and $apexrest-safety.

 How the manifests are generated

| Command or script          | What it does                                           |
| -------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| scripts/build-plugin.mjs | Generates all four files from plugins/metadata.json. |
| npm run plugin:sync      | Copies them into the repository.                       |
| npm run plugin:check     | Detects drift.                                         |

 Managed setup and direct source installs

- Managed setup binds both manifests to the same Node executable and APEXREST_HOME, preserving Claude's cache-root expansion.
- Its content-addressed payload contains both marketplaces.
- Setup registers Codex only. Claude registration uses claude plugin marketplace add <managed-marketplace> and claude plugin install apexrest@apexrest.
- Direct source installs inherit APEXREST_HOME from the launching shell. Select the same home when both hosts share connections, toolchains and coordination.

 One application workflow

Both hosts load the same [work skill](../plugins/apexrest-apex/skills/apexrest-work/SKILL.md) and use one apexrest_ship mode:apply call for an ordinary authorized edit.

- The runtime validates, plans, imports and verifies; standalone validate/plan calls serve diagnostics or explicit review.
- Backups use APEXlang.
- Identity, scoped conflicts, coordination, plan expiry and server-first recovery remain host-neutral.
- Browser checks run only when requested.

The import scope depends on what changed:

| Change                           | Import                                                     |
| -------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| Pages                            | Selected imports and selected exports.                     |
| Supported shared-component files | Selected imports with disclosed full APEXlang observation. |
| Other/global changes             | Full imports.                                              |

See [the application workflow](chat-workflow.md).

 The project argument and server lifetime

- Every project-scoped tool takes the absolute project directory as project because the host launches the server from its plugin cache.
- The MCP server pools SQLcl sessions and in-process jobs for its lifetime and shuts them down when the host closes the transport.

 Host boundaries and verification

A listed plugin, a valid manifest or a returned URL is not proof that a host rendered a skill, loaded the tools or showed a page. Browser observations, installed-plugin CLI/stdio checks and live Oracle operations are recorded separately.

 Related

- [Getting started](getting-started.md): install in Codex or Claude Code and connect a target.
- [Architecture](architecture.md): packages, the persistent SQLcl engine, jobs and durable state.
- [Programmatic automation](codex-automation.md): what each tool executes without a model.
- [Next actions](next-actions.md): open host qualification work.

title: Programmatic automation
text:
Programmatic automation for the agent surface

This page lists what each APEXREST tool executes as ordinary program code and what is left to the host model. Read it to understand which steps of a work cycle need no model, how many calls a typical task takes, and how ship records authorization.

The plugin targets Codex (desktop and CLI) and Claude Code with the same skills and the same MCP tools. Its [12 MCP tools](../packages/core/src/operations.ts) execute ordinary program code; mechanical compilation, metadata reads, planning, backups, imports and status need no model. The host model supplies task understanding, source changes and assessment in the current conversation.

 What runs without AI

Names below omit the apexrest_ MCP prefix. Programmatic execution still requires appropriate authorization for writes.

| Tool                   | Programmatic responsibility                                                                                                                                | What the model contributes                                                   |
| ---------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
