| project              | init scaffolds a project and generates the starter application with the Oracle generator; adopt, inspect, connection_add/list/test manage identity | Choose template, alias and target; ask only for missing non-secret values    |
| reference            | Rank, cache, paginate and read pinned Oracle references, component and pattern recipes (offline)                                                           | Select applicable syntax and resolve design choices                          |
| metadata_read        | Validate scope, verify target, execute allowlisted paginated queries                                                                                       | Select objects and interpret their business meaning                          |
| apex_validate        | Run the Oracle compiler in-process on a staging copy and return structured diagnostics[] (code, file, line, column, type, hint, validValues)             | Repair the named file and line                                               |
| ship                 | Validate, resolve auto/files/full import scope, create an immutable plan, record a plan-bound grant, back up, import, verify and remove the grant    | Review selected files, fallback reasons, target and risks; assess completion |
| apex_sync            | Establish and manage an existing application's trusted local checkpoint (init, status, refresh, invalidate)                                                | Select the target and reconcile changes requiring explicit refresh           |
| browser_open         | Resolve the configured URL and browser handoff                                                                                                             | Use the host browser controls and assess visible behavior                    |
| job, artifact_read | Wait with phase reporting, cancel, and read bounded sanitized artifacts                                                                                  | Interpret the result; reconcile an unknown outcome before retrying writes    |
| status               | doctor probes local tools; project aggregates settings, connections, sync, jobs, deployments and grants                                                | Interpret missing prerequisites                                              |

 CLI commands

The CLI keeps its granular commands:

- project init|adopt|inspect
- connection ...
- apex validate|export|sync|diff
- deploy plan|apply|status|restore-plan
- compose ...
- jobs status|cancel
- panel status
- ship and status

Composer and apex export/generate are CLI-only.

 Round trips

A typical work cycle uses the following operations; actual calls depend on the change and required repairs:

| Task                     | Calls                                                                                                                         |
| ------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Edit an existing page    | project inspect → ≤3 reference → edit files → apex_validate (×1–2) → ship plan → ship apply → browser_open = 8–10 |
| Create a new application | project init → ≤3 reference → edit files → apex_validate (×1–2) → ship plan → ship apply → browser_open = 8–10    |

Reference files load on demand. Validation repairs, authorization requirements and browser observations can add steps.

 Implemented reductions

 apex_validate

- Runs in-process (no job, no polling).
- Returns up to 50 structured diagnostics without truncation; a compacted result keeps the first five complete.
- Domain faults carry nextActions (for example VALIDATION_FAILED, SOURCE_DRIFT, DEPLOY_APPROVAL_REQUIRED, PRODUCTION_DEPLOY_DENIED).

 ship

- Folds validate, plan, grant, apply and verify into one call.
- mode:plan runs in-process.
- mode:apply validates and plans in-process, then runs the apply phase in a detached worker so a database write survives host termination, waiting up to waitSeconds (default 25, maximum 120).
- Job status carries phase (validating, planning, backing_up, migrating, importing, verifying).

 apex_sync jobs and sessions

- Jobs for apex_sync run inside the MCP process (same state.json and heartbeat, so job observes them identically).
- They reuse one OracleAdapter per managed-home settings digest, keeping the offline SQLcl JVM pool and capability cache warm.
- Connected sessions are discarded after each batch; no warm connected-session pool is claimed.
- The ship apply phase runs in a detached worker.
- Browser verification uses the host controls after the import.

 metadata_read and project inspect

- metadata_read accepts requests containing 1–8 scoped requests.
- project inspect defaults to detail: "summary".

 Tool annotations

| Annotation                        | Tools                                                                     |
| --------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| destructiveHint                 | Only ship and job.                                                    |
| readOnlyHint / idempotentHint | reference, apex_validate, metadata_read, artifact_read, status. |
| openWorldHint                   | Only tools that can reach the database, a browser or the network.         |

 Partial imports through the agent surface

The source checkout supports [APEX 26.2 partial imports](apex-26.2.md) through the same apexrest_ship MCP tool used by Codex and Claude Code, and through the CLI.

 Requirements

- APEX 26.1 sources use full imports.
- Direct SQLcl CLI transport is required inside the runtime, with the reviewed SQLcl 26.3.0.260.1620 / MMD 26.2.0+3479 tuple and a compatible 26.2 target. This does not prevent the host from calling APEXREST over MCP.

 Procedure

For an existing dev/test application:

1. Initialize a trusted checkpoint with apexrest_apex_sync action: "init".
2. Edit a page and its shared LOV.
3. Pass one of these selections to both the plan and apply calls:

| apexrest_ship inputs                                                                       | Behavior                                                                                                                  |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| importMode: "auto"                                                                         | Default; select eligible local changes or explain why a full plan is needed.                                              |
| importMode: "files", files: ["pages/p00001-home.apx", "shared-components/lovs/status.apx"] | Import only the selected eligible files; retain other local work. Paths are relative to the application source directory. |
| importMode: "full"                                                                         | Plan a complete application import.                                                                                       |
| importMode: "none"                                                                         | Deploy only pending migrations and changed package scripts; the application is not backed up or imported.                 |

 What the model reviews

The model reviews importSelection.requestedMode, resolvedMode, files, dependencies and reasons; the saved plan holds the complete lists if the preview is truncated.

 What the program does

- It compares checkpoint/local/fresh-server inventories, preserves remote-only edits and blocks unequal edits to the same component before fallback.
- It validates the effective tree, so selected pages must have their required components on the server or included explicitly.
- files never adds dependencies or becomes full; observed remote changes must be reconciled before an automatic full fallback.
- Partial apply retains a scoped APEXlang backup and verifies selected sources while leaving unselected local edits dirty.
- Pages use native selected export; shared files disclose full APEXlang observation.

 What a partial import does not establish

- Unselected server freshness is not established by scoped readback.
- Browser verification remains a separate host action.

See [deployment safeguards](deployment-safety.mdapex-262-partial-imports).

 Authorization recorded by ship

An explicit user request to create, update or import an identified development/test application authorizes that import.

- ship apply requires userRequest (the user's literal instruction).
- It records the request in the user policy as a grant bound to the canonical project root, target digest and plan digest, deploy only, expiring with the plan and marked grantedBy: "ship".
- The grant is removed after the attempt whether it succeeded or failed; a removal failure is reported in grant.removed.
- Production targets (kind: production or listed in the administrator-owned production trust file) and plans with unreviewed risks are refused before any grant is written.
- Trust, backup, identity, drift, coordination and unknown-outcome protections are unchanged.

 Related

- [Work in the current session](chat-workflow.md): the application workflow the tools serve.
- [APEX 26.2 partial imports](apex-26.2.md): import only the changed pages and components.
- [Deployment safety](deployment-safety.md): the plan, grant, import and recovery model.
- [Architecture](architecture.md): jobs, the SQLcl engine and durable state.

title: Plugin qualification harness
text:
Plugin quality and performance harness

This page describes the repository tools that qualify the plugin itself: the commands to run, what each measurement means, and which cases are not implemented yet. It is for maintainers who measure the plugin against a private APEX project.

The repository qualification tools exercise the plugin itself. They do not add an application test runner to the shipped plugin.

 Before you start

- Reusable definitions live in [the test catalogs](../tests/plugin-server/README.md).
- Measurements, prepared applications, exports and reports belong in Git-ignored docs/evidence/.
- APEX 26.1 is the default baseline. APEX 26.2 uses a separate catalog, explicit compiler profile and separate reports.
- Build the current runtime before running the tools.
- Prepare a private project with its existing source, lock, environment and saved connection.
- Connection identity and release checks must succeed before connected measurements qualify.

| Section                                                                                             | Use it to                                                      |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [Read-only execution](read-only-execution)                                                         | Run the baseline, quality, benchmark and cost tools            |
| [Timing and response quality](timing-and-response-quality)                                         | Understand how timings, budgets and comparisons are recorded   |
| [Native host usage and tasks](native-host-usage-and-tasks)                                         | Run agent tasks in Codex or Claude Code and read their metrics |
| [Unimplemented prerequisites and case extensions](unimplemented-prerequisites-and-case-extensions) | See which cases are blocked, unexecuted or left to an operator |

 Read-only execution

 ENV input

- ENV input is read as literal data through the existing file-access checks.
- The qualification adapter also accepts the narrow legacy sqlcl:/workspace: colon format; it never executes or expands values.

 APEX 26.1 baseline

sh
npm run build
node scripts/test-plugin-server.mjs --project <private-project> --env test --samples 3
node scripts/test-plugin-quality.mjs --project <private-project> --env test --samples 20 --output docs/evidence/qp-harness/quality-26.1.json
node scripts/benchmark-plugin-261.mjs --project <private-project> --env test --samples 20
node scripts/sqlcl-cost-probe.mjs --project <private-project> --env test --samples 20 --output docs/evidence/qp-harness/cost-26.1.json


 Runner options

- The baseline and quality runners accept --catalog and --profile.
- The quality runner accepts --cases A261-050,A261-052 and --resume.
- Retain the first report separately before replacing failed measurements.
- Successful prior cases remain in a resumed report, which records its previous runtime digest.
- A complete run can fail even when its latency scenarios pass.

 APEX 26.2

sh
node scripts/test-plugin-server.mjs --project <private-26.2-project> --env dev --samples 3 --catalog tests/plugin-server/apex-26.2.extensions.json --profile 26.2 --output docs/evidence/qp-harness/parity-26.2.json
node scripts/test-plugin-quality.mjs --project <private-26.2-project> --env dev --samples 20 --catalog tests/plugin-server/apex-26.2.extensions.json --profile 26.2 --output docs/evidence/qp-harness/quality-26.2.json
node scripts/test-plugin-262.mjs --project <private-26.2-project> --env dev --output docs/evidence/qp-harness/extension-26.2.json
node scripts/sqlcl-cost-probe.mjs --project <private-26.2-project> --env dev --samples 20 --output docs/evidence/qp-harness/cost-26.2.json


- The 26.2 runner checks profile/MMD identity, reference retrieval and two generated starters containing the six bundled 26.2 recipes.
- Offline CodeScan advisories are recorded separately from compiler results.
- The golden list has traceable corpus IDs and file digests, but its feature exclusivity and expected answers still require independent review.
- A failed connection is not evidence of release parity or fast local database access.
- Target mismatch additionally requires a valid 26.1 source/lock supplied with --mismatch-source-project; changing the profile of 26.2 sources only tests compiler refusal.

 Timing and response quality

 Budgets and measurements

- quality-performance.json supplies session and response budgets and historical baselines.
- Measurements preserve measurements[] and checks[], with excluded warm-ups, monotonic wall time and nearest-rank p95.
- CLI/MCP execution alone has no model tokens.
- Response byte overruns are diagnostics, separate from functional assertions; stack traces are flagged.

 SQLcl statement timing

- SQLcl SET TIMING ON measures each existing marked batch query, including JSON serialization.
- The parser accepts a footer adjoining the JSON closing bracket, strips it before parsing and retains all-or-nothing batch behavior.
- Only debugTimings: true exposes statementMs[] and per-operation queue/process intervals.
- Neither SQL, bindings nor usernames belong in those timing records.
- Direct CLI connection setup remains inside the execution interval; connectMs: null is intentional.

 Metadata, concurrency and drift cases

- The metadata matrix measures eight kinds and an all-kinds batch.
- Missing tables/packages gate their scenarios as not_run with objectPrerequisites; an all-kinds batch also remains unexecuted until both fixtures exist.
- Historical empty signature probes do not qualify existing-package signatures.
- The concurrency case uses one MCP client for four metadata requests, one plan and one validation, with correctness checks and recorded queue waits.
- The drift case performs unchanged plans and independent exports into private directories without refreshing the working copy.

 Cost probe and resource observation

- The cost probe uses /nolog, then the saved-connection name on stdin.
- Its three scenario differences include command handling, JVM/server variation and network effects.
- A small negative select increment is measurement noise.
- Vendor refusal text is checked even when SQLcl exits zero.
- Resource observation tracks only descendants of the harness MCP process, never kills user processes, allows bounded shutdown time, and discloses that shared stage-directory counts cannot establish exclusive ownership.

 Historical regression

- Historical regression is true, false or not_comparable.
- A comparison requires matching quality and complete machine, SQLcl and target fingerprints.
- Missing fingerprints do not become an inferred speed improvement.
- Concurrent native sessions, server load and network conditions must be controlled for a qualified comparison.

 Native host usage and tasks

sh
node scripts/run-agent-tasks.mjs --host codex --profile 26.1 --project <private-project> --env test --tasks AGT-001,AGT-004,AGT-007,AGT-008,AGT-011 --repeat 3 --output docs/evidence/agent-tasks/codex-26.1.json
node scripts/run-agent-tasks.mjs --host claude --profile 26.1 --project <private-project> --env test --tasks AGT-001,AGT-004,AGT-007,AGT-008,AGT-011 --repeat 3 --output docs/evidence/agent-tasks/claude-26.1.json


 What the runner does

- The runner verifies CLI versions/help, uses Codex exec or Claude --print, existing login and fresh private project/session copies.
- Claude receives the already installed plugin directory for that invocation; native profile/plugin settings are not changed.
- Installed-cache provenance and the current-build read-only oracle are separate.
- The recorded cache digest alone does not prove the exact active Codex payload.
- Existing model/effort defaults are observed rather than pinned, so timings remain descriptive; mixed observed models cannot qualify a host speed comparison.

 Token usage

| Host   | How usage is read                                                            |
| ------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Codex  | Reads cumulative token_count.                                              |
| Claude | Sums unique assistant message.id records, keeping the last streamed usage. |

- Normalized input includes ordinary input, cache writes and cache reads.
- Reasoning is an output subset only when supplied.
- Sidechain usage is separate.
- --rollout, --transcript and --usage-source select the usage source for the checkpoint and supported harness commands; unknown/missing/stale/reset/cross-session counters remain unavailable.
- Fresh native tasks use whole-session totals with no preceding model turns, not fabricated per-tool billing.

 Transcripts, permissions and secrets

- Transcript metrics read arguments/text only in memory.
- Persisted output contains tool names, categories, counters and safety/permission classifications.
- Only host-native permission events count as permission prompts; permission-like tool-result text is separately counted as permissionTextHints.
- Missing permission records yield null with a reason.
- Host-owned transcripts remain in their normal locations; the harness does not export them.
- Supplied ENV secrets and their JSON-escaped forms are scanned in memory and only occurrence counts are retained.
- Both AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md reference the absolute original ignored regular ENV file; no ENV copy is created.
- Instruction loading is observed from actual native tool calls, and artifact audits remove accidental credential files while persisting only counts.
- Native login tokens are never copied.

 Wall time, pass rate and statistics

- Native wallTimeMs measures CLI execution, excluding postchecks.
- New runs also record verifiedWallTimeMs including postchecks.
- Failed or unsafe runs stay in raw samples and are excluded from success statistics.
- blockedIterations are separate, and passRate uses passed plus failed iterations only.
- A passed/blocked mixture is partial; manual review is excluded from the automatic pass rate.
- Statistics under toolCalls and normalizedTokens are counts despite the shared statistics helper's historical Ms field names.
- Diagnostic tool-call limits do not override an oracle failure.
- Connected-session diagnostic limits are not yet derived from native tool-result transcripts.

 Reanalysis and task oracles

scripts/reanalyze-agent-tasks.mjs recomputes classified metrics and read-only oracles from existing sessions after a scanner fix, retaining the original assessment. It does not rerun models. --env-file may reference the absolute original ignored ENV during isolated reanalysis.

- The shared page oracle rejects fabricated/missing Markdown page rows.
- Dictionary checks associate each column with its type, normalize displayed type precision, accept explicit English/Ukrainian zero-FK wording and check FK endpoints; they do not replace semantic review.
- AGT-004 permits trailing whitespace/newline normalization only in the faulted APX; unrelated sources and binary assets remain byte-exact.
- AGT-007 requires actual APEXREST reference or skill use; independent technical review appears as needs_review in the sample and report manualReview, making the task partial if all automatic checks pass.

 Unimplemented prerequisites and case extensions

 Write cases

- Connected write requests require --allow-app-writes --user-request '<literal human instruction>'.
- These flags are necessary, but the new 26.2 and agent runners still block write cases because exact case-specific setup/readback/reset/audit fixtures are not implemented.
- The existing 26.1 title-import runner retains its narrower prepared-plan workflow; it does not cover those new cases.
- No write case was executed in this qualification work.

 Cases that are unfinished or not run

- Connected P2 pooling/prewarm cases currently implement prerequisite classification only. Their flags-on measurement logic remains unfinished.
- Read-only planning returns inline and exposes no job completion timestamp, so A261-060 records not_run; an apply job is not substituted.
- Expired/tampered-plan negatives are likewise unexecuted because their checks belong to apply.
- Human App Builder edits, restarts, cancellation, scale fixtures and transport comparisons remain operator qualification.
- AGT-012's Composer oracle and the new dashboard scenario require separate implementations.

 Failures stay findings

Keep failures as findings. Current error next-step/parity shortcomings, compiler semantic/line shortcomings, reference retrieval misses, unavailable local Oracle access and native task failures remain verification blockers. See [implementation status](implementation-status.md) and [next actions](next-actions.md).

 Related

- [The test catalogs](../tests/plugin-server/README.md): reusable case definitions.
- [Testing](testing.md): select the checks for a change.
- [Implementation status](implementation-status.md) and [next actions](next-actions.md): verification limits and open qualification work.

title: Releases
text:
Source version 2.9.0

This page summarizes what the current source version provides, how to install or upgrade it, and what its automation does and does not do.

 What this version provides

- The repository plugin provides six skills and twelve composite tools for Codex and Claude Code.
- It supports APEX 26.1 full imports and [APEX 26.2 partial imports](../../docs/apex-26.2.md), release-specific references, source validation and guarded deployment.
- Application verification uses the host in-app browser, separately from compiler and import results.
- The plugin installs no browser and provides no automatic application test suites.

 Install and upgrade

Use the [installation guide](install.md) for the repository bundle.

When you upgrade:

- Working copies are runtime/toolchain bound. Reconcile pending edits and outcomes before refreshing a clean checkpoint and creating new plans.
- Do not edit saved version fields or unknown state to bypass safeguards.

 Automation and verification

- CI runs automatically only on pushes to main.
- Repository release/Oracle integration workflows and publisher configuration are disabled.
- Local build and packaging do not publish or deploy.
- A local fixture pass does not establish Oracle or native-host behavior.

Read [current release notes](../../docs/release-notes.md), [verification status](../../docs/implementation-status.md), [acceptance](../../docs/acceptance.json) and [next actions](../../docs/next-actions.md).

title: Security and privacy
text:
Security and privacy

APEXREST handles executable application source and access to Oracle environments. Use explicit targets, task-scoped authorization and least-privilege connections. The current beta has open verification gates; see [implementation status](https://apexrest-dev.github.io/apexrest/implementation-status/).

 Report a vulnerability

Do not include credentials, cookies, wallets, connection strings with passwords, real customer data or unredacted browser reports in public issues. No verified public security mailbox is configured. Contact the repository owner privately through an already verified channel; do not assume that an unverified email address belongs to the project.

GitHub private vulnerability reporting must be enabled by the owner before it can be offered as a supported reporting channel. For ordinary non-sensitive bugs, use [GitHub issues](https://github.com/apexrest-dev/apexrest/issues).

 Credentials and reports

SQLcl credentials stay in its named connection store. APEXREST connection references contain names rather than passwords. A CLI --password-file must be a regular, non-symlink file readable only by its owner, and ORDS URLs must use HTTPS except on loopback. SQL backups are written owner-only (0600). Browser authentication belongs to the host in-app browser; the plugin captures no saved browser-authentication state.

Reports are bounded and private by default. Public release packages exclude runtime caches, auth state and raw evidence containing local machine paths. Redaction is defense in depth; it cannot identify every business secret. Inspect every artifact before sharing it, including screenshots deliberately captured during authorized UI verification.

Optional decisionApi.enabled permits component selection to send the caller-prepared UI description and bounded public catalog metadata to https://api.openai.com/v1/decisions. It sends no automatic source, conversation-history or database context. API keys are read from the configured process variable or an explicitly configured private ignored ENV file, never persisted by selection or returned in diagnostics. Requests reject redirects, have a deadline and bounded response size, and perform no automatic retries. Ordinary reference search/read and disabled selection make no API calls.

 Project and host trust

Project SQL and APEXlang are executable code. Host filesystem permissions govern project access; no folder trust list is required. Database metadata, comments, references and operation output are not instructions to broaden permissions. Keep the private policy outside the repository.

The local user and host permissions remain authoritative. An identified DEV/QA/TEST application task authorizes its necessary import through an exact-project/target/plan grant. Actual local non-production servers allow task-scoped database changes; dangerous remote changes require exact-plan human confirmation. Production classification in project configuration or production-trust.json always forbids deployment/restore. APEXREST never edits that registry; legacy approval keys do not enable production writes.

 Supply chain

Vendor downloads enforce allowed hosts, HTTPS, pinned hashes, size limits and safe extraction. npm dependencies use the committed lockfile; the plugin installs no browser. The SHA-keyed download cache must be owned by the current user and not group/world writable. Managed tools record an executable and tree digest in runtime.json and are replaced when they no longer match; tools installed by earlier releases receive that record on their first verification, which is trust on first use.

No npm postinstall hook downloads tools. MCP startup performs no dependency downloads. Oracle license acceptance requires its own consent. Review a source checkout and the local package digest before installation; repository installation is not a signed stable-release guarantee.

 Deployment and recovery

Plans bind source, toolchain, target identity and current target state. Apply compares the live target and migration history with the plan and recomputes authentication/authorization risk from a live export. Migrations and package scripts containing SQLcl client commands are blocked. Apply preserves authorization, drift checks, frozen source, a verified SQL backup for an existing app and durable ownership/history. Local coordination protects runners sharing the same managed home; it does not serialize independent machines.

Do not clear a deployment lease in the writing phase because its TTL expired. Oracle DDL may have committed. Read the actual server state before recovery; compatible application metadata may be safely replanned, while conflicting changes and database scripts require review. An APEX metadata restore does not recover business data or destructive schema changes. See [deployment safety](https://apexrest-dev.github.io/apexrest/deployment/).

title: Contributing
text:
Contributing

APEXREST is developed in [apexrest-dev/apexrest](https://github.com/apexrest-dev/apexrest). Code, CLI help, agent skill instructions, public documentation and diagrams use English. Keep changes focused and make claims match the evidence.

Keep executable examples, configuration keys, paths, version numbers and evidence boundaries accurate in every guide. Keep functional catalog provenance, third-party notices and pinned source locks intact. Generated verification reports belong in ignored docs/evidence/ and do not substitute for required live checks. Run npm run docs:check and the site checks after documentation changes.

 Set up a checkout

Use Node 24 LTS and the committed lockfile:

sh
git clone https://github.com/apexrest-dev/apexrest.git
cd apexrest
npm ci --ignore-scripts
npm run build


After source, dependency, skill or resource changes, run npm run plugin:sync. It builds and refreshes the checked-in self-contained plugin bundle used by repository installations, including the Codex manifest (.codex-plugin/plugin.json), the Claude Code manifest (.claude-plugin/plugin.json) and both repository marketplaces (.agents/plugins/marketplace.json, .claude-plugin/marketplace.json). Commit the resulting bundle with its source changes. With the claude CLI installed, npm run test:packaging also runs claude plugin validate --strict on the generated manifests. plugins/apexrest-apex/runtime/ and plugins/apexrest-apex/resources/ are generated output, marked linguist-generated in .gitattributes; do not edit them by hand. Change the sources and rerun npm run plugin:sync.

The normal build does not deploy an app or install Oracle binaries. Native-host setup, vendor downloads, connection onboarding and remote integration have their own prerequisites. See [getting started](https://apexrest-dev.github.io/apexrest/getting-started/).

 Validate a change

sh
npm run lint
npm run typecheck
npm run test:unit
npm run test:contracts
npm run test:installers
npm run site:build
npm run test:packaging


Run the checks relevant to the changed behavior, including build before packaging tests. Run npm run plugin:check after a fresh build to verify that the checked-in plugin matches its generated runtime/resources. npm run test:repository-plugin exercises the repository bundle in a fresh isolated Codex profile without connecting to or writing an Oracle target. Native registration changes also need the real isolated Codex lifecycle check; Oracle adapter or application changes need appropriate real compiler/target evidence when a target is authorized and available. If a required environment is absent, record the blocker rather than substituting a mock result. See [testing](https://apexrest-dev.github.io/apexrest/testing/).

The [documentation website](https://apexrest-dev.github.io/apexrest/) is served from main:/docs. After editing Markdown or the site/ renderer/theme, run npm run site:build and npm run site:check, then commit the generated Pages files with their sources. Run npm run site:preview to inspect the tracked output at http://127.0.0.1:4173/apexrest/; check navigation, search and narrow layouts. See the [Pages authoring guide](https://apexrest-dev.github.io/apexrest/publishing/documentation-on-github-pages).

 Engineering expectations

- Keep TypeScript strict, use ESM, and synchronize public CLI/MCP schemas with behavior.
- Preserve Oracle-generated .apex metadata, IDs, unrelated components and working-tree edits.
- Bind plans to source and target; preserve backup, drift, authorization, coordination and unknown-outcome checks.
- Keep secrets, browser state, local runtimes, raw business data and private backups out of source control.
- Update documentation and the relevant acceptance/evidence records when behavior or verification changes.
- Review dependency upgrades with pinned URLs/hashes, licensing, an architecture decision and actual compatibility evidence.

Keep repository documentation focused on the current contract. Do not commit obsolete plans, rollout archives or generated verification history. Record active requirements in AGENTS.md, the acceptance matrix and the relevant guide.

 Open a pull request

Describe the concrete problem and resulting behavior. Include the validation actually run, its environment and any remaining limitation. Explain safety or compatibility tradeoffs when they matter. Reproduce a bug before widening a fix, and avoid unrelated formatting or dependency churn.

Use a codex/ branch for Codex-created work unless the maintainer requests a different name. Review the staged diff for credentials and private artifacts before committing. A contribution does not authorize deployments, paid resources, release tags or publication.

 Release work

Before packaging a release, run npm run plugin:sync, then npm run plugin:check, and verify the native repository installation with npm run test:repository-plugin. npm run release:dry-run creates unsigned local artifacts and a readiness report. Stable readiness requires current evidence bound to the exact immutable source. Publishing requires the separate protected workflow and maintainer authorization; it is not part of a normal build or pull request. See [publisher setup](https://apexrest-dev.github.io/apexrest/publishing/).

Report security issues using [SECURITY.md](https://apexrest-dev.github.io/apexrest/security/), not public issue attachments containing secrets.

title: Implementation status
text:
Implementation status

The current source and bundled plugin version is 2.9.0. The current contract is described in [architecture](architecture.md), [testing](testing.md) and the [acceptance matrix](acceptance.json).

 Fast-development follow-up backlog (2026-11-25, local, branch feat/fast-development)

Work items are APE-405 to APE-438 in Linear; each section names its backlog ID. Implementation, repository tests, compiler evidence, native import and browser observations are reported separately.

A01 compound page edits ([APE-405](https://linear.app/apexrest/issue/APE-405)). packages/core/src/edit/transaction.ts plans every operation of one request against one immutable page snapshot, combines the text edits, parses the result, has each operation read its change back and only then replaces the file atomically under the source-edit lock after rechecking the digest. project action:edit (project.edit) accepts set operations (the patch properties and query) and insert fragments in one request. patch and insert now run through the same transaction with unchanged results. Operations target only components of the snapshot read. Verified by tests/unit/source-edit-transaction.test.ts (combined write, byte-identical failures, stale digest, MCP routing) and the existing patch and insert tests. No compiler or native import run is claimed for this change.

A02 context after every edit ([APE-413](https://linear.app/apexrest/issue/APE-413)). patch, insert and edit results carry context computed from the exact bytes written (planned bytes for a dry run) by packages/core/src/edit/context.ts: the new digest, changed and inserted targets with their editable values, and removed targets. Unchanged components are omitted, and line moves alone do not count as a change. The delta lists at most 40 entries and cuts query text at 2000 characters, pointing to action:context when bounded; context:"full" and context:"none" are available. Verified by tests/unit/source-edit-transaction.test.ts (delta values, digest reuse, external-edit conflict, removed columns, modes).

A03 working filters ([APE-422](https://linear.app/apexrest/issue/APE-422)). The addFilter edit operation (packages/core/src/edit/filter.ts) inserts the item and an optional container region, makes every target report, cards region or chart series submit the item (a missing property, a scalar list or an Oracle-exported [ ... ] array) and adds one refresh of all targets, in one page transaction. Optional complete replacement SQL is applied per report (with its column contract), cards region or chart series. Predicates are never rewritten: a target query that does not bind the item is refused (FILTER_NOT_BOUND), as are other region families. Verified:
- Repository tests (tests/unit/source-edit-filter.test.ts): submitted items and binds of every target, array extension without reformatting, one refresh of all targets, unchanged existing dynamic actions, refusals and conflicts.
- Local preview (SQLite) in the same test file: the filtered report shows all rows initially, only matching rows for a changed value, no rows for a value without matches, and all rows again after clearing.
- Oracle offline compiler (SQLcl 26.3.0.260.1620, 26.2 profile) on a scratch customer-crm project: report filter on page 10, cards and chart-series filter on page 20, both passed with 0 diagnostics and 0 warnings (docs/evidence/fast-dev/addfilter-compiler-2026-11-25.json, local, not committed).
- Not run: native import and browser behaviour on an APEX target.

A04 report columns with their dependent declarations ([APE-423](https://linear.app/apexrest/issue/APE-423)). packages/core/src/edit/columns.ts adds addColumn (complete caller SQL, one new column placed at the start, after or before a column, or at the end) and orderColumns (presentation-only reorder, SQL bytes kept). A free sequence gap is used when one exists; otherwise the listed columns are renumbered. Interactive reports keep the primary default saved report's displayColumn list in the same order. The query patch now also removes dropped columns from every saved report, shows new columns in the default report, and refuses to drop a column that a saved-report sort, filter or other declaration references (COLUMN_REFERENCED). Two fixes to the query patch: new columns go after the existing columns instead of after the saved report, and their data type uses the release's spelling (varchar2 for 26.2, STRING for 26.1) instead of always the 26.1 one. Verified:
- Repository tests (tests/unit/source-edit-columns.test.ts, tests/unit/source-patch.test.ts): placement at start, middle and end, gap use, renumbering, retained bytes, saved-report order, referenced-column refusal and conflicts.
- Oracle offline compiler (SQLcl 26.3.0.260.1620, 26.2 profile): addColumn of a date column with format mask and orderColumns on the customer-crm interactive report passed with 0 diagnostics and 0 warnings (docs/evidence/fast-dev/columns-compiler-2026-11-25.json, local).
- Not run: native import and browser display.

A05 dialog actions on existing pages ([APE-424](https://linear.app/apexrest/issue/APE-424)). The addDialogAction edit operation (packages/core/src/edit/dialog.ts) adds an interactive-report row link, a classic-report column link or a button that opens an existing modal page with item mappings and clear-cache pages, and a native dialog-closed refresh (region or button trigger). An existing equivalent refresh is reused; new names never collide. The modal page is read in the same locked transaction (the transaction now loads dependent page files); its modal mode, mapped items and COLUMN references are checked, and expectedTargetDigest binds the edit to the modal page read. Authorization is never added or removed; a modal page running processes without a page authorization scheme returns a warning. Verified:
- Repository tests (tests/unit/source-edit-dialog.test.ts): link replacement with ids kept, mappings, refresh reuse, classic column link, button with its own refresh, refusals (non-modal, missing page, unknown item or column, missing refresh, stale modal page).
- Oracle offline compiler (SQLcl 26.3.0.260.1620, 26.2 profile): row link and button to the customer-crm modal page 80 passed with 0 diagnostics and 0 warnings (docs/evidence/fast-dev/dialog-compiler-2026-11-25.json, local).
- Not run: native import and dialog behaviour in a browser.

A06 shared LOV editing ([APE-414](https://linear.app/apexrest/issue/APE-414)). packages/core/src/edit/lov.ts adds project action:lov_context / lov_edit (lov.context, lov.edit; CLI apexrest lov context|edit). A LOV is located by id or name in the release's qualified layout (26.2: one per shared-components/lovs/.apx; 26.1: all in shared-components/lovs.apx); ambiguous names, a 26.2 file with several LOVs and unknown releases fail before writing. Static entries are replaced as a complete ordered list (kept return values keep id and bytes); a local SQL-query LOV gets complete replacement SQL and optional display/return columns. The write uses the same digest check, lock and atomic replace as page edits (guardedEdit, now shared). Results list the pages that reference the LOV but report shared-component scope (affectedPages: unknown). Partial-import file selection and Oracle's page-only scoped export are unchanged. Verified:
- Repository tests (tests/unit/source-edit-lov.test.ts): 26.2 and 26.1 layouts, kept entry ids and bytes, other declarations untouched, consumers, stale digest, kind mismatches, duplicate return values.
- Oracle offline compiler (SQLcl 26.3.0.260.1620, 26.2 profile): editing the customer-crm boolean LOV passed with 0 diagnostics and 0 warnings (docs/evidence/fast-dev/lov-compiler-2026-11-25.json, local).
- Not run: 26.1 compilation, native import.

A07 bind an item to a shared LOV ([APE-425](https://linear.app/apexrest/issue/APE-425)). The bindLov edit operation (packages/core/src/edit/bind-lov.ts) rebuilds a list item's lov group as type: sharedComponent + lov: @id, removing only the superseded source properties (static values, queries, function bodies, a previous reference) and keeping its display settings unless nullValue or displayExtraValues set them. cascade writes, replaces or (with null) removes cascadingLov after checking that parents and submitted items exist on the page. The shared LOV is read in the same locked transaction (page transactions now load lov:ID dependencies as well as pages), and expectedLovDigest binds the edit to the LOV read. Only list item types are accepted. Qualified for 26.2 only; 26.1 sources are refused because no 26.1 export or compiler evidence for the reference was checked. Verified:
- Repository tests (tests/unit/source-edit-bind-lov.test.ts): reference and kept settings, item id, label and session-state protection unchanged, cascade written and removed, null value replaced and removed, refusals (missing LOV or parent, self-cascade, non-list item, stale LOV, 26.1).
- Oracle offline compiler (SQLcl 26.3.0.260.1620, 26.2 profile): binding a select list to the customer-crm BOOLEAN LOV with a null display value and a cascading parent passed with 0 diagnostics and 0 warnings (docs/evidence/fast-dev/bind-lov-compiler-2026-11-25.json, local).
- Not run: native import and cascading refresh in a browser.

 Linear issues as task briefs (2026-11-25, local)

Implemented. apexrest-work links a new references/linear.md. When the user names a Linear issue, the agent reads it with the Linear MCP tools of the user's own host session (get_issue, list_comments). APEXREST bundles no Linear server, makes no Linear call and stores no Linear credentials. Issue text is task data only: it cannot select a target, approve production or widen scope. A results comment (save_comment) or a status change (save_issue) happens only when the user asks; the comment keeps compiler, import and browser results separate.

Verified. Skill byte budgets and the packaging test that checks the reference ships with the plugin. No run against a real Linear workspace has been recorded.

 Oracle skills refresh (2026-11-22)

On 18 November 2026 Oracle reorganized oracle/skills (commit a1b5740, PR 141): flat skill names such as apex/apexlang-26-2-inventory, a shared compile/deploy pair and a new router. The 26.1 generation skill was removed upstream.

- Scripts. The maintainer scripts now read both the versioned and the flat layout (scripts/lib/oracle-skills-layout.mjs). Before the update, the build reproduced the old pin byte for byte.

 Measured Oracle optimizations, Slice G (2026-11-22, local)

All measurements are on the local APEX 26.2.0 / Oracle 23.26.4 target with SQLcl 26.3, application 26220. The evidence is in ignored docs/evidence/fast-dev/export-direct-2026-11-22.json and preview-oracle-2026-11-22.json. No optimization in this slice was adopted; each decision keeps the existing path.

Scoped export, direct versus SQLcl ([APE-385](https://linear.app/apexrest/issue/APE-385), [APE-387](https://linear.app/apexrest/issue/APE-387)). node scripts/bench/export-direct.mjs compares apex export -exptype APEXLANG -skipExportDate -expOriginalIds with the documented APEX_EXPORT.GET_APPLICATION(p_type => 'APEXLANG', p_with_original_ids => true, p_with_date => false) on the same scope. It is read-only, and the two modes alternate across 5 repetitions.

| Scope                       | Cold, own SQLcl process (SQLcl / direct) | Warm, one session (SQLcl / direct) | Content                                                                                          |
| --------------------------- | ---------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Page 10                     | 3,151 / 3,133 ms                         | 1,421 / 1,402 ms                   | Same file; canonically equal                                                                     |
| Full application (27 files) | 3,486 / 3,507 ms                         | 1,943 / 1,757 ms                   | Same files; text canonically equal; binary static files need a separate encoding through a query |

- Selection limits are identical. Both interfaces accept only one component per APEXlang call: a list such as PAGE:10,PAGE:1 fails with ORA-20987. A shared LOV is not an APEXlang export component in either interface (ORA-20987).
- Export identity is unchanged by the switch. Both interfaces export with original ids and without the export date.
- Where the time goes. About 1.7 s of a cold page export is SQLcl startup and connect; the server-side export is about 1.4 s.
- Decision. The direct export brings no material benefit (under 2% for a page) and would need its own file transport for binary content. The SQLcl adapter is kept, so the backup, readback and canonical-comparison paths are unchanged.

Validation reuse ([APE-389](https://linear.app/apexrest/issue/APE-389)). A repeated validation of an unchanged snapshot costs 77–104 ms warm (2.4–2.7 s cold) against a 9–14 s page ship. Planning validates the whole source and then the selected effective snapshot in one process, so the second run is already warm. Reuse would save under 1% of a ship. Decision: not implemented. The separate pre-import validation and Oracle's import validation are unchanged.

Connected preview profile ([APE-379](https://linear.app/apexrest/issue/APE-379)). node scripts/benchmark-preview-oracle.mjs wraps the preview's Oracle link and counts, per page request:

- round trips;
- batch segments;
- APEX session creations;
- time the main thread is blocked in Atomics.wait.

Starting the connection costs 2.3 s and 9 round trips. That includes the schema prefetch and one APEX session warm-up.

| Page            | Request, median of 10 | Main thread blocked | Round trips (segments) | Queries | APEX sessions |
| --------------- | --------------------- | ------------------- | ---------------------- | ------- | ------------- |
| 10 (report)     | 21.7 ms               | 19.0 ms             | 2 (3)                  | 1       | 0             |
| 20 (dashboard)  | 16.5 ms               | 14.7 ms             | 2 (3)                  | 1       | 0             |
| 30 (dashboard)  | 40.7 ms               | 38.0 ms             | 3 (5)                  | 2       | 0             |
| 1, 80 (no data) | under 1 ms            | 0                   | 0                      | 0       | 0             |

- Round trips. Each request with data makes one batched round trip for its queries and one for the closing rollback. A round trip takes about 9–15 ms.
- Blocking. About 90% of a request is main-thread blocking, and the worst event-loop delay equals the Oracle wait (17–35 ms).
- Edit loop. A title edit on page 10 appears in the connected page in 27.6 ms median, with 2 round trips.
- Not exercised. These pages run no PL/SQL with APEX context, so per-request APEX context initialization was not measured.

Batching and context reuse ([APE-396](https://linear.app/apexrest/issue/APE-396)). Queries are already batched. Merging the closing rollback into the last batch would save one round trip, about 10 ms per request. A browser reload dominates that, so it is not material for the edit loop. Request-scoped APEX context reuse has nothing to save on this workload, which had no per-request APEX sessions. Decision: deferred. It needs a page with APEX-context PL/SQL first.

Main-thread blocking ([APE-395](https://linear.app/apexrest/issue/APE-395)). A request blocks the event loop for at most about 40 ms on these pages, and the preview serves one developer. Decision: deferred, with this measurement as evidence. Moving a whole request to a worker is reconsidered if a page blocks for a noticeable time (hundreds of milliseconds).

 Warm state and session qualification, Slice E (2026-11-22, local, uncommitted)

Where import time goes. On the local APEX 26.2.0 target, a page import spends 2.5 s on the fresh pre-write export, 0.65 s connecting and 3.1 s in Oracle's import. The prepared import server's JVM is already started off the critical path (spawn 0 ms). Each database script costs about 1.7–1.9 s in its own SQLcl process.

JVM and compiler reuse ([APE-382](https://linear.app/apexrest/issue/APE-382), [APE-388](https://linear.app/apexrest/issue/APE-388)). Not kept across imports: there is no measurable gain, and a server is bound to one frozen import directory. The fallback rules now have tests: a server without the HOST refusal, or one that fails to connect, submits nothing and falls back; after submission a failure or cancellation is reported as an interrupted import; the server runs one import only.

Connected-session reuse ([APE-386](https://linear.app/apexrest/issue/APE-386), [APE-390](https://linear.app/apexrest/issue/APE-390)). scripts/bench/session-reuse.mjs was run on SQLcl 26.3 and Oracle 23.26.4; the evidence is in docs/evidence/fast-dev/session-reuse-2026-11-22.json.

- Without a reset, the next operation sees the earlier one's uncommitted row, its package global (42) and current_schema=SYS.
- ROLLBACK, package reinitialization and a current_schema reset clear all three.
- WHENEVER SQLERROR EXIT ends the session before the marker (exit 2) and rolls back.
- Process exit commits pending DML.

One session for an apply's scripts ([APE-404](https://linear.app/apexrest/issue/APE-404)). Implemented as ScriptSession, used when an apply has two or more scripts.

Server-mode qualification on SQLcl 26.3:

- HOST is refused;
- each script with its marker is committed;
- an error leaves no marker and rolls back; the server stays alive but its connection is dropped;
- a killed process mid-script returns "Connection closed" and the work is rolled back.

On the local APEX 26.2 target, two package scripts took 2.03 and 2.13 s against 3.91 and 3.98 s with one process per script (alternating, 2 runs each); the objects stayed VALID. In a failure run the first two scripts recorded as applied after their markers. The third failed (ORA-01476) and the run became OUTCOME_UNKNOWN (ORACLE_COMMAND_FAILED), the same classification as the process path. It was released through deploy reconcile. Unit tests cover the fallback, reset, discard and failure rules.

 Reviewed database reconciliation (2026-11-22, local, uncommitted)

[APE-403](https://linear.app/apexrest/issue/APE-403). apexrest deploy reconcile releases a run held as database-review-required once a person has inspected the database:

- the person states every migration and package of the run as applied or not_applied;
- the person types --confirm <run id>:<plan digest prefix>;
- the command records userRequest and the statement in reconciliation.json, updates the local history exactly as stated, and releases the run's ownership.

It never connects to the database. It refuses an incomplete statement, a different environment or target, production, a finished run, another host and a live run process. It is CLI only, with no MCP tool.

Database-only plans and aliases. importMode:none plans no longer fail on another workspace application's alias (APPLICATION_ALIAS_IN_USE); they import no application.

Verified on the local APEX 26.2. Held run 08e6e532 (APEXREST_262_TEST) was released after the user confirmed that both its packages were not applied. A fresh database-only ship then created APEXREST_CUSTOMERS, the package and its body, and the trigger, all VALID. Unit tests cover the refusals and the history updates.

 Development broker, Slice D (2026-11-22, local, uncommitted)

Broker ([APE-361](https://linear.app/apexrest/issue/APE-361), [APE-373](https://linear.app/apexrest/issue/APE-373)). broker.ts adds apexrest dev start|status|stop: one process per project on a private token-protected Unix socket or named pipe. It has an idle timeout, and its stop waits for running jobs. Ship apply jobs from MCP go to the broker when it runs; otherwise they use the detached worker as before.

Ownership ([APE-365](https://linear.app/apexrest/issue/APE-365)). Every runner (broker, detached worker, in-process) now claims a job with claim.json, created with O_EXCL, before it runs. An unconfirmed hand-off can therefore start a fallback worker without running the job twice. failQueuedJob no longer fails a claimed job; its heartbeat decides. Never-started, started-unknown and completed-with-lost-response jobs keep their existing records.

Coalescing ([APE-375](https://linear.app/apexrest/issue/APE-375)). The broker runs ship.apply jobs one at a time per environment. Waiting jobs collapse into the newest when its plan is at least as recent. The others become superseded (shown as a success that never started, naming the job that applies the changes). A running import is never touched.

Unknown outcomes ([APE-372](https://linear.app/apexrest/issue/APE-372)). Already enforced: an unknown outcome keeps the deployment lease (TARGET_LOCKED), as seen with the held local run 08e6e532.

Measured ([APE-378](https://linear.app/apexrest/issue/APE-378)). On the local APEX 26.2.0 target, ship.apply jobs measured from start to terminal state, 3 runs each, alternating:

| Runner          | Median | Backup | Import |
| --------------- | ------ | ------ | ------ |
| Detached worker | 9.31 s | 2.11 s | 6.52 s |
| Broker          | 9.06 s | 1.99 s | 6.49 s |

The broker saves about 0.25 s, within run-to-run noise. The import itself dominates, through the isolated SQLcl write session. A coalescing check on the same target queued two applies back to back: the first was superseded and the second completed.

 Incremental preview, Slice C (2026-11-22, local, uncommitted)

Source index ([APE-351](https://linear.app/apexrest/issue/APE-351)). loadApplication takes a per-file parse cache keyed by size, modification time and substitutions, so unchanged files keep their parsed components. preview/source-index.ts lists the changed files and the affected pages:

- a page file affects that page;
- a shared component affects the pages that reference it;
- the application, the global page, a theme or an unknown file affects every page.

Watcher and stale state ([APE-353](https://linear.app/apexrest/issue/APE-353), [APE-359](https://linear.app/apexrest/issue/APE-359)). Watcher events mark the sources dirty before the debounce. Requests rescan only when the sources are dirty, when no watcher is running, or every two seconds. A failed load keeps the last good renderer with a "Stale preview" banner and the error. Previously every page returned HTTP 500.

Targeted reload ([APE-358](https://linear.app/apexrest/issue/APE-358), [APE-366](https://linear.app/apexrest/issue/APE-366)). Reload messages carry the source revision, the files and the affected pages; hello carries the revision, and older or repeated notifications are ignored. CSS static files are replaced in place.

Region replacement ([APE-374](https://linear.app/apexrest/issue/APE-374), [APE-368](https://linear.app/apexrest/issue/APE-368)). An in-place edit that changes only static content, classic report, interactive report or cards regions is replaced through the regions' existing refresh lifecycle. Everything else reloads the page.

Text edits in those regions are covered by the region replacement. Item and button labels reload the page; there is no separate text patching.

Verified:

- Unit tests cover equivalence of cached and clean loads, scope, renames, stale state, region eligibility and the live message.
- In the built-in browser with two tabs, patching the region title on page 10 replaced that region in place: the tab was not reloaded and the new text appeared. The page 1 tab was not touched.

 Semantic page edits, Slice B (2026-11-22, local, uncommitted)

Lossless editor ([APE-350](https://linear.app/apexrest/issue/APE-350)). edit/apexlang-edit.ts scans one .apx file into components, groups and property lines with exact offsets.  literals, object and array values, and // and / / comments stay opaque. An edit replaces only a property's value bytes. A missing property or group is inserted with the file's indentation and line ending. Values that would read as references, booleans or quoted text are written as JSON-quoted text. The preview parser only validates the result.

Results:

- Over the repository corpus, the scanner accepts all 1,353 .apx files.
- Setting 68,243 scalar properties to their current value changed 0 bytes.

Committed source revision ([APE-356](https://linear.app/apexrest/issue/APE-356)). edit/patch.ts binds an edit to the digest of the page file the caller read. It checks the digest again under .apexrest/source-edit.lock right before an atomic replace, and returns the before and after digests and the SourceChange (files and affected pages). Without the digest, or with dryRun, it returns currentDigest and writes nothing. Stale, repeated, ambiguous, unsupported and overlapping requests fail before any write. A patch only edits one page file, so there is no multi-file staging.

Operations ([APE-364](https://linear.app/apexrest/issue/APE-364), [APE-362](https://linear.app/apexrest/issue/APE-362), [APE-363](https://linear.app/apexrest/issue/APE-363)):

- page title;

The 2026-11-16 post-ship sync-init fix follows a real SQLcl 26.3 / APEX 26.2 run: after --action invalidate and a successful full ship --mode apply --import-mode full of hand-written sources, apex sync --action init failed with SYNC_SOURCE_CONFLICT and named no files. The staged export differed only by Oracle's canonical rewrites across application.apx, the navigation menu and nine pages (unquoted names, inline sqlQuery, canonical slot names, dropped defaults, added savedReportMappingIdentifier/border properties). A confirmed, verified full import that is not a restore or selected-file import now reads target identity and update metadata in one targetWithMetadata call after the import (falling back to verifyTarget) and writes post-import.json to the run directory before the run is journaled succeeded. During init, lastImportProof accepts a run only when its plan digest verifies, its journal state is succeeded, project ID, project root, environment, target digest and source directory match, the plan's application sources equal the local inventory exactly, and the current target and update metadata equal the post-import record. The server export is then adopted for every differing file (normalized, rule last-import-rewrite, normalizedFromDeploymentRunId); the imported bytes stay in the run's snapshot/. The APEXlang equivalence comparator is not used as the guard: it fails closed on fenced-to-inline literals, slot renames and added properties, so it could not prove these rewrites. Provenance is the stronger proof here. Every refusal and every other difference still conflicts and leaves local files unchanged. SYNC_SOURCE_CONFLICT now carries one diagnostic per file, bounded addedFiles/removedFiles/changedFiles, differingFileCount and an importProof reason. Unit regressions cover the file list, post-ship adoption, a local edit after ship, a server change after ship and another target. The adoption test fails with the proof disabled, and the conflict tests fail with the proof forced on or the metadata comparison removed. Checks: lint, typecheck, build and the full unit suite (728 tests, 720 passed, 8 optional skips). Not verified against Oracle: init was not rerun on a real target after the fix, and runs shipped before this change have no post-import.json. Ship once more, or reconcile manually, before init can adopt.

The 2026-11-06 sync-init normalization fix follows the first deployment of a generated blank 26.2 application to the local Oracle AI Database 26ai Free (APEX 26.2.0, ORDS 26.3.0, SQLcl 26.3.0): apex sync --action init failed with SYNC_SOURCE_CONFLICT because the server export added app.id to deployments/default.json and dropped the empty deinstall script and its deinstall reference. generatedSourceNormalizations now recognises exactly those two rewrites during init (the server app.id must equal the configured application ID; the script must be empty or whitespace and absent on the server; removing the deinstall block must reproduce the server bytes), adopts the server files and reports them; any other difference keeps the conflict and leaves local files unchanged. Unit regressions cover accepted and refused variants and two sync-init workflows; they fail both with the normalization disabled and with an over-permissive version. Run against the real generated sources and the staged real server export, the function returned exactly the three expected files. The full unit suite passed in a clean clone (611 tests, 604 passed, 7 optional skips), with typecheck, lint, contracts, packaging and installer tests clean. A repeated sync init on a fresh project against the real target was not run; the local project was reconciled manually before the fix.

The 2026-11-02 transactionRisk fix replaces the two-pass regular expressions with a single left-to-right scan (codeOutsideLiterals) that masks line and block comments, '…' literals with doubled quotes, q'…'/nq'…' literals with their exact closing delimiter and quoted identifiers in the order they open. Line comments end at LF or CR, matching SQLcl line splitting, and an unclosed construct is refused. A regression covers the review's comment/q-quote bypasses, CR comments, mismatched closers, prefixes, unclosed constructs and allowed mentions; it fails with the previous expressions.
