Metadata responses add only session count/total SQLcl time by default; debugTimings: true includes the individual records. Scoped metadata reads now batch identity and all requested queries into one connected session, rejecting all rows on identity mismatch. Working-copy fingerprints batch identity and update metadata in one session. A full working-copy apply with the same read/deploy connection and no fresh export uses four connected sessions in fake-runner checks: start observation, post-freeze pre-import observation, import, post-import observation. Different connections keep a separate deploy identity check. Fresh-export paths reuse the start export as backup and retain the stronger post-freeze pre-import drift check (three total exports including plan); other export-backed paths retain the post-backup drift check; database scripts keep a post-freeze first-write barrier and exact local migration-history validation. Post-import metadata supplies the successful checkpoint. Cancellation, frozen-source checks and interrupted-write ownership remain intact. The optional same-session import guard is deferred because MCP R4 lacks a proven error-stop contract. The APEX 26.1.5 read-only follow-up passed 40 measured samples and two excluded warm-ups (20 per scenario), with 44 MCP calls in 188.97 seconds. Metadata median/p95 changed from 9.62/12.79 to 5.42/6.03 seconds; full-import plan changed from 6.86/7.96 to 3.13/4.04 seconds. Each used one fresh connected session; steady-state planning also used one reused offline compiler session. Median summed spawn/connect/execute intervals were 0.70 ms/null/5411.46 ms for metadata and 0.46 ms/null/3138.48 ms for plan. CLI spawn measures OS process creation; JVM startup and connection setup remain inside execute. Parallel plan intervals can overlap. These are separate runs on the same recorded machine/target, without controlled network/load/cache conditions. Whole-host token checkpoints are retained separately from per-call billing, which remains unavailable. The four-session apply reduction is estimated at about 12.45 seconds of saved session time using the 3.11-second read-only observation median as a proxy; it is estimated, not measured on Oracle. No import, database write or DDL was run in this follow-up. Typecheck, lint, 408 unit checks (one optional check skipped), 70 contracts, build, documentation and bundle checks passed.

Run the relevant checks in [testing](testing.md) against the current source. Local unit, contract, installer, documentation and packaging checks establish their stated fixture/build behavior. Oracle compilation, connected imports, authenticated application browsing and fresh native model-host execution require separate checks on an authorized target. Browser checks are not inferred from compiler/import success.

The current parity source passed typecheck and lint, 383 unit checks (one additional check skipped), 62 contracts, 46 installer checks and all 29 packaging cases. Claude Code 2.1.291 accepted the plugin and marketplace manifests with strict validation. The final unit run followed the completed build and had local-listener access for its ORDS protocol fixture; npm inventory used a private temporary cache. These are repository, manifest and subprocess checks, not native model-host execution.

Host parity changes preserve the existing scoped deployment core. Both manifest launch adapters are checked from a relocated package, with equal tool contracts/reference results and shared managed connection state. Installer checks cover dual-host launch bindings, source-safe reinstall, Node changes and Claude metadata integrity. Source-bound validation and packaging results are recorded separately under ignored docs/evidence/host-parity/. Native Codex/Claude model-host execution and new Oracle/browser runs are not established by these subprocess/fixture checks. Managed setup still registers Codex only; Claude uses its native plugin commands.

On the explicitly authorized local Oracle APEX 26.2 target, page creation and isolated replacement passed Oracle compiler/import/readback checks. APEXlang restoration of the previous selected page also passed without a SQL application dump. A stopped verification was reconciled as already applied without replay; Oracle filenames are matched by unique page ID rather than alias spelling. New and changed shared LOV files passed isolated imports: their plans explicitly disclose full APEXlang observation, while backup, import and comparison retain the selected scope. A final separate full audit checks unrelated files and business-row counts; it is outside the page-only edit cycle.

The authenticated in-app browser showed the new dashboard's version marker, three zero-valued CRM cards, empty customer chart, demonstration chart and the changed shared LOV label. These observations establish this dashboard and dependency rendering, not full CRM CRUD or security qualification. Page replacement measured about 34 seconds including planning/apply/readback; new dashboard creation about 44 seconds. Shared-component creation/replacement measured about 42/49 seconds because native selected export is unavailable for these families. Local no-op measured about 30 milliseconds with zero Oracle calls. The earlier whole-export flow took about 48 seconds for plan/apply; these are individual local samples, not a controlled performance guarantee. Independent machines/homes still require external serialization.

The user reported successful live Claude Code verification on 2026-10-07. That session reported an isolated analytics-page import with --import-mode files on the local 26.2 target: an occupied page 40 blocked planning, page 70 imported, and ship mode:recover recognized the already-applied result after key-ordered classic report columns caused a readback mismatch. It also reported four expected regions and unchanged pages 40/50/60, with no browser check requested. These are session-reported observations; the follow-up commit review did not independently repeat Oracle or native-host execution.

On 2026-10-15 three working-copy sync defects found during recipe imports were fixed. Native selected export now issues one -expComponents call per component, because APEX 26.2 rejects a component list with ORA-20987 even for existing pages (reproduced with pages 1 and 10). The selected-source equivalence policy now reads scalar lists, binds fenced code to its property, ignores the order of uniquely named properties and groups and of key-ordered page, process-parameter and dynamic-action children with explicit sequences, and accepts single-line JSON-quoted code, upper-cased invoke identifiers and the defaults observed in native exports (invokeApi direction/dataType/ignoreOutput, items-event change, page cursorFocus and formAutoComplete, classic-report pagination). Planning treats server files that differ from the checkpoint only by these canonical forms as unchanged, including in the reviewed before side revalidated by apply, so a full import no longer blocks the next full or selected plan and no export is added after imports. On the local APEX 26.2 target, a two-new-page selected import, a selected import of an authored page with template-option lists and a selected import after a full import all succeeded with equivalent readback, and mode:recover closed a run interrupted before the fix; tests: 421 unit (one skip), 114 contract, 29 packaging. The equivalence policy now accepts key-ordered columns only for classic reports with unique explicit sequences; other region types, absent/duplicate sequences and changed column identities/query IDs remain strict. Conflict diagnostics name the overlapping files. Follow-up repository checks passed typecheck, lint, 32 focused equivalence/partial-import/partial-export tests and the checked-in plugin CLI/stdio MCP smoke. The source bundle and documentation were regenerated and checked. Full unit, contract, installer and packaging suites were not rerun for this follow-up.

On 2026-11-04 the local stack was rebuilt in Podman (Oracle AI Database 26ai Free 23.26.3, APEX 26.2.0 installed in FREEPDB1, ORDS 26.3.0) and the current repository build was run against it from the CLI. A new customer-crm project (application 26201) passed the compiler, plan and a full apply with one migration and two packages: identity was confirmed, the grant was recorded and removed, and an independent dictionary read showed six pages, valid objects and no user_errors. After apex sync init adopted the server export, a one-page change passed an automatic selected import of pages/p00001-home.apx, and the new region was present on the server. That first selected import still needed an empty packagesDir, because selection refused any package script. Selection now skips package scripts whose checksum matches their last successful run, as the full plan already did, and the selected plan records that package history for apply validation; a changed script still falls back to a full import. A regression test covers both cases and fails without the fix. With the real packagesDir restored, a second Home change was selected automatically as pages/p00001-home.apx and applied; the server showed the new text, and the package body and trigger kept their earlier DDL time. Typecheck, lint, 608 unit tests (607 passed, one skipped), 115 contract and 30 packaging tests, the repository plugin smoke and plugin:check passed after plugin:sync. Remaining findings from this run are in [next actions](next-actions.md). No browser check was requested. Private outputs are under ignored docs/evidence/local-stack-20261104/.

On 2026-11-06 the containers were recreated on the surviving database and ORDS volumes; APEX 26.2.0 and application 26201 were intact. An automatic selected import of a Home change passed again. A database-only plan (importMode: none) on a project with a working copy could not be applied: it combined working-copy with fresh-export, which the v2/v3 plan schema refused (INVALID_INPUT). The schema now accepts that combination for database-only plans only. A unit test fails without the fix and passes with it. With a local build, the changed package script ran on the server without an application import: the package body's DDL time changed, a 201-character name raised the new ORA-20013 and user_errors stayed empty. After rebasing on the upstream agent-speed and sync-init commits, the checked-in plugin and site were rebuilt; 628 unit tests ran (626 passed, 2 skipped), and the 115 contract, 30 packaging and 46 installer tests, typecheck, lint, plugin:check, docs:check and site:check passed. This rebuilt plugin has not been rerun against the local stack. Private outputs are under ignored docs/evidence/local-stack-20261106/.

The official inventory maintenance change passed complete archive/document/type/property reconciliation and 2,269 packaged MCP reads for all 389 definitions. Its focused checks cover exact pagination, ordinary component/property discovery, independently bound search bytes, recovery of incomplete/corrupt accelerators, integrity failure, release isolation, public Oracle enums and continued operation/diagnostic secret redaction. Independent temporary-copy forward checks also passed source refresh and synthetic MMD/new-release review decisions. These are library/compiler checks, not connected or native-host qualification.

Parity implementation checks did not register the bundle into the user's existing Codex or Claude Code profiles. Local contracts exercise relocated MCP subprocesses, and Claude's native CLI validates manifests without starting a model session. The user's subsequent Claude Code verification is reported above; independent fresh cache/skill reload and model-driven tool qualification remain open for both hosts. Parity implementation and follow-up review used isolated fixtures without changing global connection, credential, toolchain or deployment-history state.

Release readiness requires source-bound reports for every mandatory gate. Generated reports are private working output under ignored docs/evidence/; their absence blocks readiness. No connected or native-host result is inferred from a local build.

The 2.3.0 repository integration checks passed on Node 24.21.0: 431 unit checks with one optional SQLcl pooling case skipped, 115 contracts, 46 installer checks and 29 packaging cases, plus lint, typecheck, documentation/site and bundle-integrity checks. Installer loopback fixtures passed with local-listener access. The final unit run used a private managed home and a completed build; earlier restricted-environment and concurrent-rebuild failures remain in private logs. Unsigned local packaging produced version 2.3.0 artifacts without publication; full readiness remains false. These local results do not qualify fresh native-host execution, connected Oracle, browser behavior or registry distribution. Private records are under docs/evidence/decisions/version-2.3.0/.

The offline Composer harness keeps its managed home outside the new project directory, preserving the initialization conflict guard. Composer now has an explicit 26.2 profile with six immutable @1.1.0 block packages and separate CRM/Service Desk blueprints. Real SQLcl build 26.3.0.260.1620 and vendor MMD 26.2.0+3479 compiled both complete scaffolds successfully; CRM materialization and repeat no-op checks passed. The adapters use exact lowercase report type enums and stable numeric process/saved-report mappings. Compiler/MMD mismatch checks remain mandatory. Fresh functional compiler records bind each new block to its generator, configuration and complete scaffold digest. Original 26.1 packages and records retain their true scope; old records cannot qualify the current generator or 26.2. This proof performs no database SQL, import, DML, authenticated browser or native model-host operation.

The retained publisher local-evidence exception is bound to 2.2.0 and does not apply to the current 2.3.0 source. Under the existing configuration, all nine source-bound qualification reports remain required for current-version npm and full readiness. Missing, failed and stale evidence blocks its applicable gate. Publication authorization, CI, package integrity, ownership and registry clean-install checks remain separate requirements; the GitHub release workflow remains disabled.

Host-parity teardown now awaits all MCP clients before removing their working directory, tracks clients before connection and retains close failures. Its focused macOS regression and all 62 contracts passed; the subsequent hosted CI passed Windows, macOS and both Linux matrix jobs. No CI workflow or database deployment safeguard was removed.

Actual isolated Codex registration/adoption/cache checks passed with the then-current package. A native conversation completed CLI Composer materialization and no-op; its MCP selected an older duplicate plugin because quoted dotted CLI overrides were interpreted as literal keys. A supported temporary config profile resolved that routing issue and actual MCP calls read the current 1.1.0 CRM blueprint and CRUD block. This was a configuration mismatch, not a current catalog defect. The user then stopped full external qualification. The already-started local import created only disposable app 92630 and the dedicated CMP fixture tables/API in APEXREST_262_TEST, with confirmed server verification and grant removal; runtime CRUD/browser qualification is incomplete. These narrower results do not establish all six external gates. Private records remain under ignored docs/evidence/.

 Repository automation

CI runs automatically only on pushes to main. Release and Oracle integration workflows are disabled in GitHub and gated off in their checked-in jobs. The publisher opts into the authorized npm target, subject to all required current evidence. Build, site generation and release dry-run create local output only.

Open checks are listed in [next actions](next-actions.md). Publication, tagging and database changes require their own applicable authorization.

 Documentation website

The Markdown pipeline generates tracked GitHub Pages output under docs/, with /apexrest/ routes, responsive grouped navigation, search, section links and previous flat .html guide URLs. site:check verifies generated freshness. The safety source is integrated before generation; The local browser verified current safety rules and the coverage route, navigation/search/anchors and a 390-pixel layout with contained table scrolling. The final generated site and packaging checks passed separately from these browser observations. This local work does not publish or verify revised live Pages output.

title: Next actions
text:
Next actions and verification limits

 Linear issues (2026-11-25)

- Run the Linear flow end to end in Claude Code and Codex with the official Linear MCP server connected: read an issue, ship to a local DEV target and post the results comment on request. Record the observations separately from the packaging test.

 Fast development and review comments (2026-11-22)

- Remaining fast-development tickets. Slices A to E (with APE-404) are implemented or qualified locally, and slice F partly. In slice F, Composer and scaffold share their APEXlang writing primitives (APE-357); merging their specification models is not planned. Block compiler evidence is bound to an older generator identity and needs composer:verify before a block release. The modal form, interactive grid, master–detail and faceted search recipes (APE-376/383/391/393) are compiled, imported and checked in the browser on local APEX 26.2 (see implementation status). Report-region buttons in the NEXT slot render below an interactive report; consider rightOfTitle for report buttons. Slice G was measured and no change was adopted, and slice H (visual edits in review mode) is implemented locally (see implementation status). The compound P2 edits (columns with projection, SQL replacement, recipe insertion, filters) belong to slice F.
- Broker gain is small. The broker saved about 0.25 s per apply (9.06 s against 9.31 s). The 6.5 s import in the isolated SQLcl write session dominates, so slice E (warm import server or session reuse) and slice G (export path) are where time can still be saved.
- Native ship cost. One-shot page ship stays about 15.5 s locally (planning 5.4–6.6 s, backup 2.4–2.8 s, import 5.8–7.5 s); no fast-development slice changed it. The next measurable gains are a warm compiler and export in the planning process, a backup reused from the plan export, and import time, which is mostly Oracle's own import.
- Benchmark gaps. Wire new-page scaffolding into scripts/bench/fast-dev.ts; shared-component edits need an edit service first. Repeat the A/B series on ORDS and SQLcl MCP transports, a remote DEV target and Linux/Windows hosts before any general claim.
- Component catalog for 26.2. Build a 26.2 component catalog from the official Universal Theme 26.2 Reference app (oracle/apex branch 26.2, sample-apps/universal-theme-reference, commit fbe095e4) next to the 26.1 catalog, and re-verify its recipes with the 26.2 compiler; 26.1 projects keep the current catalog.
- Slice G follow-ups. Repeat the connected preview profile on a page that runs PL/SQL with APEX context before deciding on request-scoped context reuse (APE-396). Revisit off-main-thread rendering only if a page blocks for hundreds of milliseconds (APE-395). Direct scoped export stays unused unless APEX allows component lists or a measured gain appears on a remote target.
- Largest measured native cost. On the local target a small page ship spends about 4.8 s planning (export and compile) and 6.6 s importing, out of a 14.2 s median. P4 (warm worker) and P6 (export path) work should be measured against that split.
- Visual editor limits. Template options and number/date format pickers are not in the patch service yet; the editor takes free-text formats. Edits of components declared on the global page are bound to page 0's file; that path has no test or browser check yet.
- Not yet covered by review mode. Comments on interactive grid columns and on items inside dialogs are not covered. Screenshots of the selection are not stored.

 Production qualification

- Complete the source-bound external matrix in [APE-342](https://linear.app/apexrest/issue/APE-342/complete-source-bound-external-production-qualification). The fresh Composer chat gate passed on candidate 2e26960f through the installed Codex plugin and real offline compiler. Repeat the source-bound gate on the current candidate. The connected runtime gate still requires authenticated command and form observations. The user directed this run to continue without browser.
- Obtain authorized Linux x64 and Windows x64 execution routes and a separate DEV/TEST APEX 26.2 target for their native release-specific cases. The available ATP is 26.1.6. Prior hosted repository self-tests are not current native-host evidence.
- Finish the native macOS cases marked partial or blocked, including the full golden workflows, browser handoffs and native apply permission comparisons. Candidate c6662d27 passed the bounded Codex job wait retest (HCX-008) and all six offline reference tool budgets (AGT-007). The earlier no-browser follow-up completed the persisted Codex toggle, Claude version upgrade and Claude polling cases on 2e26960f. Claude uses its normal model under the user's qualification exception. Codex application generation and repair use Sol 6.1 Medium.
- Use isolated disposable TEST projects and a dedicated managed history for fixture migrations, with an externally serialized write window. Preserve the normal managed-home migration/package history. Remote fixture DDL/DML requires the reviewed exact plan and its actual human confirmation.
- Retain the completed Oracle integration report for candidate 2e26960f and repeat the gate on the current candidate. The previous report covers same-run recovery after controlled loss of confirmation, shared-home contention, and the full verified backup restore on TEST application 97231. Independent homes and interruption during active execution require separate evidence.

 Home Finance qualification

- Extend the completed optimized cohort with additional workloads and a new matched control before a general speed claim. Its ten fresh Sol 6.1 Medium runs averaged 313.511 seconds including all seven repairs, versus historical skills at 659.704 seconds (52.477% less). All ten exact TEST ATP updates passed. Preserve the frozen measured payload, pilot, failures, all costs and post-measurement hardening separately. Work is tracked in [Optimize native APEX generation](https://linear.app/apexrest/issue/APE-341/optimize-native-apex-generation-and-qualify-ten-new-home-finance-runs).
- Extend the completed ten-per-arm Home Finance comparison using a uniform source checker and additional workloads before stating a general speed benefit. All twenty exact TEST ATP imports, original failures, thirty native repair turns and measured counters are retained. The completed experiment is tracked in [Qualify Home Finance generation](https://linear.app/apexrest/issue/APE-340/qualify-12-page-home-finance-generation-with-10-skills-and-10-apexrest).
- Keep future browser-requested checks of calendar customization, Session State Protection and business scenarios separate from the completed compiler, server parse, import and local SQLite evidence. The current experiment has fourteen imported pages per app and thirteen locally rendered pages per app, including Login.
- Extend private usage-journal qualification across supported native hosts. Fifty-three historical and nineteen optimized-series Codex phases were imported and reconciled. Local tests cover backend time, native counter import, invalid and incomplete captures, concurrent writes and byte retention. Keep any separately requested local Oracle qualification distinct from the current ATP results.

 Machine-wide settings

- Decide whether the global Decisions default should support a private ENV file (today only the environment variable) and whether settings needs an MCP tool for agents.
- Preview operations return before current-project recording; decide whether preview start should make a project current.

 Creation/update optimization qualification

- Extend the expanded scaffold beyond the completed 26.1 Home Finance cohort and heterogeneous compiler examples. Keep native 26.2 rich-component runtime behavior, editable grids, custom components and a full Box application as separate qualification before extending a creation speed claim. Preserve the completed update/import evidence and source edit protections.
- Repeat the interleaved Box creation comparison on more tasks and hosts, including cold caches, Claude, native marketplace loading, remote targets and Windows. The current three samples per arm are descriptive local Codex CLI measurements with explicitly configured MCP/skills. Preserve the initial near-parity pilot and the intermediate 37.3% improvement in private docs/evidence/box-ab-20261115/ and docs/evidence/box-optimization-20261115/.
- Qualify CLI-owned CONNECT -name sessions on other supported SQLcl releases and transports. Local SQLcl 26.3 probes and guarded imports cover a saved connection with no autoCommit property; explicit MCP transport retains the advertised connect tool and its prerequisites. Keep the rollback probe and fresh identity checks; do not change saved connection properties.
- Extend optional, manually invoked scaffold observations to queries with binds or required APEX session context when a task needs them. The current target-bound file returns bounded metadata/query observations, not a test verdict, and is never executed by scaffold or ship. Keep compiler/import and requested browser outcomes separate.
- Measure the local preparation changes against authorized Oracle new-app, full-update, selected-page and database-only workflows. The file benchmark is synthetic; identity query counts, auto database-only planning and staged validation integrity have repository coverage only. Keep compiler/import evidence separate from native-host authoring and requested browser observations.
- Qualify drain-expiry unknown outcomes with an actual SQLcl/JVM interruption and on Windows. The local POSIX regression covers a surviving descendant and cancellation of the timer after normal close.
- Track the current native generation optimization and its measured cohort in [APE-341](https://linear.app/apexrest/issue/APE-341/optimize-native-apex-generation-and-qualify-ten-new-home-finance-runs). Keep the older local update/preflight measurements separate from this experiment.

 Local preview as an alternative APEX runtime

Repeat connected preview check for Stock Control given an applicable test scope for its page code. Connected preview already rendered both pages of the dedicated ATP test application through direct SQLcl.

The goal is that a page renders and behaves locally as it would on APEX with the application's database. Measure each step with npm run preview:corpus (33 public Oracle 26.2 applications); the 2026-11-15 scorecard is in [implementation status](implementation-status.md). Remaining work, in order of how much of the corpus it affects:

- SQL failures (299). Remaining causes include Oracle syntax inside larger expressions, references and other SQLite keywords used as column names, tables the install scripts create with JSON or duality syntax, and columns that live only in Oracle dictionary views. Group the scorecard samples and translate the next largest cause.
- Seed script failures (213). AFTER and statement-level triggers, DML and loops inside BEFORE triggers (history tables, tag synchronization), JSON relational duality views and JSON collection tables.
- Authorization schemes that deny (341). Most read application tables the sample data leaves empty (access control lists); consider letting a project mark its seed users.
- APEX APIs (102). Add the next most called APIs from the scorecard samples (apex_util.host_url and the session time zone were the largest).
- PL/SQL interpreter. EXECUTE IMMEDIATE with binds, explicit cursors (OPEN/FETCH/CLOSE), FORALL, records declared with TYPE … IS RECORD, and running the skipped trigger statements through the interpreter when DML comes from PL/SQL.
- Plug-ins. Dynamic action and process plug-ins (render returns JavaScript; execution runs PL/SQL), application-scope plug-in settings, and APEX's own built-in plug-in files that some sample plug-ins load.
- Dictionary fidelity. Region static IDs keep the APEXlang identifier's lower case, so code comparing static_id with a mixed-case value finds nothing; template option and theme metadata views used by the Universal Theme reference application.

 Oracle skill and source maintenance

- The 2026-11-05 check found no newer APEXlang skill content: all 13 APEX entrypoints, 389 bundled 26.2 definitions and 659 bundled 26.1 source files match the reviewed sources. Keep the existing upstream pins; review future skill/router changes separately from inventory changes using the maintainer skill map.
- For a separately requested application release upgrade, follow oracle:26.2:guide/upgrade-audit on the identified DEV/QA/TEST target. The current skill/guide refresh performs no application import, toolchain upgrade or browser qualification. Verify fresh native Codex/Claude loading separately from local packaging checks.

 Release verification after review fixes

- Qualify remote SQL confirmation, saved-plan environment matching, service binding and interrupted recovery on an authorized disposable Oracle target. Fixture coverage verifies confirmation, refusal and preservation of old local records. Where an older managed home has unregistered journals, run a full read-only plan through each original verified service to register the preserved history.
- Qualify full Oracle APEXlang restore with a differing backup alias and the legacy standalone SQL restore path on disposable targets. Local coverage exercises the alias, the exact-plan safety gate and checksummed SQL input. Split SQL exports use an APEXlang backup or a separately reviewed manual recovery procedure.
- Verify live Composer row predicates and dictionary drift through the deploy-before-import check on a controlled application. Keep source-only fixtures and compiler results separate from connected runtime behavior.
- Qualify native cross-platform installer upgrades and Oracle/JVM resource behavior. Local tests verify the candidate tool catalog before activation, SQLcl startup reservations and bounded transport faults. The review machine's actual Codex update now passes scoped discovery despite a broken unrelated marketplace, with independent foreign configuration checks. Fresh-profile setup and same-version Claude cache refresh were also verified.
- Verify preview navigation and transaction behavior in the supported browser and authorized connected modes. Loopback tests cover the foreign-navigation refusal, direct navigation and a working same-origin submit.
- Use the [production qualification matrix](production-qualification) for the current candidate. Local repository, offline Oracle compiler and Composer checks pass. Full readiness also depends on the external scenarios recorded there. The lockfile audit reported zero known advisories.

 Findings from the 2026-11-04 local 26.2 run

- Local migration history is keyed only by database identity and parsing schema. A rebuilt database with the same FREE/freepdb1/schema identity inherited the destroyed database's history, so the first plan skipped 0001__customers.sql. Detect a recreated database (for example DBID or creation time) or report the mismatch before planning.
- The 2026-11-06 sync-init normalization accepts the two known server rewrites of a generated blank app (app.id, the empty deinstall script). Repeat apex sync init on a fresh template project against the real target; it was not rerun after the fix. Defaults and reordering beyond those two rewrites still raise SYNC_SOURCE_CONFLICT.
- The 2026-11-16 post-ship sync-init adoption relies on a post-import.json written by a full import. Repeat invalidate, full ship and apex sync --action init against the real target to confirm that APEX 26.2 import moves last_updated_on and that init adopts the rewrites. Runs shipped before the fix have no record and still conflict.
- ship --plan <planId> fails with INTERNAL_ERROR (ENOENT). Accept a plan ID, or return an input error that names the plan path.
- A database-only apply journals a backing_up phase although it backs nothing up; the time is spent on the fresh target export. Name the phase for what it does.

 Connected and host qualification

- Connected preview commit mode is limited to confirmed-local databases. Decide whether remote DEV/QA/TEST targets should get it with exact human confirmation; until then they are refused. COMMIT in stored code and autonomous transactions under commit mode were not exercised against Oracle.
- Repeat the 2026-11-06 Bitcoin Price Monitor comparison (reset-standard.sh, reset-plugin.sh and run.sh in the private evidence folder) at least three times per scenario before stating a speed ratio: each recorded figure is a single run. Keep both scenarios on the same model, effort, task text and starting sources.
- Investigate why opening the imported Alerts page by URL lost the APEX session in the 2026-11-06 browser-design comparison (plugin run), so the alert form was checked only in the preview. The 2026-11-07 plugin re-run did not write initialization JavaScript, so the visible note and notAppliedLocally remain unexercised in an agent run. Its second import came from the chart tooltip: consider making the preview's line-chart tooltip follow Oracle JET's default (series, group label and value format) so tooltip gaps are visible before import.
- Repeat the browser-design comparison (docs/evidence/btc-ui-20261106/) at least three times per scenario with a fixed, wider Chrome window; the recorded standard 1,330.8 s versus plugin 815.5 s is a single run per scenario in a tiled 620 px window.
- Measure the 2026-11-15 authoring changes in agent runs: enum values in selection, the executionMappingIdentifier note, MISSING_REQUIRED_PROPERTY fixes and the preview check lint. They are unit-tested only; earlier runs produced 13-14 first-validation errors on new pages. Selection's 1,500-byte value allowance does not fit every list (a number field got virtualKeyboard but not numberAlignment), when.event values are the 12 most used in samples, and whether a single process without executionMappingIdentifier compiles is unverified. Confirm SLOT-001 and the accessibility rules against real APEX and Advisor output, and decide whether lint findings should also appear in the validate result.
- Qualify the 2026-11-15 deployment speed-ups beyond the local Docker run (docs/evidence/ship-speed-20261115/):
  - interrupt an import while it runs on the prepared import server (kill the server, cancel, time out) on an authorized DEV/TEST target and confirm the unknown-outcome and recovery path;
  - repeat on a remote database, on Windows, with SQLcl 26.1 and with different read and deploy connections;
  - confirm on each supported SQLcl build that a failing statement stops a server batch under whenever sqlerror exit failure rollback (observed on 26.3.0.260.1620 only);
  - run a selected-file import on the prepared import server (unit-tested and checked offline only): confirm that -files paths resolve against the server's working directory and time it against the import process;
  - run the kept-export apply and an Oracle-rejected import (IMPORT_REJECTED) on the same target and repeat the speed measurement; the expected saving of one export (about 4-5 s) is an estimate;
  - measure the compiler preload in an MCP session, including a validation that arrives while it runs;
  - decide whether apex sync and recovery should use the read scope (they keep one process per call today).
- Deployment time still spent, estimated from the 2026-11-15 measurement of about 23 s for a nine-page application less one export: two exports (plan, before import; about 4 s each on a warm server), two server starts with their connections (about 2.5 s each, one in the MCP server and one in the apply worker) and the compiler load. title: Publishing policy
text:
Publishing policy

This page states what must be true before APEXREST is published to npm or released as a signed build, and how the documentation website is built and served. It is for maintainers who prepare a release or edit the documentation site.

[apexrest-dev/apexrest](https://github.com/apexrest-dev/apexrest) is the canonical source repository. Git commits, registry packages, signed release artifacts and a deployed website are separate distribution outcomes.

 What this policy does not do

- These settings run no publication command.
- The release and trusted Oracle/native integration workflows remain disabled in GitHub, and their jobs use if: ${{ false }}.
- CI runs automatically only on pushes to main.
- GitHub release/tag and integration execution require separate authorization.
- Any requested publication requires current applicable evidence and authorization.
- Building or previewing the documentation website publishes nothing.
- Database deployment safeguards, production refusal and unknown-outcome recovery are unchanged.

 npm eligibility and full qualification

Each gate has its own command:

| Command                                    | Gate                                                                                                    |
| ------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| npm run check-release-readiness -- --npm | npm eligibility.                                                                                        |
| npm run check-release-readiness          | The default. Continues to require all nine reports for full qualification and signed release packaging. |

Both commands report npmReady, stableReady, qualification status and each report's required scope. npm eligibility does not establish full Oracle/native qualification.

 The approved 2.8.0 npm exception

The maintainer approved npm publication of 2.8.0 using current local evidence.

- Both publisher opt-ins, enabled and npmEnabled, are required.
- The npmReadiness exception applies only to version 2.8.0.
- The three current local reports (composer-local.json, local-checks.json, oracle-local.json) block npm when missing, failed or stale.
- The six external Composer runtime/new-chat, native macOS/Linux/Windows and connected Oracle reports are advisory for this npm version. Their actual missing, blocked and stale states remain visible; they still block full qualification.
- A different package version does not inherit this exception.

 Checks to keep for any publication

Keep:

- Local checks.
- Successful CI on the final source. The approved 2.8.0 npm exception uses the local CI run, with hosted CI still pending.
- Package inventory and integrity.
- Verified registry ownership.
- fresh registry installation with CLI/MCP/reference checks.

 Full qualification and signed releases

Full qualification and signed releases require:

- current evidence bound to the exact immutable source;
- archive integrity;
- protected target/approval settings;
- an externally managed signing key where required.

Missing, blocked or stale required evidence fails its applicable gate.

 Documentation on GitHub Pages

The documentation website is [apexrest-dev.github.io/apexrest](https://apexrest-dev.github.io/apexrest/).

- The repository's Pages configuration serves the /docs directory on main, with no custom domain.
- Its entry point is docs/index.html.
- All page, asset and search routes use the /apexrest/ base path.
- Search uses a local JSON index; the website needs no server-side runtime, external fonts or third-party search service.
- No additional Pages workflow is required for this configured branch source.

 Build and preview the website

The existing Markdown renderer builds the website locally.

1. Edit the Markdown sources and site/ theme/configuration.
2. Rebuild, check and preview:

   sh
   npm ci --ignore-scripts
   npm run site:build
   npm run site:check
   npm run docs:check
   npm run site:preview
   

3. Open the preview at http://127.0.0.1:4173/apexrest/. It serves the same tracked HTML and assets that Pages will serve. The optional APEXREST_SITE_PORT changes the preview port.
4. Commit the generated HTML, CSS, JavaScript, search index, .nojekyll and docs/site-manifest.json together with their sources.

 What the build produces

- The manifest lists files owned by the generator; the build preserves authored Markdown, catalog/reference data, diagrams and examples.
- site:check detects stale tracked output.
- The .nojekyll file lets Pages serve the prepared static files directly, following [GitHub's static-site instructions](https://docs.github.com/en/pages/getting-started-with-github-pages/creating-a-github-pages-site).
- Existing flat .html guide URLs remain readable with their original anchors.

 Other site commands

| Command or path                                                   | Purpose                                                                                                               |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| site-dist/                                                      | Remains an ignored staging directory for release packaging.                                                           |
| APEXREST_SITE_BASE_PATH=/ node scripts/build-site.mjs --preview | For an alternate local preview only; this does not update the branch-hosted docs/ output.                           |
| scripts/publish-site.sh                                         | Supports an explicitly authorized mounted copy, with --dry-run before --apply; it is not needed for GitHub Pages. |

 When the live site changes

- Building or previewing changes publishes nothing.
- An authorized push to main updates the branch-hosted Pages site independently of the disabled product-release publisher.
- Confirm the live Pages build and browser result separately after that push.

 Related

See [release notes](release-notes.md), [testing](testing.md) and [next actions](next-actions.md).

title: Current release notes
text:
Current release notes

 Source bundle 2.9.0

The repository bundle supports Codex and Claude Code with six skills and twelve MCP tools. This release makes the edit–preview–deploy loop faster and reviewable: you point at components in the local preview and leave comments or edit properties, and agents apply small changes through digest-bound semantic edits instead of rewriting page files.

 Changes

- Review mode in the local preview. Alt+Shift+C selects a region, item, button, report column or the page, and leaves a comment for any agent, stored in .apexrest/review/comments.json. Edit in the same form changes a title, label, heading, format or sequence through the digest-bound patch service. preview comments returns each comment with its patch target and file digest. See [local preview](local-preview.mdreview-comments).
- Semantic page edits. project context returns a page's components and its file digest. project patch changes titles, labels, headings, formats, sequences, and report SQL together with its columns. project insert adds regions, items and refreshes to an existing page. Each edit is digest-bound, atomic and keeps unrelated bytes.
- CRUD and search recipes. project scaffold generates a report with a modal create/edit form, an editable interactive grid, a master–detail page and a faceted search. Editable regions require an authorization scheme, one primary key and lost-update detection. Compiled, imported and checked in the browser on local APEX 26.2.
- Incremental preview. Per-file parse cache, reloads only for affected pages, in-place refresh of allowlisted regions, stylesheet replacement, and the last good page kept with a stale banner after an invalid edit.
- Source revisions. Status reports latest local, preview, validated, importing and deployed revisions separately, and a late result never marks a newer revision.
- Development broker and safer recovery. dev start keeps one worker per project with exclusive job claims, and newer applies supersede queued ones. deploy reconcile releases a run held for database review after an exact, confirmed review. Migration history is bound to the schema instance, and one reset session runs an apply's database scripts.
- Align package, workspace and native plugin versions to 2.9.0.

 Measured verification

All measurements are on local APEX 26.2 with Oracle 23.26.4. Details are in [implementation status](implementation-status.md).

- Semantic edits. From the service call to the edit in preview HTML takes 25–26 ms median.
- Preview. A renamed file with an older modification time is now detected (5/5, 8.8 ms).
- Native page ship. It is unchanged: 15.4 s baseline against 15.5 s, in alternating runs on the same project. No speed claim is made for deployment.

These are local results with small samples. They do not establish remote, Windows or Linux behavior.

 Upgrade a working copy

Working copies bind their runtime/toolchain version. Reconcile local edits and unresolved outcomes, then explicitly refresh a clean checkpoint with apexrest apex sync --env dev --action refresh --json and create new plans. Never edit stored runtime versions or clear unknown ownership to bypass safeguards.

 Distribution and verification

The approved npm exception applied only to 2.8.0; publishing 2.9.0 needs its own approval and current reports. Hosted CI runs on pushes to main. Repository release and Oracle integration workflows remain disabled.

See [acceptance](acceptance.json), [open checks](next-actions.md) and [publishing](publishing.md). Repository fixtures remain separate from connected Oracle and native-host evidence.

- Semantic page edits. project context returns a page's components and its file digest. project patch changes titles, labels, headings, formats, sequences, and report SQL together with its columns. project insert adds regions, items and refreshes to an existing page. Each edit is digest-bound, atomic and keeps unrelated bytes.
- CRUD and search recipes. project scaffold generates a report with a modal create/edit form, an editable interactive grid, a master–detail page and a faceted search. Editable regions require an authorization scheme, one primary key and lost-update detection. Compiled, imported and checked in the browser on local APEX 26.2.
- Incremental preview. Per-file parse cache, reloads only for affected pages, in-place refresh of allowlisted regions, stylesheet replacement, and the last good page kept with a stale banner after an invalid edit.
- Source revisions. Status reports latest local, preview, validated, importing and deployed revisions separately, and a late result never marks a newer revision.
- Development broker and safer recovery. dev start keeps one worker per project with exclusive job claims, and newer applies supersede queued ones. deploy reconcile releases a run held for database review after an exact, confirmed review. Migration history is bound to the schema instance, and one reset session runs an apply's database scripts.
- Align package, workspace, Codex and Claude Code source versions to 2.9.0. Registry distribution and full native/Oracle qualification remain separate outcomes.
